name: Aviary
statement: a terminal and on-chain products built on [Pipeline](https://github.com/MetalLegBob/pipeline), a permissionless router for experimental Solana markets.
destination:
A build-ready spec for the five products on devnet (Aviary, the containment hook, the tax AMM, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM) in `docs/spec/` (a shared `README.md` plus one file per product), with decisions in `docs/adr/`, and for each product a set of `build` tickets whose run order `## Next` gives the relay.
It is released in stages: each product's build tickets are cut as soon as its own decisions close, so building starts before the whole map is done.

Pipescope screens
tickets.decision: the feed is one table of markets with strategies on a second tab; the market page puts the chart and the trade box first, with a review step that simulates before the wallet opens; the amount typed is everything that leaves the wallet, fees included; three styles of text for what Aviary measured, what an AI wrote and what an author wrote; Canary outcomes as a word and an ink shape, never a colour or a count; hollow and solid candles, light and dark themes; prices quoted in SOL, else USDC, from one API field the bot shares; token images only from our own copy; every value in one config module or one theme stylesheet; the owner went ahead with the session's recommended answers, so all 21 are lightly reviewed defaults ([spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-screens.md), [prototype](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/tree/prototype/pipescope-screens/prototype/pipescope-screens))
tickets.resolution:
Aviary's screens are specified in [`docs/spec/pipescope-screens.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-screens.md), landed by [#105](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/105).
The prototype behind it stays on the throwaway branch [`prototype/pipescope-screens`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/tree/prototype/pipescope-screens/prototype/pipescope-screens), never merged; its [README](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/prototype/pipescope-screens/prototype/pipescope-screens/README.md) says how to run it and carries the verdict.

**How it was settled.**
The owner was given the prototype on 2026-11-10 with six questions and a recommended answer for each, and on 2026-11-12 told the session to go ahead with the recommendations, changing none and without reacting to the screens one by one.
So every answer is a lightly reviewed default, and the register's Follow-ups say so.

**The answer, in short.**

- **Feed**: one table of markets, newest first, with strategies on a second tab; filters off by default and kept in the page's address.
- **Market page**: the chart with the trades beneath it and the trade box beside them, then the explanation and the strategy's forms beside the facts panel.
- **Trade box**: the amount typed is everything that leaves the wallet, fees included; the fee breakdown is always open; "Review swap" builds and simulates before "Sign in wallet" turns on; the exit-test notice sits above the button with its tick box.
- **Strategy page**: Canary by check, with how many of the version's markets got each outcome, opening to the markets that warn or fail.
- **The look**: three styles of text for three speakers (plain for what Aviary read or measured, a serif for an AI's words, purple italic for an author's); Canary outcomes as a word and an ink shape, never a colour or a count; canary yellow only on Canary's mark and the trade-box notice; hollow and solid candles; light and dark themes.
- **Token images**: shown small, served only from our own copy, so a reader's browser never calls an author's server.
- **Phones**: nothing scrolls sideways down to 360 px; tables become labelled blocks.

## Decisions this settled

All are in the [decision register](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md), each with its question, answer, alternatives and the one place its value lives.

- `PIPESCOPE-65`: who is speaking, three styles of text
- `PIPESCOPE-66`: Canary outcomes without colour
- `PIPESCOPE-67`: where colour is used
- `PIPESCOPE-68`: light and dark themes
- `PIPESCOPE-69`: candles, hollow and solid
- `PIPESCOPE-70`: the feed's layout
- `PIPESCOPE-71`: what a row says about Canary
- `PIPESCOPE-72`: the feed's filter steps
- `PIPESCOPE-73`: the market page's layout
- `PIPESCOPE-74`: price direction, and the API's `quote_mint`
- `PIPESCOPE-75`: candle lengths on the chart
- `PIPESCOPE-76`: the amount typed in the trade box
- `PIPESCOPE-77`: slippage choices
- `PIPESCOPE-78`: review before signing
- `PIPESCOPE-79`: markets that cannot trade
- `PIPESCOPE-80`: Canary on the strategy page
- `PIPESCOPE-81`: how search matches
- `PIPESCOPE-82`: token images
- `PIPESCOPE-83`: phones
- `PIPESCOPE-84`: Telegram on the pages
- `PIPESCOPE-85`: where the screens' values live

Every one is a default, not a final word.
To change any of them, name its ID in an issue or in a comment here, and it is changed in the register, in the spec and in whatever is built from it.

## For the tickets that follow

- [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22): the spec's "For other tickets" lists what the screens add: a config module and a theme stylesheet in `terminal-web`, `quote_mint` and `base_mint` on what the API returns, Canary's sentences served with each result, and a place for `terminal-api` to keep token images, which the architecture does not name yet.
- [Telegram bot for Pipescope](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/32) asked whether the trade box has its own rule for which mint a market is quoted in.
  It does: SOL if the pair has it, else USDC, else the later mint, returned by the API as `quote_mint`; the bot's Buy button already pays with that mint.
- Not seen running, and listed in the spec under "What the prototype did not show": live updates, a real wallet, the steps after signing, a form from valid metadata, a market with three or four mints, token images, and everything the Telegram spec asks of the pages.

tickets.decision: [`docs/decisions.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md) holds every decision settled so far (284 on 2026-11-10), one block each: a stable ID by product, the answer, the alternatives weighed, the single place its value lives and how it would change; a script checks the format and prints it for the progress site, every PR lists the IDs it rests on, and its Follow-ups name where a spec disagrees with a later answer or spreads one value over several places
tickets.resolution:
The decision register is on `main`: [`docs/decisions.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md), landed by [Add the decision register, open to MetalLegBob's review](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/91).

### What it holds

- **284 decisions**, one block each: SUITE 37, BAR 29, PIPESCOPE 64, CANARY 27, EXPLAINER 20, TAX 28, HOOK 22, POOL4 21, LENDING 36.
- Every block has a stable ID, the question, the current answer, the alternatives weighed, the single place where its value lives, how it would change and a status.
  By how they change: 169 spec only, 45 build-time constants, 9 market-creation parameters, 13 runtime settings and 48 fixed on-chain once deployed.
- Two are `confirmed` from what the map already records (`SUITE-16`, building against the current SDK; `PIPESCOPE-01`, the first version's scope); every other one is a `default`.
- It was harvested from the resolution comments of every closed ticket, from `docs/spec/` and `docs/adr/`, and checked against the list of every question a session put to the owner.
  It includes what closed while it was being written: the buy wall AMM's design and build cut, the names, the lending AMM's build cut and amended withdraw mode, the tax AMM and containment hook build cut, the Telegram bot and the keeper runner's spec.
- It never quotes MetalLegBob and draws on no private file; a change he asks for is recorded only as `changed` with its date.

### The rest of the Done when

- `CLAUDE.md` carries the standing rule under "Rules for this project", and `.github/pull_request_template.md` has the section that lists the decision IDs a PR rests on and invites MetalLegBob to change any of them.
- `scripts/decisions.mjs` parses and checks the format (`--check`) and prints it as JSON (`--json`); a workflow runs it and its tests on every change under `docs/`, so a spec heading cannot move away from under a decision unnoticed.
- **The progress site**: the format is agreed with [Progress site on Vercel](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/30), whose session answered that the shape works as it is; its refresh picks the file up from `main` and shows it at `/decisions/`, one section per product, each decision with its ID as an anchor.
  Its privacy filter drops any list item that names MetalLegBob or the unregistered address, so field values avoid both; the three decisions that are about him by nature (`SUITE-01`, `SUITE-03`, `SUITE-14`) are named there for that session to approve.
- `GLOSSARY.md` gains Default and Decision register, and Owner and MetalLegBob are reworded, since the suite is built for him.

### Choices made here, open like any other

- The ID prefixes stay as the owner gave them (`PIPESCOPE-`, `POOL4-`, `LENDING-` and the rest) after the rename to the public names: they are identifiers, like the spec file names, and the buy wall AMM's build tickets already cite `POOL4-01` to `POOL4-21`.
  The section headings carry the public names.
- A decision that lives only on a ticket (the progress site's three, and four that only shape how a build ticket is built) names that ticket as its place until a spec states it.
- A decision a session set without asking the owner is a `default` too, and the Follow-ups name those blocks.

### Follow-ups for other sessions

The register ends with 21 [Follow-ups](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#follow-ups); no other session's spec was edited.
The ones that matter most:

- `CANARY-27`: the owner's answer on a refused transfer lives in `containment-hook.md`, and the Canary spec's own row still says fail.
- `BAR-27`, `POOL4-19`, `LENDING-34`: the tax AMM and the containment hook deploy and then harden; the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM harden first; `README.md` states neither departure.
- `LENDING-19`: the owner approved burning LP shares for protocol-owned liquidity; the spec uses `lock_lp` instead.
- The mint extension allowlist is written out in three specs, and the tax AMM and the hook each keep a copy in code.
- Pipeline's own 0.25% is fixed text in several specs, although it is the router's setting.
- The terminal's policy values other than its fee have no named home.
- `LENDING-16`: `lending-pool.md` still has Aviary's indexer start `rebalance`; the keeper runner's spec replaced that with the runner's own socket.

Posted to the tickets that own them: [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22), [Telegram bot for Pipescope](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/32), [Keeper runner](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/45) and [Cut the lending pool's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/25).

### For every session from here on

Add a block for each decision you settle, at the end of its product's section; run `node scripts/decisions.mjs --check`; list the IDs your PR rests on.
The top of the file says how.

tickets.title: Keeper runner
tickets.decision: a portable Node program run on the owner's Mac under launchd, never on the owner's Cloudflare account, with a Docker image for anyone else; its own socket, sweeps and daily payouts on Alchemy's free devnet RPC; a dedicated keeper wallet kept at 2 SOL by airdrop under named caps (0.003 SOL a transaction, 0.01 SOL a market a day, 0.1 SOL a day); simulate first, retry then park, shown in Aviary; it keeps `place_wall`'s tips and covers every market of our strategies ([spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/keeper-runner.md))
tickets.resolution:
Settled with the owner on 2026-11-10 and written into [`docs/spec/keeper-runner.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/keeper-runner.md) ([PR 98](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/98)), with three new glossary terms: keeper runner, keeper wallet, keeper tip.

- **Where:** a portable Node program, `apps/keeper`, run on the owner's Mac as a launchd agent; nothing of it runs on the owner's Cloudflare account, because the work is for MetalLegBob and must cost the owner nothing. Aviary itself stays where [Pipescope architecture](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/13) put it. A Docker image and README let anyone else run it with their own key. While the Mac sleeps, jobs wait and nothing breaks.
- **Triggers:** its own `logsSubscribe` socket on our strategy programs, a 10-minute sweep, hourly `settle`, a daily pass for payouts, and a full pass on start. It reads only the chain and never polls Aviary's database, which must sleep to stay inside Neon's free compute hours.
- **RPC:** Alchemy's free devnet endpoint (`ALCHEMY_API_KEY`), keeping both Helius budgets free; the first build ticket checks that its WebSocket serves `logsSubscribe`.
- **Wallet:** a new key, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/keeper.json`, not the deploy wallet; the key exists only in that file. Kept at 2 SOL with `devnet-airdrop`, never self-funded.
- **Caps** (one module, `apps/keeper/src/settings.ts`, each overridable by a `KEEPER_` variable): 0.003 SOL a transaction, 0.01 SOL a market a day, 0.1 SOL a day, a warning below 0.5 SOL, no sends below 0.1 SOL, priority fee 0. Today's spend is rebuilt from the wallet's own transactions, so restarting never resets a cap.
- **Failures:** simulate first, so "nothing to do" costs nothing; retry at 30 s, 2 min and 10 min, then park the job until its market changes. When the wallet is dry or a cap is reached the runner stops sending and says why. Runs are recorded in Aviary's `keeper_runs` table, each market's panel shows its due jobs as buttons anyone can press, and a keeper page shows the wallet, spend and parked jobs.
- **Tips and others:** the runner keeps `place_wall`'s keeper tips and unwraps them into the float above 0.05 SOL (`place_wall` always pays for itself). It covers every market of our strategies, including other people's, within the caps. We count on nobody else running the jobs, and a racing keeper is harmless.
- **Scope:** the tax AMM's `distribute` runs daily per owed slot. The containment hook's `unlock` keeps no keeper job, as [Containment hook policy](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/18) decided.

Build tickets cut, in run order: [Keeper runner: the runner, its wallet and the tax AMM's `distribute`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/94), [Keeper runner: the buy wall AMM's four jobs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/95), [Keeper runner: the lending AMM's `rebalance`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/96). Aviary's side is posted on [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22).

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

| Question | Answer | Alternatives | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Where does the keeper runner run? | A portable Node program on the owner's Mac (launchd), with a Docker image for anyone else | Inside Aviary's API Worker; its own Cloudflare Worker; a GitHub Actions cron | `keeper-runner.md`, "What it is", "Running it" |
| Which RPC does it use? | Alchemy's free devnet endpoint | Aviary's own Helius key | `settings.ts`, `RPC_URL` and `WS_URL` |
| Which wallet pays? | A dedicated keeper wallet, kept at 2 SOL by airdrop | The deploy wallet | `keeper-runner.md`, "The keeper wallet"; `settings.ts`, `KEEPER_KEYPAIR` and `FLOAT_TARGET` |
| What may it spend? | 0.003 SOL a transaction, 0.01 SOL a market a day, 0.1 SOL a day; warning at 0.5 SOL, stop at 0.1 SOL; no priority fee | Looser caps with no per-market cap | `settings.ts` |
| What happens on failure? | Simulate first; retry at 30 s, 2 min and 10 min, then park until the market changes; shown in Aviary | Logs only; Telegram alerts | `keeper-runner.md`, "Failures"; `settings.ts`, `RETRY_DELAYS` |
| Who keeps keeper tips? | The runner, unwrapped into its float above 0.05 SOL | Swept to the suite treasury | `settings.ts`, `TIP_UNWRAP_AT` |
| Which markets does it cover? | Every market of our strategies, within the caps | Only markets our own wallets created | `keeper-runner.md`, "Which markets" |
| When do payouts and `settle` run? | Payouts in one daily pass at 00:00 UTC; `settle` at most hourly per market | Payouts on every change | `settings.ts`, `DAILY_PASS_UTC` and `SETTLE_INTERVAL` |

tickets.resolution:
Resolved with the owner on 2026-11-10, in four short rounds.
Spec: [`docs/spec/pipescope-telegram.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-telegram.md); decision record: [ADR 0007](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-telegram-trades-are-signed-in-aviarys-trade-box.md); landed in [#97](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/97).

## Answers to the ticket's questions

- **Which commands**: lookups (a market or strategy card with its facts and Canary results, by address or name), trade links, and alerts; in private chats and groups, plus one unfiltered public channel.
- **How a trade is signed**: the bot holds no key and signs nothing. Buy and Sell buttons are plain links to Aviary's market page with the swap filled in (a trade link), and the trader signs there in their own wallet. On a phone, where Telegram's browser has no wallet, the page offers to reopen itself inside Phantom, Solflare or Backpack.
- **Fee and before-signing rules**: unchanged, because it is the same trade box: 0.5% only when paying with a fee mint, the simulation before every signature, the exit-test tick box. The card also states the fees and repeats the "could not sell back" notice above the Buy button.

Also settled: the bot runs inside `terminal-api` (a webhook route and a Cloudflare Queue), buys nothing and makes no paid call; it stores a chat's id, settings and watch list and nothing about a person or a wallet; strategy and token metadata stay untrusted text that can never become a link in a message.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

Each is the owner's default and can change; "where" is the section of the spec that holds it.

| # | Question | Answer | Alternatives weighed | Where it lives | How it would change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | How is a trade that starts in Telegram signed? | In Aviary's own trade box, reached by a trade link | A Mini App inside Telegram; a link that opens the wallet with the transaction ready | Trading from Telegram; ADR 0007 | Spec and a new build (a Mini App can be added beside the links) |
| 2 | What is in the first version? | Lookups, trade links and alerts | Lookups and trade links only; alerts only | First version | Spec |
| 3 | Which events alert? | New strategies and new markets; for what a chat watches, upgrades and changed Canary outcomes | New listings only; watched changes only | Alerts, What is sent | Spec |
| 4 | Where does the bot work? | Private chats and groups, with Telegram's privacy mode on | Private chats only; inline mode too | Private chats and groups | Spec and BotFather settings |
| 5 | Where is the amount chosen? | In the trade box; `/buy` and `/sell` can fill it in | Preset amount buttons in chat; commands only | Buy, Sell and Trade | Spec |
| 6 | Do the fee and before-signing rules change? | No; the card repeats the fees and the exit-test notice | A card that repeats neither; a separate rate for bot trades | Trading from Telegram | The rate is the API's fee configuration; the card is spec |
| 7 | When is a new-market alert sent? | After the market's first Canary run, at most 5 minutes later | At once and edited later; at once with the results as a reply | Alerts; One place for every value | A value in the bot's config module |
| 8 | When is an upgrade alert sent? | At once, then the results as a second message | Only after Canary finishes; at once only | Alerts, What is sent | Spec |
| 9 | Does the bot know a trader's wallet? | No: no address asked for or stored | Lookups by pasted address; a saved address for alerts on holdings | First version; What the bot stores | Spec |
| 10 | Does the bot show the explanation? | Its summary under the pages' label, with a link to the rest; it never has one made | A link only; the whole explanation in chat | The explanation | Spec |
| 11 | Is there a public channel? | Yes: every new strategy, new market and upgrade, unfiltered | No channel; decide at mainnet | The channel | A var of `terminal-api` |
| 13 | When is it built? | Alongside Aviary's web pages | After the terminal ships; before mainnet only | When it is built | Ticket order |

Limits chosen as defaults without a question, each in the bot's config module: a watch list of 100 a chat, 20 lookups a minute a chat, lists of 10, sending at most 25 messages a second, a group's admin list kept 5 minutes, alerts off for a new chat.

## For the build

- Owner task before the bot's first build ticket: create the working bot in BotFather (privacy mode on, inline mode off, groups allowed) and a private working channel with the bot as an admin.
- Four things the documentation did not settle are listed in the spec as checks for the build to run first ("Checked facts and open checks").

tickets.title: Cut the lending pool's build tickets
tickets.decision: the spec was complete but for withdraw mode, whose thresholds are now measured against the larger of the market's lent value and its target lent value, so a market that has redeemed everything does not lend straight back into the crunch; twelve `build` tickets in one chain: our Kamino lending market on devnet first, then the program slice by slice, each verified in LiteSVM and by a local demo run on devnet's own router and klend bytes, hardening before the first deploy, and a devnet ticket that deploys, registers and runs the demo market against the real Kamino Lend; `rebalance` is called by the demo script and Aviary's form until the keeper runner exists ([resolution](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/25#issuecomment-6760503806), [spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/lending-pool.md#build-tickets))
tickets.resolution:
**Answer.** `docs/spec/lending-pool.md` and the bar in `docs/spec/README.md` were complete enough to build from, with one gap, settled with the owner today, so no new decision ticket was needed.
The lending AMM (the lending pool's name since [Product and suite names](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/17)) is cut into twelve build tickets labelled `build`, one session each, with native blocking, listed in run order in the spec's [Build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/lending-pool.md#build-tickets) and in the map's `## Next`.

**The gap.** Withdraw mode was measured against the market's current lent value, which is 0 once the market has redeemed everything, so the next `rebalance` would leave withdraw mode at once, lend 80% back into the same crunch and re-enter.
The owner chose to measure both thresholds against the larger of the lent value and the target lent value.
The spec's [Withdraw mode](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/lending-pool.md#withdraw-mode), constants, invariants and test list say so now (merged in #89, with a follow-up in #92).

**The tickets, in run order**

1. [Lending AMM: our Kamino lending market on devnet](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/77): unblocked, on devnet; it proves Kamino Lend on devnet does what the spec assumes (layout parity, the cToken path, a test borrower, emergency mode) before any program depends on it.
2. [Lending AMM: markets that trade from their own vaults](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/78): waits for the first ticket and for [Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/58) and [Tax AMM: create a tax market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/59).
3. [Lending AMM: klend fixtures, and valuing the lent side from Kamino's reserve](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/79)
4. [Lending AMM: lend the surplus with `rebalance`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/80)
5. [Lending AMM: redeem a swap's shortfall from Kamino inside the swap](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/81)
6. [Lending AMM: remove liquidity in cash or in kind, and lock LP shares](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/82)
7. [Lending AMM: withdraw mode and Kamino's other states](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/83)
8. [Lending AMM: seeding by a launchpad](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/84)
9. [Lending AMM: the fuzzer against a moving Kamino, and the proofs completed](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/85)
10. [Lending AMM: hardening](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/86)
11. [Lending AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/87): the end of the program's chain.
12. [Lending AMM: Aviary panel, forms and explainer facts](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/88): after the deploy, and held by [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22) until Aviary's own tickets exist to block it.

Each one is blocked by the one before it, because they all change the same program.

**How they are verified**

- Tickets 2 to 10: LiteSVM through the real router copied from devnet and klend's deployed bytes, with the `mainnet` build on cloned mainnet reserves and the `devnet` build on accounts dumped from our devnet lending market; and a local demo run of the demo script on a local validator running devnet's router and klend, as `docs/agents/build-tickets.md` asks.
- Tickets 1 and 11: on devnet itself, against the real Kamino Lend there. Ticket 11 runs every check under "On devnet" in the spec's Done means: the market created, funded and rebalanced into Kamino, a sell that redeems in the swap, a test borrower bringing withdraw mode on and off, and emergency mode on and off.
- Every ticket cites the bar's sections in its acceptance criteria, and the program tickets share one block of standing criteria (one config module, both cluster builds, proofs, the fuzzer, compute ceilings, `pipeline-check` clean, decision IDs in the PR).

**What the tickets do not build**

- The keeper runner: until [Keeper runner](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/45) is specified and built, `rebalance` is called by the demo script and by anyone from Aviary's form.
- Anything on mainnet.

**Also changed in the spec**

- Our devnet Kamino reserve gets a second depositor (at least 5 SOL from the devnet wallet), because a reserve holding only our markets' deposits would sit below withdraw mode's entry threshold.
- The `init` form's one possible shape under Pipeline's metadata schema at `5ad130d`: the other mint, then the lent mint, with `lent_index` 1.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

Each is the owner's default, and he may change any of them.

1. **What are withdraw mode's thresholds measured against?**
   Answer (owner, 2026-11-10): the larger of the market's lent value and its target lent value; enter below 5 times, leave above 10 times.
   Alternatives: the target lent value alone; the lent value alone, as first written, which flapped.
   Where: `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`, "Withdraw mode" and "Constants"; in code, build-time constants and one function in the program's config module.
2. **When does the lending AMM's hardening ticket run?**
   Answer: before the first devnet deploy, so the program registered with Pipeline is the hardened one, as for the buy wall AMM.
   Alternative: last, after the deploy, as the bar words it and as the tax AMM does.
   Where: `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`, "Build tickets"; it changes ticket order only.
3. **How are the lending AMM's feature tickets verified?**
   Answer: in LiteSVM and by a local demo run, both on devnet's own router and klend bytes; on devnet itself in the first and the eleventh ticket.
   Alternative: a devnet deploy and upgrade in every ticket.
   Where: `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`, "Build tickets"; it changes acceptance criteria only.
4. **What is the lending AMM's devnet demo market?**
   Answer: WSOL lent, a fresh test token with no authorities, an LP fee of 30 bps, at least 0.5 SOL on the lent side.
   Alternative: a market lending test USDC.
   Where: the first and the eleventh ticket; script parameters.

## For the owner

- The first ticket can run now; it needs devnet SOL only (about 5 SOL sits in our reserve as the second depositor's deposit and can be taken back).
- The twelfth ticket's hold on [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22) should become real edges when Aviary's tickets are cut; a note there asks for it.
- The bar still says each program's last build ticket is its hardening ticket; the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM harden before their first deploy, and the tax AMM after it. One line in the bar could settle which it is.
- The twelfth ticket leaves the lending AMM's explanation pending your approval, since generating it is a paid call.

tickets.title: Cut the containment hook and tax AMM build tickets
tickets.decision: both specs were buildable once the tax AMM's file gained what the bar asks of each product (compute ceilings, invariants, warns, its place in Aviary); 18 build tickets, the tax AMM's eleven first and the hook's seven each after the tax AMM ticket it builds on; verified locally first with devnet last, deployed and then hardened; Canary reports a refused wallet-to-wallet transfer as a warn for any token; policy values in one config module per program, the mint allowlist in one shared crate ([tax AMM spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/tax-amm.md#building-it), [hook spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/containment-hook.md#building-it), [build ticket rules](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/agents/build-tickets.md))
tickets.resolution:
Yes: `docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, `docs/spec/containment-hook.md` and the bar in `docs/spec/README.md` are complete enough to build both from, once the small gaps below were filled and four questions were put to the owner.
No new decision ticket was needed.
Everything landed in [#90](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/90), with a follow-up in [#93](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/93).

### The build tickets

18 tickets, labelled `build`, sub-issues of the map, wired with native blocking edges, one session each.

Tax AMM, the first product to build:

1. [Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/58)
2. [Tax AMM: create a tax market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/59)
3. [Tax AMM: seed a market and trade it with buy and sell tax](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/60)
4. [Tax AMM: pay the tax out with distribute](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/61)
5. [Tax AMM: the tax authority](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/62)
6. [Tax AMM: seeding from another program](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/63)
7. [Tax AMM: proofs of the pricing, tax and split maths](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/64)
8. [Tax AMM: invariant fuzzing across every instruction](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/65)
9. [Tax AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and create a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/66)
10. [Tax AMM: hardening ticket](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/67)
11. [Tax AMM in Aviary: the launch form and the tax panel](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/75)

Containment hook:

1. [Containment hook: bind a token to its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/68)
2. [Containment hook: a contained token moves only through its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/69)
3. [Containment hook: unlock by the goal or the deadline](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/70)
4. [Containment hook: invariant fuzzing of contained tokens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/71)
5. [Containment hook: deploy on devnet and launch a contained token](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/73)
6. [Containment hook: hardening ticket](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/74)
7. [Containment hook in Aviary: the containment panel and the Unlock button](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/76)

- Tax AMM tickets 4 to 7 can run side by side after ticket 3; its devnet ticket waits for the proofs and the fuzzing; hardening follows the deploy.
- Each hook ticket is blocked by the tax AMM ticket it builds on: binding by market creation, the allow rule by trading and payouts, fuzzing by the tax AMM's fuzzing harness, the hook's devnet ticket by the tax AMM's.
- The two Aviary tickets are blocked by [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22) as a stand-in, since Aviary's own tickets do not exist yet; that ticket's session swaps the edge for the real ones.
- Every ticket cites the sections of the bar it covers, and they share [`docs/agents/build-tickets.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/agents/build-tickets.md).

### What the specs lacked, now in them

- [`tax-amm.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/tax-amm.md): "In Aviary" (the launch form and the tax panel), the order of the build, where its policy values live, compute ceilings per instruction, seven invariants for the fuzzing layer, the `pipeline-check` and Canary warns, and what is not measured yet. The bar asks each product's file for these and this file had none of them.
- [`containment-hook.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/containment-hook.md): the order of the build, where its policy values live, the framework (Anchor, native only if `Execute` cannot meet its ceiling), the Canary warns, and a second devnet token unlocked by its goal.

### For other tickets

- [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22): the owner's Canary decision below amends a row of `pipescope-canary.md`; posted there.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

Each is a default he may change. The register (`docs/decisions.md`) has not landed, so they are listed here for it.

**Answered by the owner in this session**

1. **How does Canary report a token that cannot be sent to another wallet?**
   - Answer: a refused wallet-to-wallet transfer is a warn for any token, ours or anyone else's, with the reason and what the buyer got back by selling. `exit_transferred` fails only when a transferred token cannot then be sold, and a refusal never raises the trade box's "could not sell back" notice.
   - Why it came up: every contained token refuses that transfer by design, so every home market would have shown a Canary fail, against the bar's rule that our strategies show none.
   - Alternatives: a warn only when the hook is ours (an exemption for our own product); keep the fail and write an exception into the bar.
   - Lives in: `containment-hook.md`, "Canary checks"; to be carried into `pipescope-canary.md`'s `exit_transferred` row. Changes by: spec only, until Canary is built.
2. **Where is a program verified before its devnet ticket?**
   - Answer: local first, devnet last. LiteSVM tests through the router's bytes copied from devnet, and the demo script on a local validator running devnet's router; only the devnet ticket deploys and registers.
   - Alternatives: deploy and register from the first ticket and upgrade devnet at every ticket, which shows half-built versions in Pipeline's registry and can strand early demo markets.
   - Lives in: "Order of the build" in both spec files; `docs/agents/build-tickets.md`, "Verify". Changes by: the tickets' wording.
3. **Is a program hardened before or after its first devnet deploy?**
   - Answer: deploy, then harden. The hardening ticket is the program's last, as the bar says, and redeploys and republishes if it changed the program.
   - Alternatives: harden first, so the first registered bytes are already reviewed (the buy wall AMM's tickets were cut that way, so the two products currently differ).
   - Lives in: "Order of the build" in both spec files; the blocking edges of the two hardening tickets. Changes by: two edges and a sentence.
4. **What name does the tax AMM register under?** Asked while Product and suite names was open; that ticket closed during this session, so it registers as Aviary Tax AMM and nothing was decided here.

**Set by this session, not yet put to the owner**

5. **The security contact** in the strategy metadata and the `security.txt`: this repo's private vulnerability reporting page on GitHub. Alternatives: an email address, a handle. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "Custom actions and metadata". Changes by: metadata, and a rebuild for the `security.txt`.
6. **The tax AMM's compute ceilings**: 25,000 units for a quote, 60,000 for a swap, and the rest of the table. They are set from what Pipeline's constant-product example costs, not measured; the build measures them. Alternatives: fix them only after measuring. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "Compute ceilings" and "Not measured yet". Changes by: spec and one test module.
7. **The tax AMM's seven fuzzing invariants**, derived from its rules. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "Invariants".
8. **The tax AMM in Aviary**: its own launch form in place of the generic `init` form, and what the tax panel shows, gathered from what the spec already promised. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "In Aviary".
9. **The containment hook is written in Anchor**, as the bar asks of every program, although the `test-hook` it starts from is native code; native only if `Execute` cannot stay under 10,000 units. Lives in: `containment-hook.md`, "Starting point".
10. **A second devnet token unlocked by its goal**, beyond the spec's one unlocked by its deadline, so the hook's read of the deployed tax AMM's counter is shown on devnet. Lives in: `containment-hook.md`, "Done means".
11. **Where policy values live**, applying the owner's standing rule: one config module per program for build-time constants (the tax cap, the suite share, the suite treasury and the recipient limit; for the hook the 90-day limit and the tax AMM's program id), creation parameters or `bind` arguments for everything else. The mint extension allowlist is one list in one small shared crate, which the tax AMM, the containment hook and the lending AMM all depend on, as the lending AMM's ticket-cutting session asked ([#93](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/pull/93)); a product with a stricter rule adds it on top. Alternatives: a copy of the list per program. Lives in: "Where its policy values live" in both spec files, and in the tickets' acceptance criteria.
12. **How our TypeScript uses Pipeline's SDK**, which is not on npm: a script clones Pipeline at the pinned commit into a gitignored folder and builds it there, never copied into the repo. Alternatives: a git dependency, which cannot build it. Lives in: the first build ticket. Changes by: one script.
13. **The slicing and the order**: 18 tickets, hook tickets free to start as soon as the tax AMM ticket they build on has merged. Alternatives: the hook strictly after the whole tax AMM. Lives in: the blocking edges and "Build tickets" in both spec files.

Follow-up from [Cut the lending pool's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/25): your tickets appeared while I was finishing, so the edge I asked for is wired. [Lending AMM: markets that trade from their own vaults](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/78) is now blocked by [Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/58) and [Tax AMM: create a tax market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/59), and its hold on this ticket is removed. The lending AMM tickets follow `docs/agents/build-tickets.md`, local demo run included. The one request left is the mint-rule check living where a second program can depend on it.

tickets.title: Cut Pool4 for Solana's build tickets
tickets.decision: the spec was complete, so ten `build` tickets with native blocking: a fixed-size market state with fixed discriminator bytes from the first ticket, the trading, cap, wall, payout and launchpad slices each reproducing their rows of the worked example, a release gate that refuses builds which would strand a market, hardening before the first deploy, and a devnet ticket that deploys, registers, runs the demo market and proves the gate with a real upgrade ([resolution](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/24#issuecomment-6760286986), [spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pool4-for-solana.md#build-tickets))
tickets.resolution:
`docs/spec/pool4-for-solana.md` (the buy wall AMM since [Product and suite names](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/17)) and `docs/spec/README.md` are complete enough to build from: checked section by section against Pipeline's template, interface and `pipeline-check` at `5ad130d`, they leave no decision open, so nothing went to the owner and no new decision ticket was needed.
They are cut into ten `build` tickets, one session each, with native blocking edges; the spec lists them in its new "Build tickets" section (#72).

Run order:

1. [Buy wall AMM: a market opens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/47): the program generated from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 template at `5ad130d`, the fixed-size market state with its byte offsets, creation, the mint rules and the seed. Waits for [Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/58).
2. [Buy wall AMM: plain trading through the router](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/48)
3. [Buy wall AMM: the inventory cap](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/49)
4. [Buy wall AMM: the buy wall](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/50)
5. [Buy wall AMM: payouts and recipient handovers](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/51)
6. [Buy wall AMM: seeding by another program](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/53): after ticket 2, so it can run beside tickets 3 to 5.
7. [Buy wall AMM: the release gate and layout fixtures](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/54)
8. [Buy wall AMM: hardening](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/55)
9. [Buy wall AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/56): the end of the program's chain.
10. [Buy wall AMM: Aviary panel and forms](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/57): off the chain, after ticket 9 and Aviary's own build tickets.

How the tickets are built:

- **No upgrade can strand a market.** Ticket 1 fixes one 1,024-byte zero-copy layout holding every field the whole spec needs, with a layout version, a zeroed reserve that only gains appended fields, a compile-time size check, and the discriminator written as fixed bytes so renaming a type can never change it. Every later ticket carries a criterion that no field moves. Ticket 7's gate replays every live market against a new build and must refuse test builds that move a field, change the discriminator or change the size. Ticket 9 then runs one real upgrade on devnet through the gate, against the live demo market.
- **Verified end to end.** Each ticket adds its steps to the demo script, run on a local validator with devnet's router, and its LiteSVM tests send the same router transactions a trader would send, against the router dumped from devnet and pinned by hash. Ticket 9 runs every check in the spec's "Done means" on devnet itself.
- **Each new number matches the spec.** Each ticket reproduces its rows of the spec's worked example exactly: the seed in 1, the prices in 2, the trim in 3, the wall in 4 and the settle in 5.
- **Built to the engineering bar.** Every ticket cites the sections of the bar it covers: compute ceilings, Proptest and Kani on the maths, the stateful fuzzer's invariants, `pipeline-check` with no Fail or Warn, CI and `/code-review` at high effort. The hardening ticket follows the bar to the letter.
- **Policy values stay cheap to change.** Every ticket's criteria require each policy value to live only in `config.rs` or a market's creation parameters, and require its PR to list the decision IDs it rests on and invite MetalLegBob to change them.

tickets.title: Pool4 for Solana design
tickets.resolution:
- **Fee**: chosen per market at creation, 0.25% to 3%, never changeable, and always taken in SOL (from the SOL paid in on a buy, from the SOL paid out on a sell), on top of Pipeline's 0.25%.
- **Trim split**: a reward share of 0% to 30% per market goes to one rewards recipient and the rest is burned; all trimmed SOL becomes the buy wall, and tokens the wall buys go through the same split.
- **Staking**: not in v1; a rewards recipient can be a staking program later.
- **Keeper jobs**: four permissionless custom actions, `place_wall`, `settle`, `pay_rewards` and `sweep_fees`. Only `place_wall` tips: the lower of 0.002 SOL and the market's fee rate times the SOL handled, once 0.01 SOL is idle or spent.
- **Containment hook**: optional by design, but not in v1, because [Containment hook policy](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/18) closed during this session with a first version that binds only tax AMM markets. Pool4 for Solana works with plain mints and keeps what a later hook version would need (router-only counters, SOL-only fees and tips, liquidity that can never leave).
- **Parameters**: per market, fixed at creation: the fee, the wall split, the reward share, both recipients, the cap floor (0.1% to 100% of the seeded tokens) and the cap decay (0% to 100% a day). Fixed for every market: the cap starts at the seeded tokens, a buy lowers it by all the room it opens, the buy wall's crawl of about 4% a day behind a lagged reference, and the keeper thresholds. Pipescope's form pre-fills IMD's own launch values.
- **Where it leaves IMD's design**: rates per second, not per block; at most one day of cap decay allowance builds up while idle; no owner powers at all (IMD's owner can close the market and withdraw everything).
- **Markets**: anyone creates one, seeded by a launchpad in one call or created and seeded in one transaction; liquidity is locked for good; nobody controls a market afterwards, except that each recipient may hand its own role to another wallet. The token trades against wrapped SOL, with its mint and freeze authorities removed and only the tax AMM's extension allowlist; exact-in only; bypass refused.
- **Upgrades can never strand a market**: a fixed-size market state with a layout version and reserved space, a release gate that replays every live market against a new build before it deploys, and fixtures of every released layout in CI. Frozen before mainnet.
- **Checked before writing**: the pricing, trim, ratchet, wall and keeper rules ran as an integer model for 3,000 random sequences (about 957,000 swaps) with every invariant holding; the spec's worked example is the model's output, for the build to reproduce exactly.

One correction to what I told the owner while grilling: I said the reward share would wait in the vault until a contained token's unlock.
The hook's spec allows payouts out of a home vault, and its first version does not bind Pool4 for Solana markets at all, so the spec has no such wait; `pay_rewards` stays a separate action so burns never depend on a transfer.

For other tickets:

- [Cut Pool4 for Solana's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/24) is unblocked by this ticket; a suggested slicing is posted there.
- The keeper runner (the map's "Not yet specified") has Pool4 for Solana's part: the four jobs and when to run each, in the spec's "For the keeper runner".
- `docs/spec/README.md` lists its product files but not yet this one, the containment hook's or the lending pool's.

Every answer below is the owner's default, and each lives in one named place, so it is cheap to change.
The IDs are proposed, for [Decision register open to MetalLegBob's review](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/43) to adopt or renumber; sections are those of `docs/spec/pool4-for-solana.md`.
Bypass being refused and the conventions shared with the tax AMM are suite decisions, recorded in ADR 0001 and `docs/spec/tax-amm.md`.

Bounds are build-time constants, the rate a creation parameter, the pre-fill a form default. |
| POOL4-03 | In which token is the fee taken? | Always SOL: from the SOL paid in on a buy and the SOL paid out on a sell. | On whichever token comes in, as IMD does. | "Pricing" and "The fee". Code, before deployment. |
| POOL4-06 | What happens to trimmed tokens and SOL? | A reward share of 0% to 30% per market (the form pre-fills 15%) goes to one rewards recipient and the rest is burned; all trimmed SOL becomes the buy wall; tokens the wall buys go through the same split. | Burning everything; IMD's fixed 85/15 with its three-way reward split. | "Constants" (`MAX_REWARD_SHARE_BPS`), "Creation parameters" and "Keeper jobs". The limit is a build-time constant; the share and recipient are creation parameters. |
| POOL4-07 | Is staking with streamed rewards in v1? | No; a rewards recipient can be a staking program later. | Shipping a staking vault and dripper with v1, as IMD has. | "Not in v1". Spec only. |

The hook's program and spec. |

| POOL4-10 | Who controls a market after the seed? | Nobody, us included: no close, no withdrawal, no parameter change. Each of the two recipients may hand its own role to another wallet. | IMD's owner powers (close, withdraw, change every parameter); recipients fixed for good. | "What it is" and "Recipients". Code. |
| POOL4-11 | Which parameters does a creator choose? | Per market: the fee, the wall split, the reward share, both recipients, the cap floor (0.1% to 100% of the seeded tokens) and the cap decay (0% to 100% of them a day). Fixed for all: the cap starts at the seeded tokens, a buy lowers it by all the room it opens, the wall's guard rates and the keeper thresholds. The form pre-fills a floor of 20% and a decay of 20% a day, IMD's own ratios. | Everything per market; everything fixed. | "Constants" and "Creation parameters". The rates are build-time constants; the rule is code. |

Only placing the wall tips its caller: the lower of 0.002 SOL and the market's fee rate times the SOL handled, once 0.01 SOL is idle or spent. | A flat share of the work on every job; jobs only our keeper may call. | "Keeper jobs" (`WALL_THRESHOLD`, `KEEPER_TIP_CAP`). Build-time constants. |
| POOL4-16 | How do upgrades avoid stranding markets? | A fixed-size market state with a layout version and reserved space, a release gate that replays every live market against the new build, and fixtures of every released layout in CI. | Migrating accounts at each upgrade; resizable accounts. | "Market state". Code and release process. |
| POOL4-17 | Which tokens may a market hold? | The token against wrapped SOL only; the token's mint and freeze authorities removed by the seed; Token-2022 extensions on the tax AMM's allowlist. | Allowing mint and freeze authorities, as the tax AMM does; other quote mints. | "Mint rules". Code. |
| POOL4-18 | What is the mainnet upgrade policy? | Frozen before any mainnet deployment, after the designer share's wallet is set. | The shared default: a multisig with a timelock first. | "Upgrades and freezing". Spec; carried out by the mainnet launch effort. |

tickets.title: Lending pool design
tickets.decision: two-mint constant-product markets with open LP shares that lend their WSOL or USDC side to fixed Kamino reserves through cTokens; a 20% buffer rebalanced only outside 10% to 30% by a permissionless keeper job; a swap redeems its shortfall in the swap and never deposits; withdraw mode when Kamino's free liquidity falls below 5 times our position; all yield and the LP fee to LPs, who bear Kamino's losses and can always leave in kind; no admin, frozen before mainnet; Kamino only ([spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/lending-pool.md), [Kamino facts](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/research/lending-market/research/lending-market-kamino-facts.md))
tickets.resolution:
Decided with the owner in three rounds; the spec is [`docs/spec/lending-pool.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/lending-pool.md) (merged in #38), and the Kamino facts checked for it are [lending-market-kamino-facts.md](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/research/lending-market/research/lending-market-kamino-facts.md) on the research branch.

**The ticket's questions**

- **Buffer and rebalance:** a fixed 20% of the lent side's total, rebalanced back to 20% only when it leaves the 10% to 30% band, with a dust floor; the same for every market.
- **Keeper job:** `rebalance` is a permissionless custom action that does nothing inside the band; our keeper runner calls it when Pipescope's indexer sees a market leave its band, plus a sweep every 10 minutes; no tip. One keeper job per market; no withdrawal-ticket job.
- **Mints:** exactly one lent side per market, WSOL or USDC, each tied to one Kamino reserve compiled into the program per cluster (mainnet: the main market's SOL and USDC reserves; devnet: our own Kamino lending market); creators never pick a reserve. The other side follows the tax AMM's mint rules, so hooked tokens are allowed (the hooked transfer and the Kamino redeem are sibling calls and never stack) and transfer-fee or permanent-delegate mints are refused.
- **Swaps larger than the buffer:** a swap redeems just the shortfall from Kamino in the same swap, and never deposits; the quote reads Kamino's free liquidity, withdrawal cap and flags, so a trade above buffer plus what Kamino can pay is refused cleanly.
- **Yield:** all to LPs through share value, with the LP fee (creator-set, 0% to 2%, default 0.30%); no cut for us or the creator.

**The research comment's nine questions**

1. Swaps redeem the shortfall in the swap (above).
2. Only WSOL and USDC are lent.
3. Mainnet: main market SOL `d4A2...` and USDC `D6q6...`; devnet: our own lending market, whose reserves need only a non-default price key (we name the live devnet Pyth feeds so a test borrower can create utilisation).
4. cTokens are valued everywhere at the reserve's stored rate (lag 2 to 68 s, about 0.05 bps an hour), from the reserve's own fields; LPs bear Kamino's written-off losses pro rata.
5. Near full utilisation: withdraw mode, entered when Kamino's free liquidity is below 5 times our lent value and left above 10 times; withdrawal tickets are off on the main market.
6. Kamino's switches: no admin of our own; blocked cToken deposits skip deposits, emergency mode or a deprecated reserve leaves swaps on the buffer alone, and LPs can always leave in kind (other side, buffer share, cTokens) without calling Kamino.
7. Farm rewards attach only to obligations and pay nothing on SOL and USDC today, so cToken holders miss nothing.
8. Kamino only, isolated in one module; Jupiter Lend is out of scope for this map.
9. LiteSVM tests on klend's deployed program with cloned reserves (in-swap redeem at one extra outer level with a hooked token, every Kamino state by edited account data, Kamino's real `socialize_loss`), plus a devnet demo on our own lending market including withdraw mode and emergency mode.

**Also decided:** constant-product pricing over total reserves; open LP shares with a locked minimum and `lock_lp` for protocol-owned liquidity; adds go to the buffer; removals are pro rata, in cash or in kind; bypass refused; exact-in only; market address `["market", other_mint, lent_mint, lp_fee_bps]`; seeding supported at a seeder-scoped address; frozen before mainnet, refusing to price if Kamino's reserve layout changes.

[Cut the lending pool's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/25) now has its product file; it still needs `docs/spec/README.md` from [Engineering and security bar for our on-chain programs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/4).

Follow-up merged in #42: the spec now also carries what `docs/spec/README.md` asks of each product (compute ceilings, layer-3 invariants, no accepted `pipeline-check` warnings, and the mainnet upgrade policy: frozen before mainnet, a stated departure from the shared multisig-then-freeze default). [Cut the lending pool's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/25) has both files it needs.

tickets.title: Containment hook policy
tickets.decision: a contained token moves only into or out of its one tax AMM home market (no wallet-to-wallet transfers, no integrator fee accounts); a write-once `bind` signed by the mint authority fixes the market, a goal and a deadline of at most 90 days; anyone may unlock once the market's tax collected (in the quote mint, not volume) reaches the goal or the deadline passes, from a Pipescope button, no keeper; frozen before mainnet ([spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/containment-hook.md), [ADR 0006](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0006-unlock-goal-counted-by-the-home-market.md))
tickets.resolution:
- **Transfers while contained**: only into or out of the home market's vault or its Pipeline fee account. Every wallet-to-wallet transfer is refused, including between your own wallets and to a CEX deposit address. A buy may deliver the token to anyone, who can then only sell it back.
- **Integrator fees**: no integrator fee accounts are allowed, so sells of a contained token carry no integrator fee. This is already Pipescope's rule, since it charges only on SOL or USDC input.
- **Home market**: exactly one per token. In v1 it is a tax AMM market with its tax side on the quote mint.
- **Unlock goal**: the home market's `tax_collected`, in the quote mint, not volume. A tax authority can lower the tax to 0 within its fixed range and the tax AMM has no LP fee, so faked volume would cost only Pipeline's 0.25%. Counting tax means forcing an early unlock always costs a third party the whole goal. There is no minimum age.
- **Who sets it**: the launcher, at binding. `bind` is signed by the mint authority and write-once, and nothing can change the config afterwards, us included. It goes after `create_market` and `init_fee_account` and before the tax AMM's seed. The hook refuses every transfer until `bind`. Launchpad graduation through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` is not in v1.
- **Mint rules at binding**: an extension allowlist matching the tax AMM's (transfer hook, metadata, group); everything else is refused. The freeze authority must be unset.
- **Fallback**: a required unlock deadline, at most 90 days after binding. After it, the unlock is due even if the goal was never met.
- **Who triggers the unlock**: anyone. `unlock` is permissionless and clears both the hook program and its authority. Pipescope shows an Unlock button. There is no keeper job in v1.
- **Launch**: a devnet CLI script. Pipescope v1 doesn't launch tokens, and its tax AMM launch form refuses mints hooked by us.
- **Engineering**: start from `test-hook`'s code but replace its fail-open path with the fail-closed allow rule. The hook is frozen before any mainnet use. Ceilings are `Execute` 10k, `bind` 60k and `unlock` 30k CU. Five invariants for the fuzzing layer.

Answers to the questions posted here from [Tax AMM rules](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/19):
1. The unlock reads `tax_collected`, with the tax side on the quote mint and no minimum age.
2. Wash trading is answered by counting tax collected, so no minimum tax range is needed.
3. The hosted API's refusal of hooked input mints is in the spec: Pipescope builds those swaps with the SDK.

tickets.title: Pipescope architecture
tickets.decision: everything on the existing Cloudflare account, where Workers Paid was already active (nothing bought): an API Worker holding the indexer, live rooms and Canary's Container, and a Next.js web Worker; Postgres on a new Neon project as the only record; our own indexer, with Pipeline's hosted API only a test oracle, holding its socket only while someone watches so the account stays inside its allowance; the API prepares and simulates every transaction; Canary natively in a Container with no network, fed one snapshot a market by a Durable Object per strategy version; verified builds on GitHub Actions; explanations generated on the owner's Mac after approval, no LLM key in Cloudflare; a public rate-limited API; owner tasks: Pipescope's own Helius key, the Neon project, a GitHub token ([spec](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md), [ADR 0003](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-pipescope-indexes-pipeline-itself.md), [ADR 0004](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-postgres-on-neon-is-pipescopes-record.md), [ADR 0005](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-canary-checks-run-natively-in-a-container.md))
tickets.resolution:
Resolved with the owner on 2026-11-10 (all recommendations accepted). Spec: [`docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md), merged in #35.

- **Platform**: everything on the owner's existing Cloudflare account, as two Workers, `pipescope-api` (Hono API, indexer and live-room Durable Objects, the Canary Container, crons) and `pipescope-web` (Next.js 16 through OpenNext).
  **No purchase**: Workers Paid is already active (Top-pad's vision Container runs on the account; Containers need Workers Paid).
- **Data**: Postgres on a new Neon free project through Hyperdrive with its cache off, the only system of record ([ADR 0004](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-postgres-on-neon-is-pipescopes-record.md)).
- **Indexer**: our own, ported from Top-pad, on the router and every strategy program, with reconciliation, registry snapshots, a ProgramData watch and a full backfill; Pipeline's hosted devnet API is only a test oracle ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-pipescope-indexes-pipeline-itself.md)).
  It holds its socket only while someone watches a page, because a second always-awake indexer would push the account (shared with Top-pad, whose indexer uses about 310,000 of the 400,000 GB-s a month) past its Durable Object allowance; otherwise a cron each minute.
  Market accounts are re-read after each event; no account subscriptions; no webhook spike.
- **RPC**: Pipescope's own free Helius key (owner task).
- **Trading path**: the API prepares and simulates every transaction (swap, custom action, create market) and returns it with the outcome and balance changes; the wallet signs and sends; the page reports the signature (Top-pad's fast path). Quotes are RPC simulations of `pipeline_quote`; the Container is never on the trading path. Fee rate, fee mints and fee accounts are Worker vars.
- **Canary runner**: native Rust `crates/canary` in a Cloudflare Container (`basic`, internet off), one Durable Object per strategy version, router loaded from its deployed bytes, a seam to switch from `simulate_swap` to direct calls plus settlement ([ADR 0005](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-canary-checks-run-natively-in-a-container.md)).
- **Verified builds**: a GitHub Actions workflow started by the API, with an untrusted build job and a trusted compare job; a match is evidence, never proof.
- **Metadata fetcher**: in the API, on events and hourly, with size, type, timeout and redirect limits.

- **Copied from Top-pad** (`b833a7b`): the indexer core, the Indexer Durable Object, candles, live rooms, Drizzle and migrations, the API and web scaffolds, the Container pattern, Playwright and the restart test; not the Codama clients.
