  The programs load and run in LiteSVM and on the local validator, through devnet's router, so it is noise from the toolchain, not a fault of a program.

documents.title: Spec
documents.body:
The build-ready spec for the Pipeline suite on devnet, charted by [Map: a build-ready spec for the Pipeline suite on devnet](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/1).
This file holds what every product shares; each product has its own file beside it, and decisions with a lasting trade-off are ADRs in `docs/adr/`.
Terms are as in `GLOSSARY.md`, and the toolchain and its install steps are in `docs/toolchain.md`.

## Product files

- `pipescope.md`: Aviary's first devnet version.
- `pipescope-architecture.md`: where each part of Aviary runs and keeps its data.
- `pipescope-canary.md`: Aviary's Canary checks.
- `pipescope-explainer.md`: Aviary's explainer.
- `pipescope-screens.md`: what each of Aviary's pages shows and how it behaves.
- `pipescope-telegram.md`: Aviary's Telegram bot.
- `tax-amm.md`: the tax AMM.
- `containment-hook.md`: the containment hook.
- `pool4-for-solana.md`: the buy wall AMM.
- `lending-pool.md`: the lending AMM.
- `keeper-runner.md`: the keeper runner, which calls our products' keeper jobs.

The files keep the names they were written under, so links to them still work; "Names" below says what each product is called.

## Names

Decided with the owner in [Product and suite names](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/17) on 2026-11-10.
Like every decision in this spec, they are defaults that MetalLegBob may change.

- The suite and its terminal share one public name, **Aviary**.
- Our on-chain products keep plain descriptive names and carry the suite's name before their own in public: Aviary Tax AMM, Aviary Containment Hook, Aviary Buy Wall AMM and Aviary Lending AMM.
  In prose they are the tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM.
- Canary checks keep their name; they are a feature of Aviary, with no address or handle of their own.
- The buy wall AMM is a port of IMD's Pool4 design and says so wherever it is described; Pool4 is IMD's product name and is never part of ours.
- No name of ours uses Pipeline's or the Factory's branding; "built on Pipeline" appears only as a plain description.
- A name is cheap to change, because each lives in one place:
  - the terminal's public name, address and fee label are one config module of the web app ([`pipescope-architecture.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md), "`terminal-web`");
  - each on-chain program's public name lives beside the program and nowhere else: the `name` in its strategy metadata, and the `name` in the `security.txt` it embeds, a build-time constant.
- Nothing else in code carries a public name: apps, packages, Workers, databases, crates and programs are named for what they are (`terminal-web`, `tax-amm`, `containment-hook`, `buy-wall-amm`, `lending-amm`).
- The repo and folder keep the internal name `testing-pipeline`.

## Our products live inside Aviary

Decided with the owner in [Pipescope v1 scope](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/3).

- The tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM get no websites of their own.
- Their user actions run through Aviary's custom-action forms, from each strategy's own complete metadata (see "Metadata, IDL and conformance report" below).
- Each product adds its own panel and forms to Aviary when it is built, for example progress toward the unlock goal for the containment hook, the wall and the inventory cap for the buy wall AMM, the buffer for the lending AMM, and the launch form and payouts that [`tax-amm.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/tax-amm.md) describes for the tax AMM.
- So each product's build tickets include its metadata, its Aviary panel and its Aviary forms.

## Engineering and security bar for on-chain programs

Decided with the owner on 2026-11-10 in [Engineering and security bar for our on-chain programs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/4), against Pipeline commit `5ad130d`.
It applies to every on-chain program we write: the tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM, the lending AMM and any single-use AMM.
A program's build tickets count as done on devnet only when the program meets all of it, and each build ticket's acceptance criteria name the sections below that it covers.
External audits belong to the mainnet launch effort, which is out of scope.

### Framework and toolchain

- Anchor `=1.2.2`, with the rest pinned as Pipeline pins it: Rust 1.97.1, cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0, platform tools v1.58 (v1.57 on the owner's Intel Mac, see `docs/toolchain.md`), sBPF v3, LiteSVM 0.18.2 and Kani 0.67.0.
- When Pipeline moves a pin, we move ours to match, in a PR of its own; Anchor 2.0 waits for a stable release and for Pipeline to move.
- Native code or Pinocchio only when a build ticket measures that a program cannot fit its compute budget in Anchor, and that ticket records the measurement.
- The release profile sets `overflow-checks = true`, `lto = "fat"` and `codegen-units = 1`.
- On-chain code uses checked arithmetic and returns errors: no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or unchecked indexing.
- Each program is built by its own manifest, never as a whole workspace, because a workspace build unifies dependency features and changes a program's bytes.

### Starting point

- Each strategy starts from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template (`templates/strategy`, generated with `scripts/new-strategy.sh` from a scratchpad clone), copied into this repo and owned here; the PR that adds it notes the Pipeline commit.
- The containment hook, which is a transfer-hook program and not a strategy, starts from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 `test-hook` allowlist hook (`programs/test-hook`).
- Pipeline's crates (`pipeline-strategy-interface`, `pipeline-client`, `pipeline-check`) are git dependencies pinned by `rev`, never by `branch` as the template ships them.
  That `rev`, in the on-chain workspace's `programs/Cargo.toml`, is the one place in code where Pipeline's commit is pinned.
- The router's source (BSL 1.1 until 2028-11-08) is never copied in.

### Strategy rules

- Our strategies refuse bypass: `pipeline_swap` accepts only the router's market signer for that market, so every swap of ours goes through the router, pays the Pipeline fee and emits a swap event ([ADR 0001](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-our-strategies-refuse-bypass.md)).
- `pipeline_quote` and `pipeline_swap` call one shared pricing function (the template's `pricing.rs`), so a quote is exactly what the swap does.

### Test layers

Tests run against the real router.
A fixture script, from the template's `scripts/fetch-router.sh`, copies the router deployed on devnet into a gitignored fixtures folder and checks its hash against the hash pinned in the repo.
When MetalLegBob upgrades the devnet router the check fails, and a PR re-pins it deliberately after the tests pass against the new bytes.

1. **LiteSVM integration tests** of every instruction, through the router wherever the router is involved, with hostile cases modelled on Pipeline's `adversarial.rs` and `test-strategy-evil`: a wrong or missing market signer, bypass attempts, aliased and substituted accounts, and Token-2022 mints with a transfer fee and with a transfer hook.
2. **Maths proofs.** The maths lives in pure functions that take no accounts.
   Proptest runs at least 10,000 cases per property, and Kani proves them, with bounded harnesses by default and full-domain ones behind `--cfg kani_full` as in Pipeline.
   Z3 proves division and rounding where Kani cannot relate a division's output to its inputs.
   Book of Knowledge (see "Internal adversarial review") chooses the properties.
3. **Stateful invariant fuzzing**: Proptest generates sequences of swaps, custom actions and clock jumps against LiteSVM and checks after every step that value is conserved (no token is created or lost beyond the stated fees), that every holder can still exit, and that each quote equals its swap; each product's spec file adds its own invariants.
   Trident is not used: its stable release (0.12) is built on solana-sdk 2.3 and 0.13 has been a release candidate since 2026-05, so it cannot load Anchor 1.2 and Solana 3 and 4 crates.
   [Prior art for behavioural testing of Solana programs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/8) found no fuzzer that fits better: Trident runs hand-written flows on its own SVM rather than LiteSVM.
   Revisit this if Trident moves to current Solana crates.
4. **Conformance**: every strategy's LiteSVM tests run `pipeline-check`'s `check_market` on their markets and require zero Fail and zero Warn.
5. **Limits**: a compute ceiling asserted per instruction, with headroom, and a call-depth test with hooked mints wherever a program calls another program inside a swap.
6. **Outside protocols**: wherever a program calls one (the lending AMM's lending market), its tests also run in LiteSVM loaded with that protocol's programs and accounts dumped from mainnet by a fixture script pinned to a slot, and against the protocol's devnet deployment if it has one.
7. **Devnet demo**: a script deploys the program, registers it, creates a market and swaps through the router with the TypeScript SDK, and every demo market passes `pipeline-check --url devnet --market <market> --fail-on-warn`.
8. **Canary checks**: once Aviary's Canary checks exist, our strategies must pass them on devnet, like any other strategy.

A `pipeline-check` Warn, in layer 4 or 7, is accepted only with a written reason in the program's spec file; a Skip for a feature the program refuses by design (such as exact-out) needs no reason.

### CI

- One GitHub Actions workflow, required to pass before any merge that touches on-chain code.
- It runs: a check that no keypair is in the repo (as Pipeline's `scripts/check-no-keypairs.sh`), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, each program's SBF build, test layers 1 to 5 (and 6 once its fixtures exist), and the Kani proofs and any Z3 proofs.
- The first on-chain build ticket adds it; that is the tax AMM's, the first product to build.
- Standard GitHub-hosted runners cost nothing on a public repository.

### Internal adversarial review

- Tools: Stronghold of Security (an adversarial audit) and Book of Knowledge (maths verification) from MetalLegBob's MIT-licensed Solana Vibes Kit (`https://github.com/MetalLegBob/solana-vibes-kit`), the process Pipeline's router went through twice.
  They are installed in this repo's `.claude/skills` at a pinned commit, by the first on-chain build ticket.
- Each program's last build ticket is its **hardening ticket**, run in a fresh session after its feature tickets have merged:
  - Round 1: a full Stronghold of Security audit and a Book of Knowledge pass; every confirmed finding gets a fix and a LiteSVM regression test named `sos_<finding id>`, as in Pipeline.
  - Round 2: Stronghold's verify phase and a re-audit of the code the fixes changed.
- The hardening ticket is done when no Critical, High or Medium finding is open; a Low finding is accepted only with the owner's written sign-off, recorded in the report.
- Reports go in `docs/security/<program>/`.
- Separately, every build PR gets `/code-review` at high effort before it merges.
- These reviews are internal and are never presented as audits, in metadata or anywhere else.

### Verified builds

- Every devnet deploy is a `solana-verify` (0.5.2 or later) Docker build with the same pins as Pipeline: `[workspace.metadata.cli] solana` chooses the Docker image (4.3.0 at `5ad130d`), `[workspace.metadata.solana] tools-version` chooses the platform tools, and the build passes `--arch v3`.
- Each deploy is recorded in `deployments/devnet.json`: program id, executable hash, commit and Docker image digest.
- After each deploy, `solana-verify get-program-hash -u devnet <program id>` must equal the build's executable hash; OtterSec's verified builds cover mainnet only, so on devnet we compare the hashes ourselves.
- Every program embeds a `security.txt` (the `solana-security-txt` crate) with the contact and the source repository.

### Published source

- The source is published from this repo; making it public is the owner's action.
  A program may be deployed on devnet while the repo is still private (owner, 2026-11-19), and the criteria that need its public links (the metadata URI and every link in it resolving, Pipeline's hosted API reading them) are met once it is public (`BAR-21`).
- `solana-verify verify-from-repo` takes this repo with the on-chain workspace as its mount path.
- The on-chain workspace carries its own Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` ([ADR 0002](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-on-chain-source-public-under-apache-2.md)).

### Metadata, IDL and conformance report

- Every strategy publishes complete `pipeline-strategy-metadata/1` metadata that passes `pipeline-client`'s validator with zero warnings.
- `source` names this repo, the deployed commit and the program's directory; `links.idl` points at the program's Anchor IDL; `conformance` points at the devnet demo's `pipeline-check` JSON report with its SHA-256; `security.contact` is set; and the `init` form and every custom action are listed.
- Custom actions are described under a top-level key of our own, `aviary_actions`, in the shape Pipeline's metadata gave its `actions` section before Pipeline 0.2.0 dropped custom actions from its standard and SDK (BAR-41); Pipeline's validator allows the unknown key with no warning, and the `strategy-actions` package in `packages/` validates the section and builds each action, for the demo scripts and Aviary.
- The metadata, the IDL and the report are committed beside the program and linked through `raw.githubusercontent.com` at the commit hash, so the content behind a link never changes.
- Each deploy updates the router's metadata URI for the strategy.
- `security.audits` stays empty.

### Upgrade authority

- On devnet every program stays upgradeable, under one project upgrade-authority key, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/upgrade-authority.json`, separate from the wallet that pays for deploys (`wallet.json`) and never committed.
  The upgrade authority also signs `register_strategy` and pays its listing fee, so it holds a little devnet SOL.
- Nothing is frozen on devnet while Pipeline's interfaces can still change.
- Aviary gives our programs no exemption and no trusted badge: Canary checks and trust facts show them as upgradeable by a single key, exactly as they would anyone else's.
- Each product's spec file states the product's intended mainnet upgrade policy: a multisig with a timelock, then frozen once stable, unless the product says otherwise.
  The containment hook is the most sensitive, because an upgrade to it could block every contained token's transfers.
  Carrying the policy out belongs to the mainnet launch effort.

### What each product's spec file adds

- Its intended mainnet upgrade policy.
- Its compute ceilings per instruction.
- Its invariants for test layer 3, beyond the shared three.
- Any accepted `pipeline-check` Warn, with the reason.
- What its Aviary panel shows and which actions its metadata exposes.

documents.title: Containment hook
documents.body:
## What it is

- One Token-2022 transfer hook program, deployed once, that serves every contained token.
- While a token is contained, every transfer of it must go into or come out of its one home market; everything else is refused.
- Once its home market has collected the unlock goal in tax, or its unlock deadline passes, anyone can unlock it: the hook removes itself and the token becomes an ordinary Token-2022 token, tradable everywhere.
- In v1 every home market is a tax AMM market whose tax side is the quote mint, on devnet only.

## Lifecycle

1. The launcher creates the mint with the transfer hook pointing at this program and the token's unlock PDA as hook authority, and mints the supply (minting never calls the hook).
2. The launcher creates the home market on the tax AMM, binds it and seeds it (see "Launch in v1").
3. While contained, the token trades only in its home market, and its tax builds up there.
4. Once the unlock is due, anyone calls `unlock`.
5. After the unlock, Token-2022 no longer calls any hook for this mint.

Until `bind`, the hook refuses every transfer, so no liquidity can go in before the rules are fixed.

## Accounts

All are PDAs of the containment hook program, one set per contained mint.

| Account | Seeds | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config | `["config", mint]` | The mint, the home market (the router's `Market` address), its market state, the token's vault in it, its fee account, the quote mint, the unlock goal, the unlock deadline, when it was bound, when it was unlocked (or never), bumps |
| Validation account | `["extra-account-metas", mint]` (the standard transfer hook interface seed) | One extra account for Token-2022 to pass on every transfer: the config, read-only |
| Unlock PDA | `["unlock", mint]` | No data; it is the mint's transfer hook authority and signs the unlock |

The config is never closed, so it stays as the record of the token's containment after the unlock.

## Binding (`bind`)

- Signed by the mint's mint authority, which is how the hook knows the caller is the launcher; nobody else can bind a mint, so binding cannot be front-run.
- Creates the config and the validation account; it fails if the config already exists, which makes binding write-once.
- No instruction changes the config afterwards: not the launcher, not us.
- Arguments: the unlock goal (greater than zero, in quote-mint base units, a `u64`) and the unlock deadline (a Unix timestamp strictly later than the binding's clock and at most the longest deadline after it, `MAX_UNLOCK_DEADLINE_SECS` in "Where its policy values live"; a deadline exactly that far away is allowed).
- Paid for by a payer that may be the mint authority or any other signer, so a launcher whose mint authority holds no SOL can still bind.

### Checks on the mint

- Owned by Token-2022.
- Its transfer hook program is this program, and its transfer hook authority is its unlock PDA.
- Its only extensions are on an allowlist: transfer hook, metadata pointer, token metadata, group pointer, group member pointer, token group and token group member (the tax AMM's own mint allowlist, none of which gives power over anyone's balance).
  Every other extension is refused, including permanent delegate (it can move or burn anyone's tokens), confidential transfer (the hook would see `u64::MAX` instead of the amount), default account state (accounts that start frozen), transfer fee (Token-2022 withdraws withheld fees without calling the hook, an escape route), pausable, and any extension Token-2022 adds later.
- Its freeze authority is unset, because freezing the home market's vault would trap every holder with nowhere else to sell; this is stricter than the tax AMM, which allows freeze authorities.
- The mint authority may stay set; the launcher can revoke it after binding, and Canary checks report it as they do for any mint.

### Checks on the home market

- The `Market` account is owned by Pipeline's router and sits at its PDA `["market", strategy, market_state]`.
- Its strategy is the tax AMM, whose program id is fixed in the hook at build time.
- One of its two mints is the contained mint; the other is the quote mint.
- The market state passed in is the one the `Market` records, owned by the tax AMM, and its tax side is the quote mint's index, so its tax collected is counted in the quote mint.
- `bind` reads the token's vault from `Market.vaults` and derives the fee account (the Token-2022 associated token account of the router PDA `["fees", market]` for the contained mint), rather than taking either from the caller.

One home market per token: several would split the liquidity that containment exists to concentrate, and summing tax in different quote mints would need a price on chain.

## The allow rule

The hook's `Execute` fails closed: it refuses the transfer unless all of these hold.

- The validation account and the config are present and at their PDAs for this mint, and the mint is the one Token-2022 is transferring.
- The source token account has Token-2022's `transferring` flag set, so nobody can call `Execute` directly.
- The source or the destination is one of the two allowed accounts: the home market's vault for the token, or the market's fee account for the token.

It makes no CPI, because on a buy it already runs at the last call level the runtime allows (router, strategy, Token-2022, hook).
The allowed sets are the same for sources and destinations, and neither allowed account is controlled by a wallet: the vault is moved only by the tax AMM and the fee account only by the router's `sweep_fees`.

### What this allows

- Buys and sells through the router (sells pass on the destination, buys on the source).
- The Pipeline fee on sells, paid in the token into the fee account.
- `sweep_fees`, which moves the fee account to Pipeline's treasury (it passes on the source, so the treasury needs no entry).
- The tax AMM's one-time `seed` into the vault.
- The tax AMM's `distribute`, which pays tax out of the vault; with the tax side on the quote mint it never moves the contained token anyway.
- A transfer from an account to itself, which Token-2022 completes before it calls any hook, moving nothing, with or without the hook accounts (found by [Containment hook: invariant fuzzing of contained tokens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/71); `spl-token-2022` returns early on a self-transfer).

Bypass needs no rule: the tax AMM refuses it, so every trade in the home market goes through the router, pays Pipeline's fee and counts in the market's counters.

### What this refuses

- Every wallet-to-wallet transfer, including between a holder's own wallets and to a CEX deposit address; a holder who wants to move the token sells it and buys again.
- Funding a second market for the token anywhere, on Pipeline or elsewhere, and paying out of one.
- Any integrator fee on a sell, because the router pays it in the token into the integrator's own account, which is not allowed.
  Integrators must pass a zero integrator fee on sells of a contained token (at zero the router makes no transfer); buys pay their integrator fee in the quote mint as usual.

A buy may deliver the token to anyone's account, since the router does not check who owns the output account; that account can then only sell into the home market, so it is a gift, not an escape.
This includes another market's vault: a buy can deliver into it, since the hook cannot tell a vault from a wallet, but that market can neither pay the token out nor take it in from anyone, so it never trades it, and the token's liquidity stays in its home market (shown in `tests/second_market.rs` by [Containment hook: a contained token moves only through its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/69)).

## Unlock (`unlock`)

- Permissionless: it takes no signer of its own, so anyone can send it and pays only the transaction fee.
- Due when either holds:
  - the home market's `tax_collected`, read from the tax AMM market state recorded at binding (owner and address checked), is at least the unlock goal;
  - the clock's Unix timestamp is at or past the unlock deadline.
- Past the deadline the unlock does not need the market state: one that can no longer be read as the tax AMM's, after an upgrade changed it or the account was closed, counts as the goal not reached, and the deadline still unlocks, since it exists for a home market that stopped working (see "Unlock deadline").
  Before the deadline such a market state is refused, and its address is always checked against the one recorded at binding.
- Signed by the unlock PDA, it calls Token-2022's `TransferHookInstruction::Update` with no program id, then `SetAuthority(TransferHookProgramId, None)`, and records the unlock time in the config.
- Both fields must be cleared: Meteora's DAMM v2 and DLMM accept a mint with the transfer hook extension permissionlessly only when the hook program and the hook authority are both unset.
- It logs whether the goal or the deadline made it due (the goal when both hold), for Aviary's panel and indexers.
- A second call fails: the config already records the unlock (`AlreadyUnlocked`), and the hook authority that would have to sign is gone.

There is no keeper job for the unlock in v1.
Nothing breaks while an unlock waits, since sells into the home market keep working, and whoever wants out or wants the token trading elsewhere can press Aviary's Unlock button.

### After the unlock

- Token-2022 skips the hook; the mint keeps a transfer hook extension with both fields unset, as graduated Meteora DBC mints do.
- Integrators stop passing hook accounts; stale ones are ignored.
- The deprecated `Transfer` instruction without a mint still fails for this mint, as for any mint with the extension; wallets and routers use `transfer_checked`.

## Unlock goal

- The tax collected by the home market, in quote-mint base units (lamports when the quote mint is wrapped SOL): the tax AMM's `tax_collected` counter, which only router swaps change, buys and sells alike.
- Why the tax AMM counts it and not the hook: [ADR 0006](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0006-unlock-goal-counted-by-the-home-market.md).
- Set by the launcher at binding and never changed.
- Why tax collected rather than volume:
  - A tax authority may lower its market's taxes to the bottom of a range fixed at creation, which may be 0, and the tax AMM has no LP fee; at a 0% tax, faking volume would cost only Pipeline's 0.25%, so a vamp could wait for a low-tax window and force a permanent unlock cheaply.
  - Counting tax collected, forcing an early unlock always costs a third party the whole goal in tax, whatever the rate; at 0% the goal stops moving and the deadline unlocks the token.
  - It measures what containment protects: the token's tax income, until it has earned a set amount.
- The only party who can reach the goal cheaply is whoever receives the tax (they pay Pipeline's fee and the suite share and get the rest back), and they would be undoing their own protection.
- No minimum age: the deadline already bounds how long containment lasts, and the goal is the launcher's commitment.

## Unlock deadline

- Required at binding, at most the longest deadline after it (`MAX_UNLOCK_DEADLINE_SECS` in "Where its policy values live"); once it passes, the unlock is due even if the goal was never met.
- A contained token is a honeypot by construction if its home market stops working, for example after a bad tax AMM upgrade or a router upgrade that changes the fee account's derivation; the deadline caps how long holders can be stuck.

## Hook accounts callers must pass

- Every transfer of a contained token needs the same tail: the hook program, the validation account and the config, read-only.
- Sells put it in the router's `input_hook_accounts`; buys put it after the strategy's own accounts; `sweep_fees` takes it as remaining accounts; the tax AMM's `seed` takes it after its own accounts.
- Neither Pipeline client resolves hook accounts, and Pipeline's hosted API refuses to build swaps whose input mint has a transfer hook (`docs/API.md` at `5ad130d`), so Aviary, our scripts and anyone sweeping fees resolve them from the validation account and build those transactions with the SDK; a call that leaves them out is refused.

## Launch in v1

- A devnet CLI script in this repo launches a contained token.
  - Create the mint with only allowed extensions and no freeze authority, with the hook and its authority set as in "Lifecycle", and mint the supply.
  - Then the tax AMM's market creation (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Creating a market") with `bind` inserted before the seed: the router's `create_market` with the tax side on the quote mint, `init_fee_account` for each mint, `bind` with the goal and deadline given as required flags (no defaults), then the tax AMM's `seed`.
- `bind` belongs in the same transaction as the market's creation, but may go in a later one with the seed if the transaction is too large: nothing can move the token before `bind`, the market is closed to swaps until its seed, and only the seeder can seed.
  Measured by [Containment hook: bind a token to its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/68) on 2026-11-12: it does not fit (see "Measured"), so the script sends `bind` in the next transaction, before the seed, and measures it again on every run.
  It does not create an address lookup table to make it fit, since the table would cost a transaction of its own and a slot's wait before it can be used.
- Revoking the mint authority is an optional last step; it must come after `bind`, which needs the mint authority's signature, or the token can never be bound and never transfer.
- Graduating a contained token from a launchpad through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` is not supported in v1, because the seed would move tokens before the `Market` account that `bind` reads exists.
- Aviary v1 does not launch new tokens (`docs/spec/pipescope.md`), so the script is the only way to launch a contained token.
  The tax AMM's launch form in Aviary refuses a mint whose transfer hook is ours, since its seed would fail for a token not yet bound and a bound token already has its home market.

## In Aviary

`docs/spec/pipescope.md` has each product add its own panel to Aviary; this is the containment hook's, built with its build tickets.
The hook is not a strategy and has no strategy metadata, so its panel and its one action are built into Aviary rather than rendered from metadata.

- **Recognising a contained token**: its transfer hook program is ours, its hook authority is its unlock PDA, and its config exists.
- **Panel**, on the home market's page:
  - "Contained": the token can only be bought and sold in this market until it unlocks, and cannot be sent to another wallet;
  - the tax collected against the unlock goal, in the quote mint, as a number and a bar;
  - the unlock deadline, as a date and the time left;
  - once unlocked: when, and whether by the goal or the deadline.
- **Unlock button**: shown to anyone once the unlock is due; it sends `unlock` from the connected wallet.
- **Trade box**: before a buy of a contained token, the same one-line rule as the panel.
- **Swaps**: Aviary resolves the hook accounts for every swap of a hooked token, ours included, and builds those swaps with the SDK, since Pipeline's hosted API refuses them.
- **Integrator fee**: nothing to add; Aviary charges its fee only when the trader pays in SOL or USDC, so sells of a contained token already carry none.
- The facts panel shows the mint's `transfer-hook` and `transfer-hook-authority` trust flags until the unlock clears them, so traders who hide hooked tokens by those flags also hide contained ones.

## Depends on

- The tax AMM (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`): `tax_collected` and the tax side at fixed offsets that later versions never move, vaults at PDAs `["vault", market_state, mint]`, bypass refused, liquidity locked, tax paid out of the vault only, and the program frozen before mainnet because the unlock trusts its counter.
- `docs/spec/README.md`, the engineering and security bar every program of ours meets; "Building it" below adds what it asks of each product's file.
- Pipeline's router: the fee account's derivation belongs to the router, which is upgradeable on devnet; if an upgrade changed it, sells of contained tokens would fail until their deadline.

## Ruled out

- Allowing wallet-to-wallet transfers between keypair wallets signed by their owner: it needs an on-curve check, and an RFQ market maker quoting from a hot wallet could still take the home market's trading.
- A launcher-set list of integrator fee accounts allowed as destinations: it makes the allow rule asymmetric and gives launchers a list that could name a bid-only vamp pool, for a fee that only lasts until the unlock.
- Volume as the unlock goal, with or without a minimum-tax floor checked at binding: without a floor it is cheap to fake in a low-tax window, and a floor needs an arbitrary constant while still letting a third party force the unlock for the floor times the goal.
- Counting the goal in the hook, which would also count liquidity moves and donations, or from transfers into the fee account, which donations could fake; or a wrapper program reading the router's return data, which misses direct router swaps.
- A tax side on the contained token for home markets: the goal would be counted in the token itself, whose price the launcher's supply sets.
- Several home markets per token.
- Changing the goal or the deadline after binding, even only lowering them.
- A minimum age as part of the goal.
- A keeper job for the unlock in v1.
- Launchpad graduation into a contained home market in v1.
- Keeping `test-hook`'s fail-open path (see "Starting point").
- An upgradeable hook on mainnet, even under a multisig with a timelock.

## Building it

What `docs/spec/README.md` asks each product's spec file to add, and how this program meets the bar.

### Starting point

- The bar starts the hook from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 `test-hook` (`programs/test-hook`), for its licence and its extra-account-meta setup.
- `test-hook` approves every transfer when its whitelist account is left out (still so at `5ad130d`), and Token-2022 calls a hook without its extra accounts whenever a caller leaves them out, so that path is replaced by the fail-closed rule in "The allow rule"; the research's citations of the Factory's transfer hook show the checks to add (the `transferring` flag, the mint's owner, the validation account's seeds), read as a pattern, not copied.
- Pipeline crates are pinned to `rev = "5ad130d"`, as for the tax AMM; build and test with the toolchain in `docs/toolchain.md`.
- `test-hook` is native `solana-program` code, while the bar builds every program in Anchor 1.2.2 unless a build ticket measures that it cannot fit its compute budget.
  So the hook is written in Anchor, keeping `test-hook`'s validation account and `Execute`'s account order, and goes native only if `Execute` cannot stay under its ceiling below in Anchor, with the measurement recorded in that ticket.

### Order of the build

Decided with the owner on 2026-11-10 in [Cut the containment hook and tax AMM build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/23), as for the tax AMM (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Order of the build").

- The tax AMM is built first; the hook's tests need a tax AMM home market, so each hook ticket follows the tax AMM ticket it builds on, and the hook's devnet ticket follows the tax AMM's.
- **Local first, devnet last**: until its devnet ticket, the hook is verified by the LiteSVM tests through devnet's real router bytes and by the launch script run against a local validator that runs devnet's router.
- **Deploy, then harden**: the hardening ticket comes after the devnet ticket, and redeploys and repeats the devnet demo if it changes the program.

### Where its policy values live

As for the tax AMM (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Where its policy values live"), under the owner's standing rule of 2026-11-10.

- The longest unlock deadline and the tax AMM's program id are build-time constants in one config module of the program, `programs/containment-hook/src/config.rs`, and no other file repeats them; the program id is taken from the tax AMM's own crate, so its address is written once in the whole workspace.

  | Constant | Value | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `MAX_UNLOCK_DEADLINE_SECS` | 7,776,000 (90 days) | The latest unlock deadline `bind` accepts, in seconds after the binding |
  | `TAX_AMM_PROGRAM_ID` | the tax AMM's `declare_id!` | The only strategy a home market may run on |

- The mint extension allowlist is the tax AMM's own: `bind` calls the shared mint-rules crate (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Where its policy values live") and adds the hook's stricter rule that the freeze authority is unset.
- These are fixed on-chain because holders rely on them, so they can change until the hook is frozen and not after.
- The unlock goal and the unlock deadline are `bind`'s arguments, chosen per token by its launcher, with no default anywhere, the launch script included.
- The public name, Aviary Containment Hook, lives only in the `name` of the embedded `security.txt`, since the hook has no strategy metadata (`docs/spec/README.md`, "Names").
- The compute ceilings live in the table below and in one test module that mirrors it.

### Upgrade policy

- On devnet the hook stays upgradeable under the project upgrade-authority key, as the bar says.
- It is frozen (upgrade authority removed) before any mainnet use, rather than the bar's default of a multisig with a timelock: the hook's whole promise is that nobody can change the rules, and a key that can upgrade it could block every contained token's transfers at once.
- The cost is that a bug found after freezing cannot be fixed; the mainnet launch effort, out of scope here, audits the hook before freezing it.

### Compute ceilings

Tests assert the measured cost of each instruction with headroom, never above these ceilings.

| Instruction | Ceiling (CU) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Execute` | 10,000 | Runs on two transfers in every sell and one in every buy, inside the trader's swap; it uses bumps stored in the config instead of searching for them |
| `bind` | 60,000 | Creates two accounts and reads the mint's extensions, the router's `Market` and the market state |
| `unlock` | 30,000 | Two Token-2022 calls signed by the unlock PDA |

`bind`'s cost leaves out what its bump searches spend beyond each address's first bump, as the tax AMM's ceilings do (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Compute ceilings").
It searches four times, for the config, the validation account, the unlock PDA and the fee account's associated token address, at 1,500 units for each bump tried after the first, and how many each takes depends on the mint's address.
Less those, it costs the same on every mint (20,916 units measured on 2026-11-16), while with them the invariant fuzzer measured up to 55,416 units, so a ceiling on the whole cost would fail on a rare mint (measured by [Containment hook: invariant fuzzing of contained tokens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/71)).
`bind` runs once per token with the transaction's compute limit, so the search costs only compute, never a refusal.

### Invariants

For the bar's stateful fuzzing layer, beyond its shared three:

1. While contained, no sequence of actions moves the token between two accounts that are both outside the home vault and the fee account.
2. A transfer that leaves out or substitutes any hook account is refused, but for a transfer from an account to itself, which moves nothing (see "What this allows").
3. The config never changes after binding, except the unlock time, which is set once.
4. `unlock` succeeds exactly when the tax collected reaches the goal or the deadline has passed; afterwards both of the mint's hook fields are unset, and nothing else ever changes them.
5. The shared "every holder can still exit" invariant holds for contained tokens, through sells into the home market.

### Canary checks

The bar asks our strategies to pass Canary checks on devnet with every warn named in the product's file.
A contained token's home market is a tax market, so these add to the tax AMM's own (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Canary checks").

- `exit_transferred`: a warn on every contained token, because the hook refuses the wallet-to-wallet transfer the check makes.
  - Decided with the owner on 2026-11-10: a refused transfer is a warn for any token, ours or anyone else's, stating that the token could not be sent to another wallet and what the buyer got back by selling it.
  - The check fails only when a token that was transferred cannot then be sold.
  - A refused transfer is not "a buyer could not sell back", so it never raises the trade-box notice.
  - This replaces the fail in the `exit_transferred` row of `docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md`, which was written before this file fixed the allow rule.
    It follows that file's own rule that only what the ordinary trade meets can fail, and it gives our hook no exemption.
- `contained_mint`: a warn while the hook program can still be upgraded, which is always the case on devnet; it passes only once the hook is frozen.
- `token_authorities`: a warn while the launcher keeps the mint authority; revoking it after `bind` clears it.

### Not applicable

- `pipeline-check` Warns and strategy metadata: the hook is not a strategy; its Aviary panel and action are in "In Aviary".

### Build tickets

Cut by [Cut the containment hook and tax AMM build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/23) on 2026-11-10, labelled `build`, one session each, in run order after the tax AMM's (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Build tickets"):

1. [Containment hook: bind a token to its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/68): the program, its accounts and `bind` with every check; it needs the tax AMM's market creation.
2. [Containment hook: a contained token moves only through its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/69): the allow rule and the hook accounts callers pass; it needs the tax AMM's trading and payouts.
3. [Containment hook: unlock by the goal or the deadline](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/70): `unlock`, and transfers free of the hook afterwards.
4. [Containment hook: invariant fuzzing of contained tokens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/71): the hook's five invariants on the tax AMM's fuzzing harness.
5. [Containment hook: deploy on devnet and launch a contained token](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/73): the first devnet deploy, after the tax AMM's, with everything in "Done means" shown on devnet.
6. [Containment hook: hardening ticket](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/74): the hardening ticket, after the deploy.
7. [Containment hook in Aviary: the containment panel and the Unlock button](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/76): after the deploy, the tax AMM's own Aviary ticket and Aviary's build tickets.

Tickets 1 to 4 are verified by LiteSVM tests through the real router copied from devnet and by the launch script on a local validator; ticket 5 is the first to touch devnet.

### Done means

- LiteSVM tests through the real router with a tax AMM home market cover: buys, sells, the Pipeline fee and `sweep_fees` with the hook tail; refusal of wallet-to-wallet transfers, of a second market's funding, of a sell with a non-zero integrator fee and of every transfer missing a hook account or calling `Execute` directly; `bind`'s refusal of each refused extension, of a freeze authority, of a wrong signer, of a market on another strategy, of a tax side on the contained token, of a deadline beyond `MAX_UNLOCK_DEADLINE_SECS` and of a second `bind`; `unlock` by the goal, by the deadline, its refusal before either, and a second `unlock`; and transfers skipping the hook afterwards.
- The invariants above under the fuzzing layer, and the compute ceilings and a call-depth test on buys under the limits layer.
- On devnet: the hook deployed; a contained token launched by the script, bought and sold through the router with the SDK, a wallet-to-wallet transfer refused, then unlocked by a short deadline, with the mint showing both hook fields unset.
  A second contained token is unlocked by reaching a small goal, so the unlock's read of the deployed tax AMM's counter is shown on devnet too (added when the build tickets were cut).
- Whatever else `docs/spec/README.md` requires of our on-chain programs.

## Measured

By [Containment hook: bind a token to its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/68) on 2026-11-12, against devnet's router bytes:

- `bind` costs 22,366 compute units in LiteSVM (contained mint first in the market; 22,365 when it is second), under its 60,000 ceiling.
- The market's creation transaction (`create_market` and `init_fee_account` for each mint, as a version 0 transaction) is 1,143 bytes; with `bind` it is 1,307 bytes, over the 1,232 a transaction may hold, so `bind` goes in the next transaction.
  With an address lookup table holding every account that does not sign, the same transaction would be 690 bytes.
  The launch script measures both on every run, in step 4.
- `bind`'s cost moves with the bumps its PDAs need, which differ from mint to mint: 25,414 and 34,415 units on two mints measured on 2026-11-12 by [Containment hook: a contained token moves only through its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/69), still under its ceiling.

By [Containment hook: a contained token moves only through its home market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/69) on 2026-11-12, against devnet's router bytes, with `Execute` written in Anchor:

| Hooked transfer | `Execute` (CU), LiteSVM | `Execute` (CU), local validator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Out of the vault, on a buy | 5,578 | 5,578 |
| Into the vault, on a sell | 5,602 | 5,602 |
| Into the fee account, on a sell | 5,603 | 5,603 |

- Every one is under the 10,000 ceiling, so `Execute` stays in Anchor (see "Starting point"); `tests/compute.rs` asserts the ceiling on each, and the launch script prints the cost of each from its transactions' logs.
- On a buy the hook runs at the fourth call level (router, tax AMM, Token-2022, hook), the deepest a swap reaches, under devnet's limit, which does not have SIMD-0268's deeper calls; the whole buy costs 64,438 units.

By [Containment hook: unlock by the goal or the deadline](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/70) on 2026-11-16, against devnet's router bytes:

| Unlock | `unlock` (CU), LiteSVM | `unlock` (CU), local validator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| By the goal | 13,212 | 13,225 |
| By the deadline | 12,912 | 12,873 |

- Both are under the 30,000 ceiling; the cost does not move from mint to mint, since `unlock` uses the bumps the config stores, and differs between runs only by the length of the numbers it logs.
  `tests/compute.rs` asserts the ceiling, and the launch script prints the cost from the unlock's logs.

By [Containment hook: invariant fuzzing of contained tokens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/71) on 2026-11-16, against devnet's router bytes, with the invariant fuzzer (`tests/fuzz.rs`) on every market shape of the tax AMM's fuzzer:

- 20,000 sequences of up to 50 steps passed in 345 seconds on 20 threads of the owner's Mac, 10,589 of them ending unlocked; CI runs 1,000.
- The most each instruction took across them: `Execute` 5,603 units of its 10,000, `unlock` 13,655 of its 30,000, and `bind` 20,916 of its 60,000 once its bump searches beyond the first bumps are left out (see "Compute ceilings"); with them, an earlier run of 20,000 measured `bind` at up to 55,416 units.
- Each of the five invariants caught a deliberate fault in the hook on its own, with only it checked: the allow rule passing every transfer (1), `Execute` approving when Token-2022 calls it without the validation account and the config, as `test-hook` does (2), `unlock` also rewriting the deadline (3), `unlock` clearing the hook program but not the hook authority (4), and the fee account left out of the allowed accounts, which stops every sell (5).
- The fuzzer found three failures, all of its own model and none of the hook's, each fixed with a regression test: a transfer from an account to itself, which Token-2022 completes before it calls any hook (see "What this allows"); the seeder spending part of its seed before the seed, which the tax AMM's model now expects to be refused with `InsufficientFunds`; and that model judging a seed's two sides in the program's order.

documents.title: Keeper runner
documents.body:
Decided with the owner in [Keeper runner](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/45) on 2026-11-10.
It builds on the keeper jobs of [`pool4-for-solana.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pool4-for-solana.md) (the buy wall AMM, "Keeper jobs"), [`lending-pool.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/lending-pool.md) (the lending AMM, "When it runs") and [`tax-amm.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/tax-amm.md) ("Payout"), and on Aviary's architecture in [`pipescope-architecture.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md).
Terms are as in `GLOSSARY.md`: keeper job, keeper runner, keeper wallet, keeper tip.
Like every decision in this spec, each one here is a default MetalLegBob may change.

## What it is

- The keeper runner is one Node program in this repo, `apps/keeper`, that calls every keeper job of every market of our strategies when it is due, and pays for it from the keeper wallet.
- On devnet it runs on the owner's Mac as a launchd agent, reading the keeper wallet's key from `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/keeper.json`.
- Nothing of it runs on the owner's Cloudflare account (owner, 2026-11-10): the work is for MetalLegBob, so it must cost the owner nothing.
  Aviary itself stays on Cloudflare as [Pipescope architecture](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/13) decided; only the keeper runner, the one part that holds a hot key and spends SOL, lives elsewhere.
- It is portable: a Docker image and a README let MetalLegBob, or anyone, run it on their own machine with their own key, since every keeper job is permissionless.
- When the Mac sleeps or is off, jobs wait.
  Nothing breaks meanwhile: swaps keep working, a lending AMM swap redeems its own shortfall from Kamino, payouts only arrive later, and Aviary's panels show every due job as a button anyone can press.

## The jobs

| Product | Job | Due when | How the runner learns it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Buy wall AMM | `place_wall` | `idle_sol` or the wall's `converted` reaches `WALL_THRESHOLD` | After each transaction on the market, and in every sweep |
| Buy wall AMM | `settle` | `retired_tokens` above 0, at most once an hour per market | The hourly pass |
| Buy wall AMM | `pay_rewards` | `rewards_owed` above 0 | The daily pass |
| Buy wall AMM | `sweep_fees { slot }` | A slot's ledger above 0; slot 1 only once `DESIGNER_RECIPIENT` is set | The daily pass, one transaction per slot |
| Lending AMM | `rebalance` | The buffer is outside its band, or the market should enter or leave withdraw mode | After each transaction on the market, and the 10-minute sweep |
| Tax AMM | `distribute { slot }` | A slot is owed more than 0 (the burn slot included) | The daily pass, one transaction per slot |

- The containment hook's `unlock` has no keeper job in v1, as [Containment hook policy](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/18) decided: anyone who wants it presses Aviary's Unlock button.
- A job a later product adds joins this table and the jobs package below; the runner itself does not change.
- The lending AMM's spec says the runner acts when Aviary's indexer sees a market leave its band; the runner watches the chain itself instead (see "Triggers"), which gives the same result without tying it to Aviary.

### One definition of due

- Each job's due rule is a pure function of the market state in one shared package, `packages/keeper-jobs`, with the instruction builder for that job.
- The keeper runner and Aviary's panels both use it, so a button shows in Aviary exactly when the runner would act.
- Each product's package entry also names the refusal codes that mean "nothing to do" (for example the lending AMM's `WithinBand`, or a payout with nothing owed), which the runner treats as a skip, not a failure.
- A program that succeeds without effect when there is nothing to do, rather than refusing, says so in its entry instead: the tax AMM's `distribute` on a slot owed nothing succeeds and moves nothing ([`TAX-43`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#tax-43-which-tax-slots-distribute-pays)), so its entry has no "nothing to do" code and counts a simulation that emits no `Distributed` event as nothing to do ([`SUITE-50`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-50-keeper-runner-nothing-to-do-when-a-program-does-not-refuse)).
- It also names the refusal codes that mean "try again in a later slot", which the runner retries from the next slot, never counting them as a failure: the buy wall AMM's `SwapThisSlot`, which refuses `place_wall` in a slot a swap already ran in ([`POOL4-50`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-50-when-the-walls-floor-moves); a market with a swap in every slot can starve it, the Low residual R2-03 the owner signed off).

## Which markets

- Every market of our strategies on devnet, including markets other people create, within the spending caps.
- The runner finds them with `getProgramAccounts` on each of our strategy programs when it starts and in every 10-minute sweep, and adds a market as soon as a transaction names one it does not know.
- The per-market daily cap is what stops anyone from making us pay for many markets with fresh recipients (see "Spending caps").

## Triggers

- **Its own socket**: one `logsSubscribe` subscription per strategy program of ours, held open while the runner runs; a notification makes the runner fetch that transaction, find which of our markets it touched, re-read their market states and check `place_wall` and `rebalance`.
  The socket reconnects on its own, and every reconnect runs a sweep so nothing between is missed.
- **The 10-minute sweep**: re-reads every known market's state in batches of 100 with `getMultipleAccounts` and checks `place_wall` and `rebalance`; this also catches withdraw mode, which depends on Kamino's state rather than our market's.
- **The hourly pass**: `settle`, at most once every `SETTLE_INTERVAL` on each market, a restart included: the runner learns when each job of the hourly pass last ran on each market from the keeper wallet's own successful transactions of the last `SETTLE_INTERVAL`, each job known by its instruction's discriminator in `packages/keeper-jobs`, and holds it back in every pass until the interval is up ([`SUITE-56`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-56-keeper-runner-settle-at-most-hourly-across-a-restart)).
- **The daily pass** at `DAILY_PASS_UTC`: `pay_rewards`, `sweep_fees` and `distribute`.
- **On start**: one full pass of every job, since the Mac may have slept through any of the above; paying out again after a restart costs only transaction fees, because each payout pays the whole amount owed and the next one finds nothing.
- The runner reads only the chain; it never polls Aviary's database (see "What it records").

## RPC

- Alchemy's free devnet endpoint, from `ALCHEMY_API_KEY` in the owner's `~/.config/env/global.env`, so the runner's load stays off both Aviary's own Helius key (budgeted at about 500,000 of its 1 million free credits) and the owner's shared Helius key (already rate-limited when several sessions run).
- The HTTP and WebSocket URLs are the settings `KEEPER_RPC_URL` and `KEEPER_WS_URL`; their defaults are built from `ALCHEMY_API_KEY`.
- The first build ticket checks that Alchemy's devnet WebSocket serves `logsSubscribe`; if it does not, the socket uses Aviary's Helius key and HTTP stays on Alchemy, and the ticket records which.
- It does not: on 2026-11-20 ([the first build ticket](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/94)) Alchemy's free devnet WebSocket answered `logsSubscribe` with `Method 'logsSubscribe' not found`, and its free tier refuses `getProgramAccounts` too (`getProgramAccounts is not available on the Free tier`), which finding the markets needs.
  So the socket and market discovery go to Aviary's Helius key, once the project's `.env` has it as `RPC_URL` ([Aviary: owner setup](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/110)), and until then to Solana's public devnet endpoint, which serves both free and without a key; reads, simulations and sends stay on Alchemy ([`SUITE-49`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-49-keeper-runner-the-socket-and-discovery-off-alchemy)).
  Discovery has its own setting, `DISCOVERY_RPC_URL`, beside `RPC_URL` and `WS_URL`.
- No paid tier: if the free tier runs out, the runner slows its sweeps rather than spending.

## Sending a job

1. Build the job's transaction from `packages/keeper-jobs`, with the keeper wallet as fee payer and, for `place_wall`, the keeper wallet's wrapped-SOL account as the tip account (created in the same transaction if missing).
   A buy wall market's token never has a live transfer hook (the seed refuses one, `POOL4-48`), so its `pay_rewards` needs no hook accounts.
2. Simulate it.
   A "nothing to do" refusal is a skip and costs nothing; a "try again in a later slot" refusal is sent again from a later slot and costs nothing; any other simulation error counts as a failure (below).
   The same holds for a job that passed simulation and then lands refused with a "try again in a later slot" code, as `place_wall` does when a swap reaches the slot first: it costs that transaction's fee, is sent again from a later slot, and is not a failure.
3. Estimate its cost (the fee plus the rent of any account it creates) and check it against every cap; a job over a cap is held, not sent.
   The estimate is what the simulation takes from the keeper wallet: its balance before, less its balance in the simulation's result, which has the fee taken ([`SUITE-51`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-51-keeper-runner-what-a-job-costs)).
4. Send it at `PRIORITY_FEE_MICROLAMPORTS` (0 on devnet) and wait for confirmation.
- A payout that would create its recipient's token account waits until what it pays is worth that account's rent: the job's entry in `packages/keeper-jobs` gives the reason, the runner skips it at no cost and checks again in its next pass, and a payout into an account that exists goes whatever it pays; a buy wall market's rewards are valued at the market's price ([`SUITE-54`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-54-keeper-runner-a-payout-into-an-account-it-would-create)).
- One job is sent at a time, so two jobs never race each other or count the same cap headroom twice.
- Another keeper running the same job first is harmless: the second simulation finds nothing to do.

### Failures

- A failed job is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes and 10 minutes (`RETRY_DELAYS`).
- After the last retry the job is parked: the runner leaves that job on that market alone until the market's state changes, and records the park with the last error.
- Only the job's own failure counts: a simulation or a landed transaction refused with any code but a "nothing to do" or "try again in a later slot" one, or an instruction that cannot be built.
  When the RPC cannot be asked (a transport error, a timeout, a send that never lands before its blockhash expires) the job is not counted as failed and is due again in the next pass, so an RPC outage never parks a job that would succeed ([`SUITE-52`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-52-keeper-runner-when-the-rpc-fails)).
- A parked job still shows as due in Aviary, with its button, so anyone can press it.

### When the wallet runs low or a cap is reached

- Below `LOW_BALANCE` the runner keeps working and records a low-balance warning in every pass.
- Below `MIN_BALANCE`, or once a cap is reached, it sends no job (for the day, or for that market) and records why; Aviary's keeper page shows it.
  It still unwraps its tips, which lifts the balance (see "Keeper tips").
- The runner never funds itself.
  The keeper wallet is topped up only with `devnet-airdrop ~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/keeper.json --target 2`, run by the owner or an agent session in the background, as the owner's global rules say for every devnet wallet.

## The keeper wallet

- A new key made only for the runner, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/keeper.json`, by the first build ticket with `solana-keygen new`.
- It is not `wallet.json` (the deploy wallet) or `upgrade-authority.json`, so a leaked keeper key loses only its float and controls nothing.
- The key lives only in that file on the owner's Mac: never in the repo, the Docker image, a Worker, a GitHub secret or a log.
  The path is the setting `KEEPER_KEYPAIR`, so someone else's copy points at their own key; the Docker image takes it as a read-only mount.
- Its public address is published (here, and in Aviary's keeper page), so anyone can see what it spends: `8qTRTAXmbpVCFmKRNH5nkF2XGb1HpSDhjeqkyaqMvQC2`, made on 2026-11-20 by [the first build ticket](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/94).
- Its float is kept at `FLOAT_TARGET` (2 SOL) by `devnet-airdrop`.

### Keeper tips

- The buy wall AMM's `place_wall` is the only job that pays a keeper tip, into the keeper wallet's wrapped-SOL account.
- The runner keeps its tips: once that account holds more than `TIP_UNWRAP_AT`, the end of the pass closes the account to unwrap them into the float (the account's rent comes back too), and the next `place_wall` recreates it.
- No cap and not `MIN_BALANCE` hold the unwrap, since it returns far more than its fee; the fee still counts in today's spend ([`SUITE-55`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-55-keeper-runner-unwrapping-tips-under-the-caps)).
- `place_wall` pays for itself: at the lowest fee (0.25%) on the smallest work (`WALL_THRESHOLD`, 0.01 SOL) the tip is at least 25,000 lamports, five times the 5,000-lamport transaction fee.
- The other jobs pay no tip, so their fees and any recipient token accounts they create come out of the float.
- Caps count what the runner spends, never net of tips.

## Spending caps

All the runner's policy values live in one module, `apps/keeper/src/settings.ts`, each one overridable by an environment variable of the same name prefixed `KEEPER_`; no other file repeats a value.
The runner logs the values it started with.
A `KEEPER_` variable that names no setting stops the runner at start, so a misspelt override never leaves a default in force ([`SUITE-53`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-53-keeper-runner-a-misspelt-setting)).

| Setting | Default | What it limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FLOAT_TARGET` | 2 SOL | The balance `devnet-airdrop` tops the keeper wallet up to |
| `LOW_BALANCE` | 0.5 SOL | Below it, every pass records a low-balance warning |
| `MIN_BALANCE` | 0.1 SOL | Below it, the runner sends nothing |
| `MAX_TX_COST` | 0.003 SOL | The most one transaction may cost: the fee plus the rent of one new token account (2,039,280 lamports for a plain one) |
| `MARKET_DAILY_CAP` | 0.01 SOL | The most the runner spends on one market in a UTC day |
| `DAILY_CAP` | 0.1 SOL | The most the runner spends in a UTC day, all markets together |
| `PRIORITY_FEE_MICROLAMPORTS` | 0 | The priority fee on devnet |
| `TIP_UNWRAP_AT` | 0.05 SOL | The wrapped-SOL balance at which tips are unwrapped |
| `RETRY_DELAYS` | 30 s, 2 min, 10 min | The retries before a job is parked |
| `SWEEP_INTERVAL` | 10 min | How often every market is re-read |
| `SETTLE_INTERVAL` | 1 hour | How often `settle` may run per market |
| `DAILY_PASS_UTC` | 00:00 | When the daily pass runs |
| `KEEPER_KEYPAIR` | `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/keeper.json` | Where the key is read from |
| `RPC_URL` | Alchemy devnet, from `ALCHEMY_API_KEY` | The RPC the runner reads, simulates and sends through |
| `WS_URL`, `DISCOVERY_RPC_URL` | Aviary's Helius key (`RPC_URL` in the project's `.env`), else Solana's public devnet endpoint | The socket, and the `getProgramAccounts` that finds the markets, which Alchemy's free tier does not serve (see "RPC") |
| `DATABASE_URL` | unset | Aviary's database, where runs are recorded; unset, the runner only logs |

- A new market's first payouts may create up to five recipient token accounts (a tax market with four recipients and the suite share), about 0.0102 SOL, so on its first day the last one can wait for the next day's cap; that is accepted.
- What the runner has spent today is rebuilt from the chain whenever it starts: the keeper wallet's own transactions since 00:00 UTC (`getSignaturesForAddress`, then each one's fee and balance changes), per market from the accounts each one touched.
  A transaction's spend is what left the keeper wallet, and never less than its fee, so one that brings lamports back (unwrapping tips) still counts its fee; it is put to the first known market among its accounts.
  A sent job is counted the same way once it lands, so the spend the runner tracks and the spend a restart rebuilds are one sum ([`SUITE-51`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#suite-51-keeper-runner-what-a-job-costs)).
  So the runner keeps no state file, and a restart can never reset a cap.
  This holds because the keeper wallet is used by the runner alone.

## What it records

- The runner writes to Aviary's Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`, the Neon project `terminal-devnet`) directly, as the explainer's approve command does from the Mac, never through Aviary's public API.
- One table, `keeper_runs`, in Aviary's database package (`packages/terminal-db`): a row per pass (when, which pass, the keeper wallet's balance, today's spend against each cap, the settings it ran with, any warning) and a row per job it sent, held or parked (market, job, slot, signature, cost, outcome, error).
- It writes only in passes that sent, held or parked something, in one database transaction per pass.
  Neon's free plan gives 100 compute-hours a month, and the database must sleep while devnet is quiet; `place_wall`, `rebalance` and `settle` follow swaps, when Aviary's indexer has just woken the database anyway, and the daily pass wakes it once a day.
- Without `DATABASE_URL` (someone else's copy, or before Aviary's database exists) the runner logs the same rows to its log file and works the same.
- Logs go to `~/Library/Logs/testing-pipeline-keeper.log` on the Mac, and to standard output in Docker.

## How Aviary shows it

These are for Aviary's build tickets ([Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22)) and each product's Aviary panel ticket.
The `keeper_runs` table and the runner's writer for it belong to the Aviary ticket that builds the keeper page, since neither can be tested before Aviary's database exists; until then the runner only logs.

- Each market's panel shows every keeper job that is due, from `packages/keeper-jobs`, with how long it has been due, the runner's last attempt from `keeper_runs` (sent, held by a cap, or parked with its error) and a button that prepares and simulates the job for the viewer's own wallet, as any custom action.
- A keeper page shows the keeper wallet's address and balance (read through RPC), today's spend against each cap, the last pass of each kind, every held or parked job, and any warning; it is read-only and public, like the rest of Aviary.
- If the last pass is more than `SWEEP_INTERVAL` plus a few minutes old, the page says the runner looks stopped.

## Running it

- **On the owner's Mac**: a launchd agent, `testing-pipeline.keeper`, with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive`, started by a script in `scripts/` that loads `~/.config/env/global.env` and the project's `.env` (launchd has no direnv) and runs the built program on the Node version in `docs/toolchain.md`.
  `pnpm keeper:install` writes and loads the agent, `pnpm keeper:uninstall` removes it, and `pnpm keeper:status` prints the wallet's balance, today's spend and the last pass.
- **Anywhere else**: the Docker image built from `apps/keeper`, with the key mounted read-only and the settings as environment variables, documented in `apps/keeper/README.md`, which also lists the decisions here and invites MetalLegBob to change any of them.
- **One-off**: `pnpm keeper:once` runs one full pass and exits, for tests, demos and anyone who would rather press nothing in Aviary.
- On mainnet the runner would need its own hosting decision; that belongs to the mainnet effort, which is out of scope.

## Testing it

- Unit tests of every due rule in `packages/keeper-jobs` against market states from each product's fixtures, including the boundary values (exactly `WALL_THRESHOLD`, the band's edges, slot 1 with `DESIGNER_RECIPIENT` unset).
- Tests of the runner against a local validator running devnet's router and our programs (each product's local demo run), with a fake clock for the passes: a job sent when due and only then, a "nothing to do" refusal skipped at no cost, every cap holding a job, the spend rebuilt after a restart equal to the spend before it, a failing job retried and parked, and a second keeper racing the runner costing only a refused simulation.
- On devnet, for each product as its deploy ticket lands: the runner calling that product's jobs on its demo market, with the signatures in the PR.

## Build tickets

Cut by [Keeper runner](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/45) on 2026-11-10, labelled `build`, one session each, in run order:

1. [Keeper runner: the runner, its wallet and the tax AMM's `distribute`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/94): `apps/keeper`, `packages/keeper-jobs`, the keeper wallet, the caps, the launchd agent and the Docker image, after [Tax AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and create a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/66).
2. [Keeper runner: the buy wall AMM's four jobs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/95): with keeper tips, after the first and [Buy wall AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/56).
3. [Keeper runner: the lending AMM's `rebalance`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/96): after the first and [Lending AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/87).

Each waits for the product whose jobs it adds to be on devnet, so the runner is built against deployed programs; the second and third can run in either order.
Aviary's side (the `keeper_runs` table and its writer, due jobs on each panel, the keeper page) is left to [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22), where it is posted as a comment.

documents.title: Lending AMM
documents.body:
## What it is

- A Pipeline strategy whose markets are two-mint constant-product pools with open LP shares.
- One mint of each market is the lent side, WSOL or USDC; most of the lent side is lent to Kamino Lend through its cToken instructions, and a buffer stays in the market's own vault for swaps.
- Prices come from the market's total reserves: the other side's vault, and on the lent side the buffer plus the market's cTokens valued at Kamino's exchange rate.
- A swap that must pay out more of the lent side than the buffer holds redeems just the shortfall from Kamino in the same swap; a swap never deposits into Kamino.
- A permissionless keeper job, `rebalance`, moves the buffer back to its target when it drifts out of its band.
- The LP fee and all the lending yield go to LPs, through the value of their shares.
- The program has no admin: nobody, us included, can pause it, change a market or move a market to another reserve; it reacts to Kamino's own state.

## Not in v1

- Exact-out swaps.
- Lending both sides of a market, or any lent mint other than WSOL and USDC.
- Any lending market other than Kamino Lend: Jupiter Lend is out of scope for this map (see the map's Out of scope), and so are Kamino's obligations, which refuse calls from our program (`CpiDisabled`).
- Kamino withdrawal tickets: issuance is switched off on Kamino's main market (2026-11-09), so the program never enqueues one.
- A buffer target or band chosen per market.
- A share of the yield or the LP fee for us or for the market's creator.
- Markets with more than two mints.
- On-chain token metadata for LP mints.
- Mainnet: nothing deploys there before Pipeline's router does, and the program is frozen first (see "Upgrades and freezing").

## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BUFFER_TARGET_BPS` | 2000 (20%) | The buffer's target share of the lent side's total |
| `BUFFER_MIN_BPS`, `BUFFER_MAX_BPS` | 1000, 3000 | The band; `rebalance` acts only when the buffer's share is outside it |
| `MIN_REBALANCE` | 0.05 SOL (50,000,000 lamports) for WSOL, 5 USDC (5,000,000 base units) for USDC | Smaller moves are skipped |
| `KAMINO_RATE_HEADROOM_BPS` | 10 (0.1%) | Headroom `rebalance` leaves below Kamino's freely available liquidity and withdrawal cap when it plans a redeem, for the interest klend accrues when it refreshes the reserve inside the redeem (see "The rule") |
| `WITHDRAW_MODE_ENTER` | 5 | Enter withdraw mode when Kamino's freely available liquidity is below 5 times the larger of the market's lent value and its target lent value (see "Withdraw mode") |
| `WITHDRAW_MODE_EXIT` | 10 | Leave withdraw mode when it is back above 10 times that amount |
| `MAX_LP_FEE_BPS` | 200 (2%) | The highest LP fee a market may charge |
| `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` | 1,000 LP base units | Locked for good by the first deposit |
| `LP_DECIMALS` | 9 | Decimals of every market's LP mint |
| `KLEND_PROGRAM` | `KLend2g3cP87fffoy8q1mQqGKjrxjC8boSyAYavgmjD` | Kamino Lend, the same id on devnet and mainnet |
| `LENT_MINTS` | per cluster, below | The lent mints and the one Kamino reserve each lends to |

`LENT_MINTS`, selected at build time by a cluster feature (`devnet` or `mainnet`):

| Cluster | Lent mint | Lending market | Reserve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mainnet | WSOL `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` | Kamino main market `7u3HeHxYDLhnCoErrtycNokbQYbWGzLs6JSDqGAv5PfF` | SOL `d4A2prbA2whesmvHaL88BH6Ewn5N4bTSU2Ze8P6Bc4Q` |
| mainnet | USDC `EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v` | Kamino main market | USDC `D6q6wuQSrifJKZYpR1M8R4YawnLDtDsMmWM1NbBmgJ59` |
| devnet | WSOL `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` | Our own Kamino lending market `DCKrWS5G3YEcrRP1Ayu8S8nBR4QfgFsSaRzRdPrjqzj3` (see "Devnet") | WSOL `5vJJ1sQi972Qcf6oUy3gHEx6prijjSj31CWo5He85Hjw` |
| devnet | Our test USDC `CqHMaMB72rTsJGRDzeQmcAsVHuwoBw7V7gdaCexcjcC7`, 6 decimals | Our own Kamino lending market | Test USDC `72wAn7eQBbBSXQcb2eAMHz2SDxUgAM51LHhH3aGbY7T3` |

- Market creators never choose a reserve: a reserve in a lending market the creator owned could be reconfigured to let its owner borrow the LPs' deposits away.
- The devnet rows come from [`deployments/kamino-devnet.json`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/deployments/kamino-devnet.json), which also holds the lending market's authority and each reserve's liquidity supply, fee vault, collateral mint and collateral supply; the program's devnet constants must equal that file.
- The constants are compiled into the program; changing one is a program upgrade, which ends when the program is frozen.
- They live in one module, `programs/lending-amm/src/config.rs`, where each `LENT_MINTS` entry also names its reserve's lending market and collateral mint and its `MIN_REBALANCE`.
  The cluster is chosen by the crate's `devnet` or `mainnet` feature, exactly one of them; `devnet` is the default, since devnet is the only cluster this project deploys to, and CI builds both ([Lending AMM: markets that trade from their own vaults](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/78), 2026-11-12).

## Markets

### Shape

- Exactly two mints: the lent mint, which must be on the cluster's `LENT_MINTS` list, and the other mint.
- The mints must differ.
- If both mints are on the list (a SOL and USDC market), the creator's `lent_index` decides which one is lent, and the other is never lent.
  Such a market is allowed but pointless next to cheaper SOL and USDC venues, since every hop pays Pipeline's 0.25%.
- `pipeline_market_info` reports the mints in the order the creator gave them, with `supports_exact_out = false`.

### Mint rules

- The lent side is exactly the listed mint, owned by SPL Token.
- The other side follows the tax AMM's mint rules ([`tax-amm.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/tax-amm.md), "Mint rules"): SPL Token, or Token-2022 with only transfer hook, metadata pointer, token metadata, group pointer, group member pointer, token group and token group member extensions; transfer fees, permanent delegates and every other extension are refused at creation.
- So hooked tokens may trade in a lending AMM market.
  The hooked transfer and the Kamino redeem are sibling calls under the strategy and never stack: the deepest chain is the redeem, router (1), strategy (2), klend (3), SPL Token (4), or 5 when the trader uses a smart wallet, inside the limit of 5.
  A transfer hook that makes calls of its own fails for smart-wallet traders, as it does in any Pipeline market.
- A contained token can only trade in its home market until its unlock, and Kamino refuses hooked mints, so a contained token is never lent.

### Addresses

- The market state is the PDA `["market", other_mint, lent_mint, lp_fee_bps as u16 little-endian]` of the lending AMM program, so there is one market per pair, lent side and fee.
  Every creation parameter is in the seeds, so nobody can occupy a market's address with other parameters.
  Someone may create a market first at a bad price with dust liquidity; correcting that price by a swap costs little, and the locked minimum stops share inflation.
- Markets created through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` live at `["seeded", seeder, other_mint, lent_mint, lp_fee_bps]` instead, as Pipeline's guide asks, so nobody can create or price them first.
- The vault authority is the PDA `["authority", market_state]`, a data-less address that signs every transfer out of the vaults, owns the cToken account, signs Kamino calls as the depositor and is the LP mint's mint authority.
- Each vault is a token account at `["vault", market_state, mint]`, owned by the vault authority; the lent mint's vault holds the buffer.
- The cToken account is a token account at `["ctoken", market_state]` for the reserve's collateral mint, owned by the vault authority; each market holds its own cTokens.
- The LP mint is an SPL Token mint at `["lp_mint", market_state]`, with `LP_DECIMALS` decimals, the vault authority as mint authority and no freeze authority.
- The lock account is the vault authority's associated token account for the LP mint; no instruction ever moves LP shares out of it.
- An LP's shares account is a token account of the LP mint at `["lp_shares", market_state, lp]`, owned by the LP; `add_liquidity` mints the LP's shares into it and creates it, at the LP's expense, if it is missing.
