## Building it

- Generate the program from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template with `scripts/new-strategy.sh`, from a scratchpad clone at `5ad130d`, and pin the Pipeline crates to `rev = "5ad130d"`, as for the tax AMM.
- Keep the program keypair in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`, never in the repo.
- Put every Kamino call and read in one module (deposit, redeem, reserve checks, total supply, what Kamino can pay now, flags), so a later strategy version can add another lending market without touching the pool's maths.
- Write the Kamino instruction data, account lists and reserve offsets by hand from klend 1.28.0, and never depend on the klend crate: klend is BSL 1.1 with no use grant until 2027-11-17, so we call its deployed program but never compile its code into ours.
- Tests load klend's deployed program bytes with cloned mainnet reserve, lending market and mint accounts, as `docs/spec/README.md` (test layer 6) sets.
  A fixture script dumps the accounts once and commits them with the slot they were read at, since an RPC cannot serve an account's past state; it fetches klend's program bytes into a gitignored folder at each setup and checks them against a hash pinned in the repo, as the router's fixture does, so a Kamino upgrade fails the check and is re-pinned deliberately; klend's bytes are never committed.
- The fixtures, from [Lending AMM: klend fixtures, and valuing the lent side from Kamino's reserve](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/79) (2026-11-12): `programs/lending-amm/scripts/kamino_accounts.py dump` reads each reserve a cluster build lends to, its lending market (and its authority, when it holds an account), mints and token accounts in one `getMultipleAccounts` call, so all are as they were at one slot, into `programs/lending-amm/tests/fixtures/kamino/<cluster>/` with the slot and its time; its `check` dumps afresh and compares the layout (owners, sizes, discriminators, the addresses the reserve check compares, token accounts' mints and owners).
  `programs/lending-amm/scripts/fetch-klend.sh` fetches klend from mainnet and devnet into `fixtures/klend/`, refused unless each matches its hash in `fixtures/pins.env`, and its header says how to re-pin after a Kamino upgrade.
  The tests of each cluster build load that cluster's dump with the clock one slot past it, and klend's bytes wherever klend runs.
- Build and test with the toolchain in `docs/toolchain.md` (`source scripts/toolchain-env.sh`).

### Build tickets

Cut by [Cut the lending pool's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/25) on 2026-11-10, labelled `build`, one session each, in run order:

1. [Lending AMM: our Kamino lending market on devnet](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/77): the devnet script that creates our Kamino lending market, its two reserves and the test USDC mint, and proves the cToken path, a test borrower and emergency mode there; it needs no program of ours and can run first.
2. [Lending AMM: markets that trade from their own vaults](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/78): the program from the template, the market state's final layout, creation, the mint rules, adding liquidity and exact-in swaps, with nothing lent yet.
3. [Lending AMM: klend fixtures, and valuing the lent side from Kamino's reserve](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/79): the fixture script for both clusters, the reserve checks, and quotes, swaps and deposits priced from the buffer plus cTokens at the stored rate.
4. [Lending AMM: lend the surplus with `rebalance`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/80): the band, the target, the dust floor, and Kamino's deposit and redeem by CPI.
5. [Lending AMM: redeem a swap's shortfall from Kamino inside the swap](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/81): the in-swap redeem, the redeem accounts resolved only when needed, and the call-depth test with a smart-wallet stand-in and a hooked token.
6. [Lending AMM: remove liquidity in cash or in kind, and lock LP shares](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/82): `remove_liquidity` both ways, `lock_lp` and SPL burns of LP shares.
7. [Lending AMM: withdraw mode and Kamino's other states](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/83): withdraw mode as amended, every row of "When Kamino can't pay", and a falling rate from Kamino's real `socialize_loss`.
8. [Lending AMM: seeding by a launchpad](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/84): `pipeline_seed_liquidity` with a stand-in launchpad.
9. [Lending AMM: the fuzzer against a moving Kamino, and the proofs completed](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/85): the invariants checked while Kamino's rate and state move, the Kani and Z3 proofs completed, and the compute table measured.
10. [Lending AMM: hardening](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/86): the hardening ticket, before the first deploy, so the registered bytes are hardened and the layout freezes once.
11. [Lending AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/87): the end of the program's chain, with every check under "On devnet" below run on devnet itself.
12. [Lending AMM: Aviary panel, forms and explainer facts](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/88): after the deploy and Aviary's own build tickets.

The second waits for [Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/58), which sets up the on-chain workspace, CI, the fixtures, the keys, the local demo run and the review skills, and for [Tax AMM: create a tax market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/59), whose mint rules it shares.
Tickets 2 to 10 are verified end to end in LiteSVM through the real router copied from devnet and klend's deployed bytes, with the `mainnet` build on cloned mainnet reserves and the `devnet` build on accounts dumped from our devnet lending market; tickets 1 and 11 run on devnet itself, against the real Kamino Lend there.
Tickets 2 to 8 and the hardening ticket also pass a local demo run: the demo script, on Pipeline's TypeScript SDK, against a local validator running devnet's router and devnet's klend, with the accounts of our Kamino lending market cloned from devnet.
Ticket 11 points that same script at devnet.
The hardening ticket comes before the deploy, not last as `README.md` words it, so that what is registered with Pipeline is the hardened program.
The keeper runner is specified separately ([Keeper runner](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/45)); until it runs, the demo script and Aviary's form call `rebalance`.

### Done means

- LiteSVM tests through the real router and the real klend program cover:
  - pricing both ways at LP fees of 0, 30 and 200 bps, and quotes matching swaps on both sides of the buffer's edge;
  - an in-swap redeem: the shortfall, its rounding (the market receives at least the shortfall), and the excess staying in the buffer;
  - an in-swap redeem at one extra outer level (a smart-wallet stand-in program calling the router), with a hooked token (Pipeline's `test-hook`) on the other side;
  - a swap needing a redeem but built without the redeem accounts, failing cleanly;
  - Kamino states made by editing cloned account data: too little free liquidity, the withdrawal cap used up, reserve and market emergency mode, `block_ctoken_usage`, a deprecated reserve, and a reserve failing each part of the layout check, with quotes, swaps, `rebalance`, adding and removing behaving as in the table above;
  - a falling rate from Kamino's real `socialize_loss`, run on an edited obligation that has debt and no collateral, lowering LP share value pro rata;
  - `rebalance`: inside the band, above it, below it, the dust floor, entering and leaving withdraw mode, a market that has redeemed everything staying in withdraw mode until Kamino's free liquidity is back above the exit threshold, no first deposit into a reserve below the entry threshold, and deposits skipped under `block_ctoken_usage`;
  - LP shares: the first deposit and its locked minimum, an inflation attempt by donating to the vaults or the cToken account, adding at the ratio, removing in cash and in kind, locking, and an SPL burn;
  - seeding at the seeder-scoped address, shares to the LP recipient, and the vault authority as recipient locking them;
  - refusal of exact-out, of bypass, of every refused mint extension, and of a lent mint not on the list;
  - donations never credited.
- `pipeline-check` passes every check on a funded market (with `exact_out_refund` skipped), both in the tests and against devnet.
- On devnet:
  - our Kamino lending market created by script;
  - the program deployed and registered with the router's `register_strategy`, with its metadata and conformance report published;
  - one market created, funded, rebalanced into Kamino, and traded both ways through the router, including a sell beyond the buffer that redeems in the swap;
  - a test borrower raising utilisation until the market enters withdraw mode;
  - emergency mode turned on for our reserve, with swaps from the buffer only and an in-kind removal, then turned off again.
- Whatever else `docs/spec/README.md` requires of our on-chain programs.

documents.title: Aviary: architecture
documents.body:
Decided in [Pipescope architecture](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/13) with the owner on 2026-11-10.
It builds on the findings of [Where Pipescope's indexer gets its data](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/6) ([findings](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/research/indexer-data-source/research/indexer-data-source.md)), [Where the quoter runs for Canary checks](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/7) ([findings](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/research/quoter-hosting/research/quoter-hosting.md)), [Prior art for behavioural testing of Solana programs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/8), [Prior art for AI explanations of contracts, and what an explainer can safely say](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/9) and [How the containment hook works with the router and unlocks](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/10), and on the explainer spec in `pipescope-explainer.md`.
Patterns are copied from Top-pad at commit `b833a7b` (`Top-pad`, read only), whose devnet build runs on the same Cloudflare account.
[Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22) reconciled this file with the other Aviary spec files on 2026-11-12 and cut the build tickets listed under [Build tickets](#build-tickets); the files stay separate, one per topic, because the decision register and every product's tickets link into their sections (`PIPESCOPE-86`).

Decisions: [ADR 0003](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-pipescope-indexes-pipeline-itself.md) (our own indexer, not Pipeline's hosted API), [ADR 0004](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-postgres-on-neon-is-pipescopes-record.md) (Postgres on Neon is the only system of record), [ADR 0005](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-canary-checks-run-natively-in-a-container.md) (Canary checks run natively in a Cloudflare Container).

## Where each part runs

| Part | Runs on | Keeps its data in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web app | `terminal-web` Worker: Next.js 16 through OpenNext, a pure client of the API | Nothing of its own |
| API | `terminal-api` Worker: Hono with a zod contract | Postgres |
| Indexer | The `Indexer` Durable Object in `terminal-api`, one instance | Postgres; Durable Object storage only for its own socket and alarm state |
| Candle builder | Inside the indexer, folded per trade | Postgres |
| Live rooms | `LiveRoom` Durable Objects in `terminal-api`, one per market and one for the feed | Memory only |
| Metadata fetcher | `terminal-api`, on router events and an hourly cron | Postgres |
| Canary runner | `crates/canary`, a native Rust binary in a Cloudflare Container, driven by one `CanaryRun` Durable Object per strategy version | Postgres |
| Verified builds | A GitHub Actions workflow in this repo, started and read by `terminal-api` | Postgres |
| Explainer | Evidence built by `terminal-api`; generation by `pnpm explainer:approve` on the owner's Mac | Postgres |

- Aviary holds no private keys at all: traders sign in their own wallets, the integrator fee goes to a fee wallet Aviary knows only by address, the Canary runner signs with throwaway keys inside its simulated chain, and the LLM key never leaves the owner's Mac.
- Pipeline's hosted devnet API serves none of the pages: the feed, charts and wallet page read our own indexer's data ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-pipescope-indexes-pipeline-itself.md)).
- Nothing paid runs from Cloudflare: the only paid call, the explainer's, runs on the owner's Mac when the owner approves it.

## Platform and plans

- Everything runs on the owner's existing Cloudflare account, beside Top-pad's devnet build.
- **Workers Paid is already active; nothing is bought.**
  Checked 2026-11-09: the account runs Top-pad's vision service as a Cloudflare Container (`top-pad-api-devnet-vision-devnet`, created 2026-11-02, healthy), and Containers run only on Workers Paid.
  The billing API refused the token (403), so the plan was not read from billing itself.
- Aviary shares the account's monthly allowances with Top-pad, so both stay inside them by design:

| Allowance (Workers Paid, per account per month) | Top-pad's devnet build | Aviary | Overage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Durable Object duration, 400,000 GB-s | Its always-awake indexer, about 10,300 GB-s a day measured 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-09, so about 310,000 | Its indexer only while someone watches (see Indexer), Canary runs about 8,300, live rooms hibernate | None expected; an always-awake second indexer would have added about 324,000 and gone over (about $3, or $12.50 if the overage rounds up to a whole million GB-s) |
| Container memory, 25 GiB-hours | Vision, up to about 50 minutes a day | Canary, about 20 GiB-hours for four sweeps a day (`pipescope-canary.md`), plus re-runs of new markets | At worst a few GiB-hours over, cents |
| Container vCPU, 375 minutes; disk, 200 GB-hours | Small | About 90 vCPU-minutes and under 100 GB-hours | None |
| Workers requests, 10 million; CPU, 30 million ms | Small | Small at devnet volume | None |

- Prices and allowances: the owner's Cloudflare knowledge base, `build/01-compute.md` (Durable Objects pricing as of 2026-10-05; Containers pricing), from https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/ and https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/.
- **Database**: a new Neon project on the free plan, `terminal-devnet`, separate from Top-pad's (see Data).
- **RPC**: Aviary's own free Helius key, separate from the owner's shared key, which Top-pad and every agent session use and which is already rate-limited when several sessions run at once.
  It is kept in the project's `.env` as `RPC_URL` (the Helius devnet URL carrying the key) and as the Worker secret `RPC_URL`, as Top-pad does.
  Expected use is about 400,000 credits a month for the indexer, about 53,000 requests for Canary's sweeps and some thousands for re-runs of new markets, trade-box quotes and pre-signature simulations, about 500,000 credits in all, inside the free plan's 1 million.
- **GitHub Actions**: verified builds run on GitHub's free minutes (2,000 a month while the repo is private, unlimited on standard runners once it is public).
- **LLM**: the explainer's model (`EXPLAINER-18`) through the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the owner's `~/.config/env/global.env`, one approved batch at a time (`pipescope-explainer.md`, Model and cost).
- Nothing else is paid. The paid upgrades for mainnet (a dedicated Helius plan with LaserStream, a paid Neon plan if compute runs out) belong to the mainnet effort.

## Pipeline's packages

Pipeline published its TypeScript SDK and its Rust crates on 2026-11-10 (commit `5ac3121`, release 0.1.0; 0.1.1 followed on 2026-11-11 with the `checks-*` and `conformance-stale` flags), all under Apache-2.0 (`PIPESCOPE-87`).

- The web app, `terminal-api`, the indexer, the explainer package and the Telegram package use `@pipeline-sol/sdk` from npm, at one exact version in the pnpm catalog of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the one place the terminal's TypeScript pins Pipeline.
  Nothing of the terminal links to a clone of Pipeline's repo.
- `crates/canary` uses `pipeline-check`, `pipeline-quoter`, `pipeline-client` and `pipeline-strategy-interface` from crates.io, at exact (`=`) versions in the `[workspace.dependencies]` of `crates/Cargo.toml`, the one place the terminal's Rust pins Pipeline.
  `crates/` is its own Cargo workspace, apart from the on-chain workspace in `programs/`, so a native dependency of Canary's can never change a program's bytes ([`README.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/README.md), Framework and toolchain).
- The router's program is never a package and never copied: Canary and the tests load the router's deployed bytes.
- A move to a newer Pipeline release is a PR of its own that moves both pins together and re-runs the parity checks.

## The two Workers

### `terminal-api`

- Hono with a zod contract, `nodejs_compat` and `global_fetch_strictly_public`, observability on, and `version_metadata` bound so the indexer can tell when the Worker calling it runs a newer version (Top-pad's lesson below).
- Durable Objects, all SQLite-backed: `Indexer`, `LiveRoom`, `CanaryRun`, and `CanaryContainer` (the Container's class).
- One Container: `crates/canary`'s image, instance type `basic` (a quarter of a vCPU, 1 GiB, 4 GB of disk), `max_instances` 1.
- Hyperdrive in front of Neon, with its query cache off.
- A rate-limiting binding for the public API (see API).
- One cron, every minute, which runs whatever is due by the intervals in the config module ([One place for every value](#one-place-for-every-value)): the indexer's reconciliation, ProgramData watch and registry snapshot, polling running verified builds, the hourly metadata re-fetch and Canary's scheduled sweep ([`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md), When Canary runs).
  So no interval is written in `wrangler.jsonc`, and changing one is a change to one constant.
- Secrets: `RPC_URL`, and `GH_ACTIONS_TOKEN`, a fine-grained GitHub token limited to this repo with Actions read and write and nothing else, for verified builds.
- A KV namespace, `TERMINAL_CACHE`, for public caches and for the copies of token images ([Data](#data)).
- No LLM key, no wallet key and no Secrets Store binding.

### `terminal-web`

- Next.js 16 on Workers through OpenNext, a pure client of the API, built per environment because `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is baked in at build time.
- Wallets through Wallet Standard on `@solana/kit` (Top-pad's `WalletProvider`), charts with TradingView Lightweight Charts v5, live updates over the live rooms' WebSockets.
- What the pages are is settled by [Pipescope v1 scope](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/3) and [Pipescope screens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/16).

## Data

[ADR 0004](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-postgres-on-neon-is-pipescopes-record.md).

- Postgres on Neon is the only system of record, through Drizzle, reached by the Workers through Hyperdrive with its query cache off (Hyperdrive never invalidates a cached read when a write lands, and the indexer, the Canary runner and the explainer must read what was just written).
- What it holds, as tables for the build to name: strategies; strategy versions (program id, ProgramData slot, `executable_sha256`, when seen); markets and their mints; indexed transactions; trades (keyed by signature and event index, with slot and in-block position); candles; indexer cursors; metadata snapshots (URI, fetch time, outcome, hash, normalised document); Canary runs and one record per check; verified-build requests and results; explanation keys with their stored evidence, estimated cost and status; explanations; reports from the "This is wrong" control; each strategy version's instruction list; token image records; the keeper runner's `keeper_runs` ([`keeper-runner.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/keeper-runner.md), What it records); and the Telegram bot's chats, watch lists, alerts and deliveries ([`pipescope-telegram.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-telegram.md), What the bot stores).
- Durable Object storage holds only the indexer's socket and alarm state and the Canary run's progress.
- KV holds public caches up to 60 s stale, and the copies of token images, keyed by the SHA-256 of their bytes (`PIPESCOPE-88`): Postgres records, per mint, the image's URI, hash, type, size and fetch outcome, and KV holds only bytes that a re-fetch could replace, so Postgres stays the only record ([ADR 0004](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-postgres-on-neon-is-pipescopes-record.md)).
  Serving an image never wakes the database: the page gets the hash with the mint, and `terminal-api` serves `/images/<hash>` from KV.
  KV is already in the architecture and inside the account's allowance (devnet holds a few dozen images of at most 1 MB), so nothing new is bought or added.
- D1 and R2 are not used.
- The free plan gives 100 compute-hours a project a month, so the database must sleep when devnet is quiet: reconciliation asks the chain first and touches the database only when there is something new, as Top-pad's does.
- Local development uses a Docker Postgres, as Top-pad's `docker-compose.yml` does.

## Indexer

[ADR 0003](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-pipescope-indexes-pipeline-itself.md).
The design is the recommendation of [Where Pipescope's indexer gets its data](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/6), ported from Top-pad's indexer.

- **What it watches**: the router and every registered strategy program; a strategy joins the watched list when its `StrategyRegistered` event arrives or the registry snapshot finds it.
  Watching the strategy programs is what shows custom actions, bypass swaps and upgrades, none of which the router reports.
- **Live source, only while someone watches**: one standard `logsSubscribe` socket on Helius devnet, holding a subscription per watched program, open only while at least one browser is connected to a live room, and closed a few minutes after the last one leaves.
  An outbound socket cannot hibernate and keeps the object billed, so an always-open socket would push the account past its Durable Object allowance (see Platform and plans).
  While the socket is open, a 15 s alarm reopens it if it drops; when it opens, a reconciliation runs at once, so nothing between the last cron run and the socket is missed.
- **Every reported transaction** is fetched whole (`getTransaction`), because swap events are inner instructions, not log lines, and decoded with Pipeline's TypeScript SDK (`extractEventsFromInnerInstructions`); its position in the block comes from `getBlock`, or from `transactionIndex` when `getTransactionsForAddress` served it.
- **Reconciliation** from a cursor per watched address, every minute for the router and every five minutes for strategy programs, oldest first, stopping at the first transaction it cannot fetch yet so the cursor never passes an unindexed one (Top-pad's `reconcileAccount`), through `getTransactionsForAddress` while the free key gets it, else `getSignaturesForAddress` plus `getTransaction`, behind one history-source interface.
- **Registry snapshot** every 10 minutes: `getProgramAccounts` on the router for `Strategy` and `Market` accounts; any account not yet indexed is a missed event and is indexed from its account.
- **ProgramData watch** every minute: one `getMultipleAccounts` with a 45-byte `dataSlice` per 100 programs reads each strategy's and the router's last-deploy slot.
  A changed slot on a strategy is a new strategy version: it is recorded, a Canary run of all its markets starts, a verified build is requested if a source lead exists, and the strategy's markets are re-read.
  A changed slot on the router is recorded and flagged, and starts a Canary run of every market, since a router upgrade can change event layouts; events the decoder does not know are kept and indexed again by newer code.
- **New markets**: each `MarketCreated`, and each market the registry snapshot finds, starts that market's Canary runs on the schedule of [`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md), When Canary runs.
- **Strategy-program calls**: every instruction the indexer sees on a strategy program is stored with its caller, which Canary's `custom_instructions` result reads as who has called each instruction.
- **Instruction lists**: when a strategy version is recorded, `terminal-api` reads its program's bytes once and stores the instructions compiled into it, as [`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md) (Custom instructions are listed, not called) defines them; the facts panel, the forms' instruction check, the explainer's F items and Canary's snapshot all read that one list (`PIPESCOPE-92`).
- **Market accounts**: after each event or custom action that touches a market, its market state and vaults are re-read; there are no account subscriptions.
- **Mints**: when a market brings a mint not yet seen, its mint account and on-chain token metadata are read once and stored, for the facts (Pipeline's trust flags) and for symbols and images, which `pipescope.md` treats as untrusted.
- **Unknown or failed decodes** are kept with the transaction, and re-indexing transactions first indexed by older code is Top-pad's `reindexTransactions`.
- **Deploys**: an object kept awake goes on running the code from before a deploy, so the indexer resets itself whenever the Worker calling it runs another version (Top-pad's `wake`).
- **Backfill**: the router's whole history (185 transactions on 2026-11-09) is indexed as soon as the indexer first runs, because devnet history may be reset and Postgres must be the record.
- **Trades made through Aviary** reach the indexer at once through the trade fast path (see Trading path); other people's trades show live while anyone is watching, and within a minute otherwise.
- **Parity checks**: Pipeline's hosted devnet API (`https://pipeline-devnet.up.railway.app`, `docs/API.md` in Pipeline's repo) is a test oracle, never a source ([ADR 0003](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-pipescope-indexes-pipeline-itself.md)), and the devnet tests lean on it wherever it answers the same question (`PIPESCOPE-93`):
  - trades, per market and per trader, equal its `/v1/markets/{market}/trades` and `/v1/traders/{address}/trades`;
  - candles, for the lengths it serves, equal its `/v1/markets/{market}/candles` for the same base and quote;
  - the trust flags of every strategy, market and mint equal its `flags`, apart from `checks-passed`, `checks-failed` and `checks-pending`, which record its own `pipeline-check` runs; Aviary shows its own Canary `conformance` result instead, and a test checks the two agree for the same code hash;
  - a quote equals its `/v1/quote` for the same market, mints, amount and integrator fee;
  - a prepared swap of an unhooked mint carries the same router instruction as its `POST /v1/swap-transaction`; for a hooked input mint, which it refuses, our own hook accounts are checked against the mint's `ExtraAccountMetaList` instead.
- **Restart test**: Top-pad's pattern (`tests/devnet/src/indexer-restart.test.ts`): stop the indexer, make swaps with this project's devnet keys (`~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`), restart it, and check the indexed trades equal the swaps decoded from the chain.

### Candles

- Each trade is folded into its candle at every length the config module lists as it is indexed, by trade order (slot, in-block position, event index) rather than arrival, the same fold a rebuild makes (Top-pad's `candles.ts`); any candle can be rebuilt from trades.
- Candles are kept per market and mint pair, since a market has two to four mints; a trade's price is `received / net_sent` for its pair (Pipeline's integrator guide); which mint of a pair is shown as the quote is for Aviary's v1 scope and screens.
- Lengths and retention as Top-pad's, kept in the config module (`PIPESCOPE-30`): 1 s, 15 s, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m, 1 h, 4 h and 1 d; 1 s candles kept 7 days, 15 s candles 30 days, coarser ones and all trades forever.
- The API returns `quote_mint` and `base_mint` with every market, candle series and trade, from the quote mint order in the config module ([`pipescope-screens.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-screens.md), Price direction).

### Live rooms

- One `LiveRoom` Durable Object per market and one for the feed, holding hibernatable browser WebSockets, so they cost no duration while idle; the indexer publishes each decoded trade, new market and new strategy version to its room, and rooms batch at the interval in the config module, 100 ms (`PIPESCOPE-31`).
- A reconnecting browser resyncs from its last slot through the API.
- The rooms tell the indexer when the first viewer arrives and when the last one leaves, which opens and closes its socket.

## API

- **Public** (owner, 2026-11-10): the read endpoints and the prepare endpoints are open to anyone, with no key and any origin, behind a per-IP limit from the Workers rate-limiting binding, and labelled unstable until v1 ships, so other builders can use Aviary's data.
- **Rate limits** (`PIPESCOPE-90`), per IP, in the rate-limiting bindings of `terminal-api`'s `wrangler.jsonc`, their one place: 300 reads a minute; 60 a minute for quotes, prepares and trade signatures together; 10 "This is wrong" reports a minute.
  A page view of the feed or a market makes about ten reads, and a quote is asked at most once per pause in typing, so a reader never meets them; an answer over the limit is a 429 that names the wait, and the page says so in the panel that asked.
  This is also where Canary results get their "page and API" in the map's Canary attestations fog.
- Endpoints, as a sketch for the build to settle in the zod contract:
  - strategies, a strategy's versions, and per version its facts, Canary results, verified-build status and explanation;
  - markets, a market's facts, trades and candles, with the feed's filters (liquidity, volume, age and Pipeline's trust flags);
  - search by name, mint, market address or strategy address, from Postgres;
  - a wallet's swaps through Pipeline, from our trades, and its balances in mints that trade in Pipeline markets, read through RPC;
  - a quote while the trader types;
  - `POST` prepare for a swap, a custom action and a new market, each returning the unsigned transaction with its simulation's outcome and balance changes;
  - `POST` a trade's signature (the fast path);
  - `POST` a "This is wrong" report against an explanation key.
- Owner-only operations are not in the API: the explainer's approve command and the reports list read and write Postgres directly from the owner's Mac.

## Trading path

Top-pad's flow (`apps/web/src/components/coin/QuickTrade.tsx`, `prepareSwap` then `signAndSendTransaction` then `reportTrade`), with what `pipescope.md` asks for.

1. While the trader types, the trade box shows a quote from RPC simulation of the strategy's `pipeline_quote` through the SDK's `quoteStrategy` (50 to 300 ms), asked through the API on Aviary's Helius key; the Container quoter is never on the trading path.
2. When the trader asks to swap, the API prepares the unsigned transaction with Pipeline's Kit-based TypeScript SDK: the router `swap` instruction, our integrator fee at the rate on screen when the input is a fee mint, the transfer-hook extra accounts, wrapping and unwrapping SOL, idempotent creation of the trader's token accounts, and the market's `init_fee_account` when a sell needs it.
3. The API simulates that exact transaction (see Simulation before every signature) and returns it with the simulation's outcome; if the simulation failed, the page shows the error and the sign button stays off.
4. The wallet signs and sends through Wallet Standard's `signAndSendTransaction`.
5. The page sends the signature to the API, which waits for it to confirm (asking every 300 ms), reads it back, answers with the trade and a provisional order key, and hands it to the indexer, which later replaces it in place.

- Transfer-hook extra accounts are resolved by our own code for buys, sells and sweeps, from each mint's `ExtraAccountMetaList`, because neither Pipeline's SDK nor its Rust client does it ([How the containment hook works with the router and unlocks](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/10)).
- Custom actions and market creation are prepared and simulated the same way, with the SDK's generic builders (`buildActionInstruction`, `buildCreateMarketFromMetadata`) from the strategy's validated metadata after the discriminator check; a custom action is signed directly on the strategy, outside the router's protections.

### Simulation before every signature

- Every transaction Aviary prepares (swap, custom action, create market) is simulated by `terminal-api` in the same request that builds it, with `simulateTransaction` on Aviary's Helius key, the trader's wallet as fee payer, signature checks off and the blockhash replaced.
- The simulation is asked for the post-state of every token account the transaction touches; with their balances read just before, the API returns the wallet's balance changes, which the form shows before signing (`pipescope.md`, Custom-action and create-market forms).
- The transaction returned is exactly the one simulated, so what the trader signs is what was checked, apart from the chain moving in between.

### The integrator fee's configuration

- The rate ([`pipescope.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope.md), The integrator fee), the fee mints (wrapped SOL and the cluster's USDC mint) and the fee wallet's two token accounts are vars of `terminal-api` per environment in its `wrangler.jsonc`, so they change by a configuration deploy, with no code change; the fee wallet's key is never on a server ([`pipescope.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope.md), The integrator fee).
- The API returns the rate it built each swap with, so the trade box shows exactly that rate.
- Pipeline's own fee is the router's setting, not ours: `terminal-api` reads it from the router's config account (cached up to 60 s) and returns it with every quote and on the fees endpoint, so the trade box, the Fees page, the Telegram bot and Canary's cost split never write it as a number (`PIPESCOPE-91`).

## Canary runner

[ADR 0005](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-canary-checks-run-natively-in-a-container.md).
The hosting is the recommendation of [Where the quoter runs for Canary checks](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/7).
What the checks are, how a run copies a market and when runs happen are in [`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md), from [Canary checks on the four devnet strategies](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/14); this section says where Canary runs and where its results go.

- **Binary**: `crates/canary` in the root Rust workspace, a native Rust program on `litesvm` (0.18.2) and Pipeline's Apache-2.0 crates at a pinned commit through Cargo (`pipeline-check`, `pipeline-quoter`, `pipeline-client` and `pipeline-strategy-interface`), never copied into this repo; Rust per `docs/toolchain.md`.
  It serves one HTTP endpoint that takes one market's snapshot and returns one Canary result per check, or the addresses of accounts the snapshot lacks.
- **Image and instance**: linux/amd64, which keeps the sBPF JIT measured on x86_64; a `basic` instance, one at a time, sleeping 2 minutes after its last run; internet access off (`enableInternet = false`), so the container never holds an RPC key and never reaches the network.
  The build measures a sweep on `basic` before trusting the cost below, and whether a shorter sleep or the `lite` instance (1/16 vCPU, 256 MiB) serves as well.
- **Orchestration**: one `CanaryRun` Durable Object per strategy version, keyed by program id and ProgramData slot, which runs that version on all of its markets or on one of them.
  For each market it builds the snapshot through Helius, posts it to the single `CanaryContainer`, fetches any accounts the binary names as missing and posts again, at most four times, stores the results in Postgres, and retries on its alarm if the container restarts mid-run.
  Its triggers are those of [`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md), When Canary runs, the one place that states them; a manual re-run command is part of the build.
- **Snapshot**: per market, the router's and the strategy's ProgramData, the router config, the market with its market state, mints, vaults and fee accounts, whatever `pipeline_resolve_accounts` asks for, and the cluster's slot, epoch and time; about 7 RPC requests a market (442 for all 61 devnet markets on 2026-11-10).
  The router is loaded from its deployed bytes, never a local build, so checks test what is on chain.
- **Results**: one Canary result per check, market, strategy version and slot, kept as `pipescope-canary.md` says (the latest of each check per market and version, and every earlier one whose outcome differed from the next); the facts panel and the explainer read them as C items, and changed outcomes make a new explanation key.
- **Cost**: four sweeps a day are about 960 runs a month and about 53,000 RPC requests; if each sweep keeps the container awake about ten minutes, that is about 20 GiB-hours of the 25 included, and re-runs of new markets add their 2-minute sleeps (`pipescope-canary.md`, When Canary runs).
  With Top-pad's vision service (about 10 GiB-hours a month at its pace since 2026-11-01), the account may go a few GiB-hours over, a few cents a month.
- **Fallback**: a small server elsewhere (Fly.io from $2.19 a month) runs the same binary if Containers misbehave; it is not built unless needed.

## Verified builds

- A strategy version's source counts as evidence (S items) only when Aviary rebuilt it from a named repository and commit and got the deployed bytes; OtterSec's hosted check does not cover devnet (empty hashes for all four devnet strategies on 2026-11-09; Top-pad found it runs on mainnet only), so Aviary runs `solana-verify` itself.
- **Leads**: the strategy metadata's `source` (repository, commit, path) and any on-chain verification record left by `solana-verify verify-from-repo`; neither is evidence until the hashes match.
- **Where**: a GitHub Actions workflow in this repo, `verify-build.yml`, started by `terminal-api` with `workflow_dispatch` for a strategy version with a lead, and read back by the every-minute cron through the run's status and its result artifact, with `GH_ACTIONS_TOKEN`.
- **Two jobs**:
  1. `build`, untrusted: no secrets, a token with no permissions, `solana-verify build` in its Docker image at the named commit, with dependencies fetched first and the build run with the network off where `solana-verify` allows it; it uploads the built program.
  2. `compare`, trusted, on a fresh runner: hashes the uploaded program, reads the on-chain executable hash at the version's slot, and uploads the result.
- **Known limit**: a hostile build script can still emit the deployed bytes, so a match shows the repository's build produced them, not that the visible source alone did; OtterSec's check has the same limit, and a verified source is evidence, never proof.
- Our own strategies are deployed only from verified builds and verified on chain at deploy, as in Top-pad (its `CLAUDE.md`).

## Metadata fetcher

- Runs in `terminal-api` on `StrategyRegistered`, on `MetadataUpdated`, and every hour, because the document behind an unchanged URI can change with no event.
- Limits, in the config module (`PIPESCOPE-36`): `https:` only, at most 64 KB, a JSON content type, a 5 s timeout, at most 3 redirects, each `https:`; it never fetches a URL found inside the document.
- The same fetcher, under the same limits apart from the size, fetches the image a mint's on-chain token metadata names, once per URI and again when the URI changes, and keeps it only as [`pipescope-screens.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-screens.md) (Token names and images) allows.
- The document is validated with Pipeline's `parse_strategy_metadata` (the TypeScript SDK's port), giving the `metadata-missing`, `metadata-unreachable` or `metadata-invalid` fact, then normalised as `pipescope-explainer.md` says, and stored with its hash.
- A changed hash is a metadata change: it makes a new explanation key, pending approval.
- Everything works with no metadata at all, as on devnet today, where all four strategies' metadata links returned 404 on 2026-11-09.

## Explainer jobs

What the explainer is, its key, prompt, validator and presentation are in `pipescope-explainer.md`; this is where its parts run.

- When a new key arises (a new strategy version, a metadata change, changed Canary outcomes, or a new prompt or model version), `terminal-api` builds the evidence input: P items from constant text, F items with Pipeline's trust facts from the TypeScript SDK, C items from the Canary records, S items from the verified source at its commit, and A items from the normalised metadata.
  It stores the input with the key, its estimated cost and the status pending.
- `pnpm explainer:approve`, run by the owner on their Mac, lists the pending keys with their estimated cost; for the keys the owner approves it calls the model named in the explainer's rules module ([`pipescope-explainer.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-explainer.md), One place for every value) with the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `~/.config/env/global.env`, runs the validator, retries once with the validator's errors, writes the explanation or the failed status to Postgres through the project's database URL, and appends one line per batch to `~/.config/spend/ledger.csv`.
- No LLM key is in Cloudflare, so nothing paid can run from the deployed product, whatever its code does.
- `pnpm explainer:reports` lists the "This is wrong" reports with the keys they refer to.
- Until a key's explanation exists, the strategy page shows the facts panel alone, with "No explanation for this version yet."

## One place for every value

`terminal-api`'s config module, `apps/terminal-api/src/config.ts`, holds every policy value of the API, the indexer and the jobs that is not a per-environment var (`PIPESCOPE-89`).
Each is a named constant; the pages and the Telegram bot read what they show from the API and never repeat it.

| Value | Default | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reconciliation: router, strategy programs | every minute, every 5 minutes | `PIPESCOPE-28` |
| Registry snapshot, ProgramData watch | every 10 minutes, every minute | `PIPESCOPE-28` |
| Socket: reopen alarm, close after the last viewer | 15 s, 3 minutes | `PIPESCOPE-27`, `PIPESCOPE-28` |
| Candle lengths and retention | as [Candles](#candles) | `PIPESCOPE-30` |
| Live-room batching | 100 ms | `PIPESCOPE-31` |
| Fast path: confirmation poll | every 300 ms | `PIPESCOPE-33` |
| Metadata fetcher limits and re-fetch interval | as [Metadata fetcher](#metadata-fetcher), every hour | `PIPESCOPE-36` |
| Quote mint order | wrapped SOL, then the cluster's USDC, then the later mint of the pair | `PIPESCOPE-74` |
| Token image types and size | PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 1 MB | `PIPESCOPE-82` |
| Canary's schedule | as [`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md), When Canary runs | `CANARY-22`, `CANARY-23` |
| Public caches | up to 60 s stale | `PIPESCOPE-32` |

- Per-environment values are vars or bindings in `terminal-api`'s `wrangler.jsonc`: the integrator fee's settings (`PIPESCOPE-13`), the rate limits (`PIPESCOPE-90`) and the Telegram bot's handles and origin (`PIPESCOPE-62`).
- The web app's own values are in its screens' config module, theme stylesheet and brand module ([`pipescope-screens.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-screens.md), One place for every value); Canary's are in `crates/canary/src/config.rs` ([`pipescope-canary.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md), One place for every value); the explainer's in `packages/terminal-explainer/src/rules.ts`; the bot's in `packages/terminal-telegram`'s config module.

## Copied from Top-pad

Each copied file starts with a header naming Top-pad commit `b833a7b` and its path there; once copied, it is owned here.

| From Top-pad | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/indexer/src/index.ts` (`indexTransactions`, `reindexTransactions`, `reconcileAccount`, the history source) | `packages/terminal-indexer`, with Pipeline's decoder in place of Meteora's |
| `packages/indexer/src/live.ts` (`logsSubscribeRequest`, `parseLogsMessage`, `blockPositions`) | `packages/terminal-indexer` |
| `packages/indexer/src/candles.ts` | `packages/terminal-indexer`, per market and mint pair |
| `apps/api/src/indexer.ts` (the Indexer Durable Object: socket, alarm, reconciliation, version reset) | `apps/terminal-api`, without Heat's graduated pools, Bundle Radar and keeper starts, and with the viewer-gated socket |
| The live rooms (Top-pad `docs/spec.md` section 10.2) | `apps/terminal-api` |
| `packages/db` (Drizzle, migrations; `0000_init.sql` and `0002_indexer.sql` as the pattern) and `docker-compose.yml` | `packages/terminal-db` |
| The API Worker's scaffold (`apps/api/wrangler.jsonc`, Hono with a zod contract, environments) | `apps/terminal-api` |
| `apps/api/src/visionContainer.ts` (a Container behind a Durable Object that sleeps when idle) | `apps/terminal-api`'s `CanaryContainer` |
| The web scaffold (`apps/web/open-next.config.ts`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `WalletProvider.tsx`, Lightweight Charts v5 use) | `apps/terminal-web` |
| `tests/ui` (Playwright) | `tests/terminal-e2e` |
| `tests/devnet/src/indexer-restart.test.ts` | `tests/devnet` |

- Not copied: Top-pad's Codama clients (Aviary calls none of our programs, and Pipeline's SDK is already on Kit; Codama comes with our strategies' build tickets), its keeper Workflows, the vision service, Heat's decoders and anything of Heat's devnet bank.

## Repo layout

- `apps/terminal-api`, `apps/terminal-web`
- `packages/terminal-db`, `packages/terminal-indexer`, `packages/terminal-explainer` (the prompt, its rules module, the normaliser and the validator, shared by `terminal-api` and the approve command), `packages/terminal-telegram`
- `crates/canary`, in its own Cargo workspace, `crates/Cargo.toml` ([Pipeline's packages](#pipelines-packages))
- `tests/terminal-e2e` (Playwright), `tests/devnet` (the restart test and the parity checks)
- `.github/workflows/verify-build.yml`
- Each joins the root pnpm workspace or, for Rust, `crates/`; none is built by the on-chain CI jobs, and CI gets a terminal job of its own behind the same `gate` check.

## Environments

- **Local**: `wrangler dev` for both Workers against devnet, with the Docker Postgres and `RPC_URL` from the project's `.env`.
- **Devnet**: `terminal-api-devnet` and `terminal-web-devnet` on `workers.dev`, deployed together by one root script; secrets set with `wrangler secret put --env devnet`.

## Owner tasks before the build

1. Make Aviary's own free Helius key (a second free Helius project or account; whether one account can hold a second free project was not confirmed, since Helius's docs could not be fetched on 2026-11-09) and put its devnet URL in the project's `.env` as `RPC_URL`.
2. Create the Neon project `terminal-devnet` on the free plan and put its connection string in the project's `.env` as `DATABASE_URL`.
3. Create a fine-grained GitHub token for this repo with Actions read and write only, for the verified-build workflow; the build session sets it as `GH_ACTIONS_TOKEN`.
4. Approve the explainer's first paid run, as `pipescope-explainer.md` says.

Nothing is purchased: Workers Paid is already active.

## Build tickets

Cut by [Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22) on 2026-11-12, labelled `build`, one session each, with native blocking edges on GitHub (`PIPESCOPE-95`).
They replace the slices this section first suggested: each ticket is a vertical slice, from the database to the page it shows on, so each is demonstrable on devnet on its own.
Every ticket works as [`docs/agents/build-tickets.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/agents/build-tickets.md) says, and in addition:

- **Verified on devnet data** (`PIPESCOPE-96`): its criteria run on Aviary's devnet deployment; every page it adds or changes is checked at 1440, 390 and 360 px wide in the light and the dark theme, with Playwright screenshots in its PR; CI runs the same tests on recorded devnet fixtures with no network.
- **Signing in tests** (`PIPESCOPE-94`): Playwright registers a Wallet Standard test wallet, only in test builds, that signs with a devnet test key from `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`; each ticket that adds a signing flow also runs it once in a real wallet extension set to devnet, driven in the owner's Chrome.
- **The keeper page** lives at `/keeper`, linked from every page's footer and from each product panel's due keeper jobs (`PIPESCOPE-97`).

Owner tasks first, each a HITL task ticket on the map:

1. [Aviary: owner setup for the first deploy (Aviary's Helius key and the Neon project)](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/110), before the scaffold.
2. [Aviary: owner setup for verified builds and the Telegram bot (GitHub token and working bot)](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/111), before verified builds and the bot.

The terminal, in run order:

1. [Aviary: scaffold both Workers, the database, the page shell with its themes, and the devnet deploy](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/113)
2. [Aviary: index the router's history into Postgres, with the feed's two tables](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/116)
3. [Aviary: index strategy programs and their versions, with the strategy page's version history](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/117) and [Aviary: candles, live rooms and the market page's chart and trades](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/118), side by side
4. [Aviary: strategy metadata, trust facts and the facts panel, with the feed's filters](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/119) (after strategy versions) and [Aviary: trade plain mints: quotes, the trade box, review and sign, the fast path and the Fees page](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/121) (after the market page), side by side
5. [Aviary: token names and images, and search](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/120), [Aviary: hooked mints, markets of three or four mints, and the wallet page](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/122) and [Aviary: custom-action forms, the create-market page and a place for product panels](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/123)

Canary, whose binary needs none of the above and starts at once:

1. [Aviary: Canary's binary, with readability, conformance, the exit test over sizes, quote against swap and cost](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/112)
2. [Aviary: Canary over time and across wallets (holding, later, launch clock, insiders, transferred tokens, a queue of buyers)](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/114) and [Aviary: Canary's control checks, token authorities acting, and transfer-hook accounts](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/115), side by side
3. [Aviary: Canary in a Container, run by CanaryRun, with results in Postgres](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/124), after both and the strategy versions
4. [Aviary: Canary's results on the pages and the trade box's exit-test notice](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/125), after the facts panel and the trade box

Then the explainer and the rest:

1. [Aviary: explainer jobs: the evidence, the validator, the approval queue and the approve command](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/126), after Canary in the Container and the facts; its first paid run waits for the owner's approval
2. [Aviary: the explanation on the strategy and market pages](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/127)
3. [Aviary: verified builds of strategy versions](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/128), after the explainer jobs, the GitHub token and [Tax AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and create a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/66), whose program is the first verified match
4. [Aviary: the keeper page and the keeper runner's records](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/129), after the scaffold and [Keeper runner: the runner, its wallet and the tax AMM's `distribute`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/94)

The Telegram bot, built alongside the pages ([`pipescope-telegram.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-telegram.md), When it is built):

1. [Aviary: arriving from Telegram (trade links, the wallet chooser on phones, alert links and the official handles)](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/130), after the trade box
2. [Aviary: the Telegram bot's scaffold](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/131), after the scaffold and the working bot
3. [Aviary: Telegram lookups (cards, search and the trade buttons)](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/132), after Canary in the Container, the facts and the explainer jobs
4. [Aviary: Telegram alerts and the public channel](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/133)
5. [Aviary: the Telegram watch list (upgrades with their results, changed Canary outcomes)](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/134)

Each product's Aviary ticket waits for the terminal tickets it builds on, wired as native edges:

- [Tax AMM in Aviary: the launch form and the tax panel](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/75) and [Containment hook in Aviary: the containment panel and the Unlock button](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/76): the market page, the facts, hooked mints, the forms and product-panel place, and Canary on the pages; the tax AMM's also the keeper page, for its due `distribute` jobs.
- [Buy wall AMM: Aviary panel and forms](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/57): the market page, the facts, hooked mints, the forms, the explainer jobs and the keeper page.
- [Lending AMM: Aviary panel, forms and explainer facts](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/88): the strategy-program calls, the market page, the trading path, hooked mints, the forms, the explainer jobs and the keeper page.

documents.title: Aviary: Canary checks
documents.body:
Decided in [Canary checks on the four devnet strategies](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/14) on 2026-11-10, from a rough harness run on every devnet market and the owner's reaction to its results.
The harness, its output for all 61 markets and a summary table are on the throwaway branch [`prototype/canary-checks`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/tree/prototype/canary-checks/prototype/canary-checks); that branch is never merged.
It builds on [Prior art for behavioural testing of Solana programs](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/8) ([findings](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/research/behavioural-testing-prior-art/research/behavioural-testing-prior-art.md)) and [Where the quoter runs for Canary checks](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/7) ([findings](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/research/quoter-hosting/research/quoter-hosting.md)).
[Cut Pipescope's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/22) reconciled this file with the other Aviary spec files on 2026-11-12 and cut its build tickets, listed in [`pipescope-architecture.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md#build-tickets).

## What Canary is

- Canary checks trade a private copy of one market the way a trader would, and record what happened.
- They detect; they cannot prove a market safe, and no result is a promise about a later trade or a later strategy version.
- Canary covers every strategy and every market registered with the router, not a chosen list: on 2026-11-10 devnet had 8 strategies and 61 markets, four more strategies than when the ticket was written.
- A Canary result belongs to one market, one strategy version and one slot, and says so.

### Three layers, and what each one sees

Pipeline published its own trust flags and its own checker, `pipeline-check`, on 2026-11-09.
Canary builds on both and does not repeat them.

| Layer | Whose | What it reads | What it cannot see |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trust flags (`pipeline-client`, the hosted API) | Pipeline's | The shape of accounts: upgradeable or frozen, mint and freeze authorities, Token-2022 extensions, metadata status | Anything a trade does |
| `pipeline-check` | Pipeline's | Whether quoting and trading one market through the router conforms to the strategy interface, at one moment, for the strategy's author | What a trade costs, what happens later or earlier, at other sizes, to other wallets, or when an authority acts |
| Canary | Ours | What a trader meets: whether they can get out, what the round trip returns, and how that changes with size, time, wallet and the use of an authority's powers | Rules reached only by inputs it did not try, and code that can tell a simulation from a real trade |

- Canary runs `pipeline-check` unchanged on every market copy and keeps its report as the **conformance report**, one Canary result among the others.
  This answers the question the explainer spec left open.
- Canary reuses Pipeline's trust flags for token facts and adds nothing to them except what its own runs measure.

## How a run works

- A Canary run covers one strategy version, on all of its markets or on one of them, and treats each market on its own.
- For each market it builds a copy of the market and everything its trades touch in a local Solana VM, with the cluster's slot, epoch and time, using `pipeline-check`'s own cloner.
- The cloner reads accounts from a source the caller supplies.
  On a developer's machine that is read-only RPC, as in the prototype.
  In the container [`pipescope-architecture.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md) specifies, which has no network, it is the snapshot the `CanaryRun` Durable Object posts in.
- A strategy can name more accounts when a later trade resolves its accounts than it did for the first snapshot.
  When a trade names an account the snapshot lacks, the binary answers with the missing addresses instead of results, and the Durable Object fetches them and posts the snapshot again, at most four times; after that the affected checks are "not run", naming the accounts.
  On devnet the prototype needed about 7 RPC requests a market, no more than the first copy takes, so no strategy there asked for more.
- The router and the strategy are the cluster's own program bytes, so the run tests what is deployed.
- Signature checks are off in the VM, so the run can act as any key: a fresh wallet, the market creator, an upgrade authority or a token authority.
- Every trade goes through the router's real `swap`, is committed in the VM, and can be followed by another trade in the state it left.
- Before every swap the run resolves the strategy's accounts in the current state and takes a quote with `pipeline-quoter` holding only what an integrator would hold; the swap is then compared with that quote.
- Each scenario starts from a fresh copy of the snapshot unless it says otherwise, so one scenario never changes another's starting state.
- Wallets are new random keys on every run.
- Transfer-hook accounts are resolved as `pipeline-check` resolves them; the prototype skipped this because no devnet mint has a hook.

### The money side and sizes

- Sizes are always set on the **money side** of a market, and a sale only ever sells what a buy in the same run produced.
  The prototype first sized sales by a share of the token vault and sold more tokens than could exist, which produced false alarms of 2% to 20% returns on two curves; this rule removes them.
- The money side is wrapped SOL when the market has it; otherwise it is the mint whose vault holds the smallest share of that mint's supply.
- With wrapped SOL the sizes are 0.00001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 SOL, and the **reference size** is 0.01 SOL.
- Without wrapped SOL the sizes are 1, 100, 1,000, 10,000 and 50,000 parts per million of the money vault, and the reference size is 1,000 parts per million; when that vault holds under 2,000,000 units they are 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 whole tokens and the reference size is 1 token.
- When the reference size cannot be bought and sold back, the largest size that can stands in for it and the result says so.
- Every size is reported beside its share of the money vault, because 10 SOL into a devnet pool holding 0.2 SOL buys the whole pool.
- Mainnet sizes, including a size equal to Jupiter's 500 dollar routing benchmark, are for the mainnet plan.

### Clock positions

- **Waits**: the same slot, the next slot, 10 seconds, 1 minute, 10 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day, 3 days and 30 days, moving slot, epoch and Unix time together (2.5 slots a second, 432,000 slots an epoch).
- **Launch clock**: the market's creation time and 10 seconds, 1 minute, 10 minutes, 1 hour and 1 day after it, for every offset that is already in the past.
  The state is today's; only the clock is set back, so the figures show the strategy's time rules, not what early buyers actually got.

## Outcomes

- A Canary result has one of five outcomes: **pass**, **warn**, **fail**, **not run** or **noted**.
- The number behind an outcome is always shown beside it, and a code-written sentence gives the reason.
- **Fail** is kept for what the **ordinary trade** meets right now: a buy of the reference size or the smallest size at the cluster's current clock, sold back in the same slot or the next (owner, 2026-11-10).
- Anything that depends on another time, a larger size or an authority choosing to act is at most a **warn**, with its numbers.
  A market still inside a launch-time tax fails on its own, because its ordinary trade returns too little right now.
- **Not run** always carries its reason, such as "the market refuses every trade (`WrongStatus`: Not allowed in the curve's current status)".
- **Noted** is for facts Canary reads and does not judge.
- The round-trip return bands are the owner's (2026-11-10): **95% or more back is a pass, 50% up to 95% is a warn, under 50% is a fail**.
  The rows below call these the **pass band** and the **fail band**; their values live only in Canary's config module ([One place for every value](#one-place-for-every-value)), with the 1-point tolerance and the other policy values.
  On devnet today the ordinary trade returns 97.0% to 99.5% on seven strategies and 48.8% to 49.4% on the outside builder's AMM, so the bands sit in a wide gap.
- These words follow `pipeline-check`'s (pass, warn, fail, skip) so one page can show both.
- An outcome belongs to one check on one market.
  Canary never adds outcomes up into a score, a badge or a colour, which [`pipescope.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/pipescope.md) rules out; how a result is shown is for [Pipescope screens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/16).
- The engineering bar in [`README.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/README.md) asks our own strategies to pass Canary checks on devnet.
  That means no fail on any market of the version, with every warn named and explained in that product's spec; it is a gate for us, never something shown to traders.
- One consequence of the rule: a strategy that lets a buyer sell at once and refuses them a day later gets a warn, not a fail.
  The result's sentence says plainly that the tokens could not be sold after that wait.

### How a failure is named

Every failed step is classed from the transaction's error and logs, with the program that raised it and, for Anchor programs, the error's name, number, message and source line:

- **cannot read state**: the strategy cannot deserialise the market's state (`AccountDidNotDeserialize`, `AccountDiscriminatorMismatch`).
- **strategy refused**, **router refused**, **token program refused**: a clean error from that program.
- **crash**: the program panicked instead of returning an error.
- **out of compute**: the step ran out of its compute limit (200,000 units for a quote, 1,400,000 for a swap).

A crash or an out-of-compute anywhere in a run is at least a warn on the check it happened in.

## The checks

Check ids are stable.
Each row gives the outcome rule; "ordinary trade" is as defined above.

### Readability and conformance

| Id | What it does | Fail | Warn | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readable` | Calls `pipeline_market_info`, resolves accounts and quotes the smallest size in every direction | The strategy's current version cannot read the market's state: a **stranded market** | A direction resolves and then crashes or runs out of compute | The version reads the market; a market that reads but refuses every trade passes here and its trading checks are "not run" with the strategy's own error |
| `conformance` | Runs `pipeline-check` on the copy and keeps its whole report | `pipeline-check` reports fail | It reports warn | It reports pass |

### Exit test

| Id | What it does | Fail | Warn | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exit_sizes` | Buys each size and sells everything bought in the same slot | At the reference size or the smallest size, the tokens cannot be sold back | At a larger size, the tokens cannot be sold back | Every size that could be bought was sold back; sizes that could not be bought are listed and are not a finding |
| `exit_hold` | Buys the reference size, then sells after each wait, each wait from the same bought state | The sale fails in the same slot or the next | After a longer wait the sale fails, or returns more than the tolerance less than in the same slot | Every wait sells within the tolerance of the same slot |
| `exit_late` | Moves the clock forward by each wait, then buys and sells the reference size | Never: it is not the present | A later round trip fails, or returns more than the tolerance less than now | Every later round trip is within the tolerance of now |
| `exit_launch_clock` | Sets the clock to each launch-clock position, then buys and sells the reference size | Never: it is not the present | A launch-clock round trip fails, or returns more than the tolerance less than now | Every one is within the tolerance of now |
| `exit_wallets` | Round-trips the reference size from five fresh wallets, the market creator, the strategy's upgrade authority and each mint authority, each from the same starting state | Fresh wallets get different results from the same state, or an insider gets more back than a fresh wallet | An insider gets less back than a fresh wallet | All get the same |
| `exit_transferred` | One wallet buys the reference size and sends the tokens to a second wallet, which sells them | The transfer went through and the second wallet cannot sell | The transfer is refused (for any token, ours or anyone's: the result says the token could not be sent to another wallet, and what the buyer got back by selling it), or the second wallet's return is below the pass band while the buyer's own is not, or, when the buyer's own is below it too, more than the tolerance below the buyer's own (`CANARY-37`) | The second wallet's return is in the pass band, or no more than the tolerance below a buyer's own return that is also below it |
| `exit_queue` | Five wallets buy the reference size one after another, then sell in the same order | Any of the five cannot sell, or together they get back within the fail band | Together they get back less than the pass band | All five sell and together get back within the pass band |

- Wallets that are a program's address, not a wallet, are skipped and named: a key off the Ed25519 curve, a program, or an account a program holds (`CANARY-39`).
- In `exit_queue` only the total is judged: in a thin pool the first buyer out gains what the last one loses, which is ordinary price movement.
- Every row but `exit_sizes` trades the reference size, or the size that stands in for it in `exit_sizes`, and judges a later or earlier time against a round trip measured in the same row at the cluster's clock, from the same kind of starting state (`CANARY-40`).

### Quote against swap

| Id | What it does | Fail | Warn | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quote_matches_swap` | Compares every swap the run commits with the quote taken in the same state just before it: output received, input sent, Pipeline fee, and the trader's own balance changes | In the ordinary trade, any difference, a quoted swap that fails, or a swap that works when its quote failed | The same at another size or clock position | Every compared swap equals its quote; the count is reported |

- Exact-out quoting stays with `pipeline-check`'s `quotes`, `quote_matches_swap` and `exact_out_refund` checks, carried in the conformance report; Canary trades exact-in only.
- Of the exit checks' own swaps, the ordinary trade is a buy or sale of the reference size by a fresh wallet in the copy's own state, at the cluster's clock or the next slot: `exit_hold`'s buy and its sales in the same and the next slot, `exit_late`'s round trips now and a slot later, `exit_launch_clock`'s round trip now, the fresh wallets' round trips in `exit_wallets`, the buy in `exit_transferred` and the first buy in `exit_queue` (`CANARY-41`).

### Fee honesty

| Id | What it does | Fail | Warn | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cost` | Reports the **round-trip return** at every size of `exit_sizes`, and splits the loss at the smallest size and at the reference size into Pipeline's fee on both legs, Token-2022 transfer fees, and the rest, which is the strategy's own fee and spread | The ordinary trade's return is in the fail band | The ordinary trade's return is between the two bands, or any other size returns less than the pass band | Every size's return is in the pass band |

- Pipeline's fee on the sale is charged in the token and is valued at the sale's own price; at the reference size on devnet the two legs together come to 0.49% to 0.50% of what was put in, and to 0.37% on the outside builder's AMM, where the sale brings back half as much.
- The same bands apply to the returns measured by the other exit checks.

### Control

| Id | What it does | Fail | Warn | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direct_call` | Calls the strategy's `pipeline_swap` without the router, once with another key signing as the market signer and once with the real market signer not signing, after sending the input to the vault as the router would | Never | The call is accepted: trades can skip the Pipeline fee and leave no swap event | Both calls are refused |
| `token_authorities` | For each of the market's mints, acts as each authority that exists and then trades again (see below) | Never: it depends on an authority acting | An authority exists and its action took from the market or stopped or emptied a trade; the figure is reported | No mint has such an authority |
| `transaction_accounts` | Lists accounts the strategy asks for that describe the transaction, not the market: the Instructions, SlotHashes and RecentBlockhashes sysvars | Never | The strategy asks for one, so it could tell a simulated trade from a real one and Canary's results may not hold | It asks for none |
| `contained_mint` | For a mint with a transfer hook, reads the hook program, whether it can still be upgraded, and the hook's authority, as [`containment-hook.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/spec/containment-hook.md) recognises a contained token | Never | The hook is not our containment hook with the mint's unlock PDA as its authority, or the hook program can still be upgraded | The hook is our containment hook, its authority is the mint's unlock PDA and the hook program is frozen; "not run" when no mint has a hook, and when a mint's transfer hook extension has both its program and its authority unset, as a contained token's has after its unlock |
| `custom_instructions` | Lists every instruction in the strategy's code beyond Pipeline's six, each with how often it has been called and by which signers | Noted only | Noted only | Noted only |

What `token_authorities` does with each authority, when the authority is a wallet:

- **Mint authority**: mints 100 times what the market's vault holds of that mint and sells it all; the result is the share of the other vault taken.
- **Freeze authority**: after a buy of the reference size, freezes the buyer's token account, then tries the sale.
- **Transfer-fee authority**: sets the fee to 100% with no maximum, moves the clock two epochs on so the fee applies, then round-trips the reference size.
- **Permanent delegate**: after a buy, moves the buyer's tokens away.
- **Pause authority**: pauses the mint, then tries the sale.
- An authority that is a program's address is "not run" and named with the program that owns it, because only that program's own instructions can use it.
- An authority is a program's address by the same rule as an insider in `exit_wallets` (`CANARY-39`): a key off the Ed25519 curve, a program, or an account a program holds, such as a market's own state or an SPL multisig (`CANARY-43`).
- An authority of the money side's mint acts in the same round trip: freezing the buyer's account of it or pausing it between the buy and the sale, setting its transfer fee before the buy, and, as permanent delegate, taking what the sale returned once the buyer holds it; a mint authority sells what it minted into each other mint, each sale from the same state (`CANARY-44`).

The prototype ran the first and third on devnet and built the second; no devnet mint has a freeze authority, a permanent delegate or a pause authority.

### Custom instructions are listed, not called

- Instruction names come from the strategy's code: each "Instruction: Name" string Anchor compiles in is kept only when the discriminator of that name is also in the code, which also cuts names that run on into the next string.
- That list is worked out once per strategy version, by `terminal-api` when the indexer records the version, and stored with it; the facts panel, the forms' instruction check and the explainer read it from there, and the `CanaryRun` Durable Object posts it in the snapshot, so one implementation serves all four.
- The snapshot carries it in an optional `instructions` field, whether the program is built with Anchor and each instruction's name, call count and signers; Canary drops Pipeline's six by name and notes the rest, and a run given no list records `custom_instructions` as "not run" (`CANARY-46`).
- A program that is not built with Anchor gets "none found", worded as such and not as "none".
- Who has called each instruction, and how often, comes from the indexer's history of the strategy program.
- Canary v1 does not call custom instructions: the prototype can name them and cannot build their arguments without each strategy's own layout (owner, 2026-11-10).
- Canary does use the standard token powers above, which need no strategy-specific knowledge.
- The 34 on devnet: `Deposit` (constant product); `ClaimAllocation`, `ClaimCreatorFees`, `ClaimLeftover`, `FundCurve`, `Graduate`, `SetFeeRecipient` (bonding curve); `RebalanceWall`, `SeedPool`, `SettleRetired`, `SweepFees` (Pool4 port); `Buy`, `Buyback`, `CreateMarket`, `DeepenQuote`, `DeepenToken`, `InitializeFactory`, `PublishManifest`, `Sell`, `SetMetadata`, `SplitFees` (outside builder); `ClaimFees`, `ClosePack`, `OpenDraw`, `OpenPack` (`2Tmcmq...`); `BurnToClose`, `ClaimFees`, `Deploy` (`4LHmX6...`); `ClaimFees` (`4scUVy...`); `ClaimTax`, `InitializeConfig`, `Launch`, `SweepProtocolFees`, `UpdateConfig` (`EZwLuZ...`).
