| Ledgers | `pool_tokens`, `pool_sol`, `retired_tokens`, `rewards_owed`, `idle_sol`, `fees_recipient`, `fees_designer`, `fees_suite` |
| Cap | inventory cap, `decay_credit`, `decay_time` |
| Wall guard | `ref`, `ref_time`, `floor`, `floor_time`, `last_slot`, `last_close`, `low_since_placement` ([`POOL4-50`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-50-when-the-walls-floor-moves)) |
| Totals | tokens trimmed, SOL trimmed, tokens the wall bought, tokens burned, rewards paid, tips paid |
| Reward share | `cap_fall_unmatched`, `retired_rewardable` ([`POOL4-49`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-49-which-retired-tokens-earn-the-reward-share)) |
| Reserve | zeroed to the end of the account |

The first build ticket ([Buy wall AMM: a market opens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/47)) fixed the byte offsets below; they are frozen from the first devnet deployment ([Buy wall AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/56)) and published in the IDL.
The creation parameters `cap_floor_bps` and `cap_decay_bps` are kept as well, because `cap_floor` and `cap_decay_per_day` can only be computed at the seed, from what the seed brings.

### A release gate

- Before any upgrade, a script downloads every live market state of the program from the cluster, with its mints and vaults, and loads them into LiteSVM with the new build and the real router.
- On every market it runs account resolution, a quote, a buy and a sell through the router, and each keeper job whose condition holds or that the deployed build runs.
- The upgrade is refused if a step fails on any market that passes there under the deployed build, if a layout check fails, or if a quote differs from the deployed build's quote on the same state without the release declaring a pricing change.
- Every run also makes and trades a market of its own with the new build, so a cluster with no market still tests it.
- The deploy script accepts only a build whose hash the gate has passed.

How it does each of these ([`POOL4-41`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-41-what-the-release-gate-runs-on-each-market) to [`POOL4-45`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-45-how-the-gate-reads-a-cluster), [`POOL4-46`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-46-when-a-failed-step-counts-against-a-candidate), [`POOL4-47`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-47-markets-the-router-has-not-recorded) and [`POOL4-53`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-53-every-gate-run-trades-a-market-of-its-own)):

- It finds the market states as the accounts the program owns that start with the discriminator, and refuses outright if one of them is not `MARKET_STATE_SIZE` bytes.
- It copies each market as `pipeline-check` does (the router and its config, the Market, the strategy's registration, program and ProgramData, the mints, vaults, fee accounts, transfer hooks and every account `pipeline_resolve_accounts` lists), adds the token accounts the payouts pay into, reads them all again in as few calls as it can so they agree, and saves them in one snapshot file with the cluster's clock read last.
- A market state the router has no Market for, which any wallet can make by calling `pipeline_seed_liquidity` itself, is copied the same way, as if the router had recorded what `pipeline_market_info` gives, and saved marked unregistered.
- When it takes the snapshot it replays it with the deployed build and records what that build did: its quotes, and whether each other step passed, with the program a failure started in and its error, every keeper job tried whether due or not, each slot of `sweep_fees` on its own.
- Each replay asks the build it runs for the wallet of every fee slot it sweeps, never the gate's own tree, which is the candidate's: a sweep simulated with the gate's payer as the recipient, which the build refuses naming the wallet it pays (Anchor's `require_keys_eq!` logs it), or refuses for its own reason (nothing owed, no wallet set), which is then that build's answer; so a tree that refuses a slot's wallet cannot drop that sweep from the deployed build's record and its own test alike (review finding R2G-03).
- The gate's own market still takes its due jobs from this tree, so a tree that refuses a slot's wallet is caught on the cluster's markets the deployed build swept that slot on, and not on a cluster with no such market.
- On every market, with the candidate and the router copied from the cluster, it registers a market the router never recorded, with the router's `register_existing_market` and `init_fee_account` for both mints, and creates any missing router fee account, as anyone may, so such a market is checked like the rest.
- It then resolves the accounts of a buy and a sell, quotes exact-in both ways at a tenth, a hundredth and a thousandth of the input vault and compares each quote with the deployed build's on the same state, and checks that `pipeline_market_info` gives the mints and vaults the router records.
- It runs each keeper job that this tree's rules say is due on the state as downloaded and each job the deployed build ran on the snapshot, so a candidate that narrows a rule cannot drop that job from its own test, then buys with a hundredth of the SOL vault and sells what that bought, each swap with the candidate's quote as its minimum and delivering exactly it.
- A market waiting for its seed is seeded first, as its seeder would seed it (the replay checks no signatures, and removes the mint's authorities and clears its transfer hook as a seed requires), then traded like the rest, so a build that could not seed it is refused.
- A failed step counts against the candidate unless the deployed build failed the same step, matched by kind and not by name, on the same snapshot, with the same error starting in the same program: a market whose token's hook refuses the gate's trader, or whose fee recipient handed its wrapped SOL account to another owner, fails those steps under every build and cannot veto a release, while a candidate that newly fails a step, fails it in its own code where the deployed build failed in the hook, or fails it with another error where the deployed build failed in the same program, is refused.
- The error compared is the instruction error, which carries the failing program's own error code (`InstructionError(0, Custom(6033))`), or the whole message when no program raised it, so a third party who blocks one step of a market inside the buy wall AMM (a reassigned recipient's account, say) excuses only that refusal there, never a different regression of the step on that market (review finding R2G-01).
- The layout checks (reading the market state, finding the market, account resolution, the quotes and `pipeline_market_info`) never count as failing under the deployed build too, and run on every market whatever else fails there, so a build that would strand a market is refused even on a market whose trades are blocked.
- Both replays sign with the same keys, the payer derived from the program and each market's trader and keeper from the market, so a step whose compute depends on a PDA's bump cannot pass in one replay and fail in the other.
- After the cluster's markets, every run (`run` and `check` alike) makes a market of its own with the candidate, so a cluster with no market, as before the first market or the first deploy, still exercises it, and a build that refuses every instruction, such as one declared for another address as the `test-designer-recipient` build is, is refused (review findings H097 and H098).
- It makes that market in a world of its own, holding only the router the replay runs and the candidate at the program's address, at the snapshot's clock: the run makes the router's config as devnet's (a 0.01 SOL listing fee) and registers the program paying the listing fee, and takes nothing else from the cluster, so the market's payouts go to token accounts made fresh, and neither a pause of the router nor a fixed fee wallet's reassigned wrapped SOL account (`SUITE_TREASURY`'s, or `DESIGNER_RECIPIENT`'s once set) can refuse every candidate, an emergency fix included (review finding R2G-02).
- It creates and seeds the market through the router at IMD's launch values and trades it past its first wall and settlement, as the synthetic fixture's market A is made, then ten minutes on runs the checks every market gets, with each quote required to serve and each keeper job that has become due.
- Every step on that market counts against the candidate, none excused as one the deployed build fails too, since the deployed build never ran it.
- A release declares a pricing change in `programs/buy-wall-amm/release.json`, committed with it, by naming the executable hash of each build whose quotes it changes, so a declaration left behind after its release stops covering anything once the build it named is no longer deployed.
- A declaration lets amounts differ, never a quote the deployed build served turn into a refusal, and a pass that relied on one is recorded only from the committed `release.json` with no uncommitted change, and counts for a deploy only while the committed file still declares it.
- A passing run against a cluster is recorded in `deployments/release-gate/buy-wall-amm/<cluster>.json` (a local validator's records are kept out of git), with every failed step that did not count and why; the deploy script accepts a build only with a record for that cluster and that executable hash, made against the build deployed there now and covering every market there now, so an upgrade or a new market since the run means running the gate again.
- A record says the run traded a market of its own, and a record without that, written by a gate before `POOL4-53`, never covers a deploy.
- It reads a cluster only through read-only JSON-RPC calls, sent with `curl`, and can send nothing; it prints and saves an RPC URL without its path, query or user part, where a provider's key sits.

#### How to run it

The gate stands in front of the one deploy path every program takes, `scripts/deploy-devnet.sh` ([`POOL4-54`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-54-one-deploy-path-with-the-release-gate-in-front)): that script builds the commit with solana-verify in Docker and, before it sends anything, runs `programs/buy-wall-amm/scripts/pre-deploy.sh` on the very bytes built, which refuses unless a passing gate run covers that build on that cluster now.
From a clean checkout of `main`, with the toolchain on `PATH` (`source scripts/toolchain-env.sh`):

```sh
# The verified build, and nothing sent; prints its executable hash.
scripts/deploy-devnet.sh buy-wall-amm --build-only --out <dir>
# Replay every market on the cluster with that build; records the pass, or exits 1 naming
# each market and step that failed.
(cd programs && cargo run -p buy-wall-gate -- run --cluster devnet --candidate <dir>/buy_wall_amm.so)
# Deploy or upgrade: the same build again, refused unless a passing run covers it on this cluster now.
scripts/deploy-devnet.sh buy-wall-amm
```

- `--cluster` takes `devnet`, `localnet` or an RPC URL; `--snapshot-out <file>` keeps what was downloaded, and `cargo run -p buy-wall-gate -- check --snapshot <file> --candidate <build>` replays it again offline.
- For a release that changes pricing, set `pricing_change` in `release.json` to the builds it changes (`{ "from": ["<hash>"], "why": "..." }`, each hash from `cargo run -p buy-wall-gate -- hash <build>` or the gate's own output), and once it has deployed, set it back to `null` and re-record each fixture's baseline (its quotes and step outcomes) with the deployed build (`cargo run -p buy-wall-gate -- rerecord --fixture <file> --build <deployed build>`).
- `cargo run -p buy-wall-gate -- help` lists every command.

### Fixtures in CI

- The repo keeps a saved market state for every layout version ever deployed, taken from a real market.
- CI runs the release gate's checks on each of them against every build.
- Layout version 1 has two: `layout-1-devnet.json`, the devnet demo market saved on 2026-11-20 with every keeper job due, after its first walk through all of them and one more buy and sell (`demo.ts --market <its state> --trade-only`, then `cargo run -p buy-wall-gate -- snapshot --cluster devnet --out <file>`), and `layout-1-synthetic.json`, three markets made by a LiteSVM run through devnet's router before the first deploy (one with every keeper job due, one with none, one waiting for its seed), marked synthetic; CI keeps both ([`POOL4-20`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-20-the-first-layout-fixture)).
- Fixtures are snapshots in `programs/buy-wall-amm/gate/fixtures/`, without the programs: CI replays each with the pinned router and the build under test, and compares its quotes with the ones the fixture records.
- CI also builds seven test builds from edited copies of the workspace, never from the program's own source ([`POOL4-44`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-44-how-the-gate-is-proved-to-catch-stranding)): one moving a field, one renaming the market state type with its discriminator left to Anchor, one growing the account, each of which the gate must refuse on every fixture, failing on every open market, one whose payout rule can no longer sweep fee slot 2 and one whose fee slot 2 wallet is refused as unset, each of which it must refuse on every market the deployed build swept that slot on and on its own market, and one appending a field into the reserve as layout version 2 and one with the designer's wallet set, as the upgrade that sets `DESIGNER_RECIPIENT` will set it, each of which it must pass.
- A fixture records the deployed build's outcome of every step as a cluster snapshot does; `rerecord` records them again, and reads a fixture saved before they were recorded.

## Upgrades and freezing

- On devnet the program stays upgradeable under the project's upgrade-authority key, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/upgrade-authority.json`, as `README.md` sets for every program, and every upgrade there passes the release gate.
- Intended mainnet upgrade policy: frozen (upgrade authority removed) before any mainnet deployment, after `DESIGNER_RECIPIENT` is set.
  This departs from the shared default of a multisig with a timelock first: a market's promise is that nobody has power over it, and an upgrade key would be exactly that power, over locked liquidity, the cap and the burns.
- Carrying the policy out belongs to the mainnet launch effort.

| `set_fee_recipient` | `other` | The fee recipient |
| `set_rewards_recipient` | `other` | The rewards recipient |

- Every action that moves the token forwards transfer-hook accounts after its own, as the template's swap does.
  Since the seed refuses a live hook ([`POOL4-48`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-48-a-transfer-hook-at-the-seed)), a seeded market's token never needs any, so the generic forms work for every market; the forwarding matters only to a seed attempted while a hook is live, which is refused before any transfer.
- Each instruction emits an event (market created, seeded, wall placed, settled, rewards paid, fees swept, recipient changed), and a swap emits one when it trims or lowers the cap (`Trimmed` or `CapLowered`, [`POOL4-30`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-30-what-a-swap-that-moves-the-cap-reports)), so Aviary's indexer can show a market's history; Aviary reads current values from the market state, not from events.
- `pipeline_seed_liquidity` is described in a top-level `seed_liquidity` form shaped as `init` is, which Pipeline's validator allows as an unknown key: the seeded market state as a `pda:` source keyed by `input:seeder`, `input:token_mint` and wrapped SOL, `data` as init's arguments under the same IDL type with the seeder marked ignored, and the vault authority and both vaults after Pipeline's fixed seed accounts, so the SDK's `resolveInit` resolves it ([`POOL4-28`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-28-how-metadata-describes-seeding-from-another-program)).
- The metadata follows `pipeline-strategy-metadata/1` at `5ad130d`: name, a description that credits IMD's Pool4, category `amm`, tags including `pool4`, links including `source` and the IDL, `init` as above with `market_state: new_keypair`, every action above, `security.contact`, and `conformance` pointing at a published `pipeline-check` report and its SHA-256; where they are published is in `README.md`.
- The trust flags describe programs and mints, not markets, so nothing there says a market trims or burns: the metadata declares it, and Aviary reads each market's parameters, ledgers and cap from its market state.
- Pipeline's API reports raw vault balances, so retired tokens, the buy wall, idle SOL and unpaid fees show there as liquidity; Aviary reads the ledgers instead.

## Worked example

Checked against an integer model of this file's rules, which also held every invariant in "Ledgers" over 3,000 random runs (about 957,000 swaps, 65,000 trims and 33,000 wall placements).
The build must reproduce these numbers exactly.

A market is seeded with 1,000,000 tokens of 6 decimals (1,000,000,000,000 units) and 10 SOL, with `fee_bps` 100, `wall_split_bps` 5,000, `reward_share_bps` 1,500, `cap_floor_bps` 2,000 and `cap_decay_bps` 2,000.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Seed | `sqrt_price` 1,844,674,407,370,955,161; `liquidity` 99,999,999,999; cap 1,000,000,000,000 |
| One hour later, a buy of 1 SOL | Fee 10,000,000: designer 1,000,000, suite 1,000,000, fee recipient 4,000,000, wall 4,000,000. Out 90,081,892,629 units; `sqrt_price` 2,027,297,173,702,505,949. The cap falls by one hour's allowance, 8,333,333,333 units, to 991,666,666,667 |
| 60 seconds later, a sell of those 90,081,892,629 units | Gross 989,999,999; fee 9,900,000 (3,960,000 of it to the wall); out 980,099,999. `sqrt_price` 1,844,674,407,372,029,099. The trim retires 8,333,333,329 units, all matched by the cap's fall, and moves 83,333,332 lamports to idle SOL, leaving `liquidity` 99,166,666,666, `pool_tokens` 991,666,666,671, `pool_sol` 9,916,666,669 and `idle_sol` 91,293,332 |
| `place_wall`, in a later slot | Tip 912,933. `wall_top` 1,844,674,407,370,955,161, the opening price: the floor drops to the sell's price, but the lowest close since the seed is the opening price, just below it; `wall_liquidity` 903,804,010; `wall_sol_placed` 90,380,400; `pool_sol` 10,007,047,068; 11 units of dust join the retired tokens (8,333,333,340), leaving `pool_tokens` 991,666,666,660 |
| `settle` | The reward share of the 8,333,333,329 matched units, 1,249,999,999, joins `rewards_owed`; the other 7,083,333,341 units, the dust among them, are burned |
| 60 seconds later, a sell of 20,000,000,000 units | Gross 196,081,138; fee 1,960,812; out 194,120,326, through the curve and the wall together. `sqrt_price` 1,808,529,293,214,755,428. The wall has spent 1,770,941 lamports on 180,633,508 units |

In the same model, on a market seeded the same way with 5 SOL idle, buying with 30 SOL, placing the wall in the next slot (it is refused in the buy's own slot) and selling everything back loses 0.595 SOL, and the wall's top ends no higher than the price before the buy.

## Aviary's panel

Aviary's buy wall AMM panel shows, per market:

- the price, the buy wall's top, the SOL in the wall and what it has bought since it was placed, and the wall's floor;
- the inventory cap against what the curve holds, the cap floor, the cap decay and the allowance built up;
- retired tokens, rewards owed, and the tokens burned so far as a share of the supply;
- the fee and its split, each fee ledger, and whether the designer share has a wallet yet;
- the market's parameters and both recipients;
- each keeper job that is due, as a button, and the recipients' handover forms;
- the create form, pre-filled with IMD's launch values and showing the whole fee split, the designer and suite shares included.

The explainer's fact table carries the same facts, and its risks for every buy wall market are: the curve thins as the cap falls, so the same trade moves the price more over time; after a fall in price the buy wall can sit well below the price, because its floor rises only about 4% a day; and the rewards recipient can trade the cap down itself and take the reward share of that fall at once, though never more than the budget the reward share and the cap floor set.
A hook that could stop trading is not among them, since the seed refuses a token whose transfer hook is still live ([`POOL4-48`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-48-a-transfer-hook-at-the-seed)).

## For the shared engineering bar

What `README.md` asks each product's file to add; the mainnet upgrade policy is under "Upgrades and freezing".

### Compute ceilings

Asserted per instruction in test layer 5; the build ticket measures each one and may lower it, and raising one needs a written reason here.
They start from another Pool4 port's swaps on devnet, measured at 13,000 to 29,000 units, with room for 256-bit maths.
No transfer hook runs on a seeded market's token ([`POOL4-48`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-48-a-transfer-hook-at-the-seed)), so they cover every transfer the strategy makes, including those of a token whose hook was cleared, which the tests measure beside SPL Token and Token-2022.

| Instruction | Ceiling (compute units) | Main cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pipeline_quote` | 40,000 | Two pricing steps at most; well under the quoter's 200,000 cap |
| `pipeline_swap`, one step | 45,000 | Pricing, one output transfer, the books and the guard |
| `pipeline_swap`, crossing into the wall and trimming | 60,000 | Two pricing steps and the trim |
| `pipeline_resolve_accounts` | 10,000 | Two accounts, the output vault and the vault authority |
| `pipeline_market_info` | 10,000 | |
| `pipeline_init_market` | 120,000 | Creating two vaults |
| `seed` | 80,000 | Two transfers in and two square roots |
| `pipeline_seed_liquidity` | 180,000 | Creation plus the seed |
| `place_wall` | 50,000 | Closing and placing the wall, one transfer |
| `settle` | 30,000 | One burn |
| `pay_rewards` | 60,000 | One transfer, possibly creating the recipient's token account |
| `sweep_fees` | 60,000 | One transfer, possibly creating the recipient's token account |
| `set_fee_recipient`, `set_rewards_recipient` | 10,000 | |

Measured on 2026-11-12 by [Buy wall AMM: plain trading through the router](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/48), on markets from 10^-7 to 10^9 lamports a unit and trades from dust to a third of a pool: `pipeline_quote` at most 15,682 units, a one-step `pipeline_swap` 14,837 to 27,630 (a hook's own compute left out), and `pipeline_resolve_accounts` 5,181 to 5,372.
The ceilings stay as they are for the wall's second step and the trim.
Measured on 2026-11-12 by [Buy wall AMM: the inventory cap](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/49), on the same five markets: a buy that lowers the cap 22,240 to 35,480 units and a sell that trims 26,649 to 33,223, within their ceilings of 45,000 and 60,000 (a hook's own compute left out); with the cap's steps on every swap, the costliest one-step swap of the earlier measurement is now 36,396.
Measured on 2026-11-16 by [Buy wall AMM: the buy wall](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/50), on the same five markets: `place_wall` 16,858 to 29,143 units (the most when it closes a wall that has bought tokens, on the market of 10^-7 lamports a unit), a sell that crosses into the wall and trims 41,013 to 48,388, and its quote 25,886 to 28,534; the ceilings stay as they are.
Measured on 2026-11-17 by [Buy wall AMM: hardening](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/55), with the floor's slot rule ([`POOL4-50`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-50-when-the-walls-floor-moves)), on the same five markets: `place_wall` 17,611 to 29,889 units, about 750 more for reading the Clock and bringing the floor up to date; the ceilings stay as they are.
Measured on 2026-11-16 by [Buy wall AMM: payouts and recipient handovers](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/51), on SPL Token, Token-2022 and Token-2022 with a transfer hook, with recipients whose associated token accounts have bump 255 (a payout derives that address twice, once itself and once in the associated token program, at 1,500 units for each bump below 255, a cost of the recipient's address and not of the program): `settle` 6,894 to 8,605 units, `pay_rewards` 10,383 to 19,390 into an account that exists and 27,354 to 40,213 when it creates one (the most for the hooked Token-2022 token, the hook's own compute left out), `sweep_fees` 10,381 into an account that exists and 27,347 when it creates one, and a handover 1,590; the ceilings stay as they are.
Measured on 2026-11-17 by [Buy wall AMM: hardening](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/55), with the payouts sharing one helper and a handover refusing the market's own addresses ([`POOL4-52`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-52-which-wallets-a-role-may-be-handed-to)), on the same three tokens: `pay_rewards` 10,242 to 19,249 units into an account that exists and 27,204 to 40,063 when it creates one, `sweep_fees` 10,230 and 27,187, and a handover 3,196 (deriving the vault authority from its stored bump costs most of the rise); the ceilings stay as they are.
Measured on 2026-11-12 by [Buy wall AMM: seeding by another program](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/53), inside the stand-in launchpad's call in LiteSVM: `pipeline_seed_liquidity` 48,850 units for an SPL Token token, 59,716 for a Token-2022 one and 65,802 for one with a transfer hook (the hook's own compute left out), and 60,847 for an SPL Token token on a local validator; its ceiling stays at 180,000, room for what later tickets add to creation and the seed.

### Invariants for test layer 3

Beyond the shared three (value conserved, every holder can exit, each quote equals its swap), checked after every step of generated sequences of swaps, keeper jobs and clock jumps, including several trades in one slot:

- Every invariant in "Ledgers".
- "Every holder can exit" means, at a price bound ([`POOL4-36`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-36-every-holder-can-exit-at-a-price-bound)): a holder's whole holding sells, or it pays nothing (worth less than one lamport), or it is more than the curve can take before `MIN_SQRT_PRICE` and is refused whole, as "Rules for both" says, and then the most the curve can take sells or pays nothing, and one token unit more is refused for the bound.
  A trim can leave a curve of `MIN_LIQUIDITY` close to the bound, which takes fewer tokens than some holdings; what such a holding cannot sell could only sell below the bound, for the `(L + W) × MIN_SQRT_PRICE / Q` lamports the curve and the wall keep there, which no sell reaches for anyone, with or without the cap.
  A trim lowers `L`, so it only shrinks that amount, which is less than one lamport whenever `L + W` is below 2^32.
- A trim never changes `sqrt_price`.
- A buy sold straight back never returns more than it cost, whatever keeper jobs run in between: in its own slot `place_wall` is refused, and a buy sold back after `place_wall` in a later slot with no time passed in between never returns more either, whether it opened its slot or followed a fall earlier in that slot (the back-run the placement cap closes, [`POOL4-50`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/decisions.md#pool4-50-when-the-walls-floor-moves)).
- A placed wall's top is never above the lowest close since the last placement, which every swap's close lowers and only `place_wall` resets, to the price at placement.
- For the rewards recipient, settling and paying itself inside the round trip, the rewards it takes never exceed the reward share of the cap's fall and of the cap's fall left unmatched before it.
- The reference and the floor never move on a trade in the slot they were last updated in, and `place_wall` is refused in a slot a swap has run in.
- No instruction other than `pipeline_swap` changes `sqrt_price` or the counters.

### Accepted `pipeline-check` warnings

None.
Exact-out checks are skipped by design and need no reason.
The checks that shape this design are `quote_matches_swap` (exact to the unit), `determinism` (the same quote twice, and for any trader), `round_trip` (a buy sold straight back never returns more), `dust_and_zero` (a zero input is refused) and `transaction_size` (a swap resolves two accounts, the output vault and the vault authority).
The checker sizes its trades from vault balances, which include the wall and the other ledgers; that needs no special handling.

## Where it differs from IMD's Pool4

| | IMD's hook | The buy wall AMM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fee | 1%, on whichever token comes in | Chosen per market, 0.25% to 3%, always in SOL |
| Owner powers | Close the market, withdraw the position, the wall's SOL and the fees, change every parameter | None; a recipient may hand over its own role |
| Reward share | To IMD's stakers, bonding reserve and nodes | To one rewards recipient per market |
| Rates for the wall's guard | Per block | Per second |
| Decay allowance while idle | Unlimited | One day |
| Burns | Bridged to Base | Native |
| Trim and payouts inside a swap | Held as claims, settled later | Booked in ledgers, paid by keeper jobs |

## Building it

- Generate the program from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template with `scripts/new-strategy.sh`, from a scratchpad clone at `5ad130d`, and pin the Pipeline crates to `rev = "5ad130d"`, as for the tax AMM.
- Replace the template's Borsh-decoded pool account with the fixed-size, zero-copy market state above.
- Keep the pricing, the cap and the wall's guard in pure functions that take no accounts, so the proofs and the worked example run against them directly.
- Keep the program keypair in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`, never in the repo.
- Build and test with the toolchain in `docs/toolchain.md` (`source scripts/toolchain-env.sh`).

### Build tickets

Cut by [Cut Pool4 for Solana's build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/24) on 2026-11-10, labelled `build`, one session each, in run order:

1. [Buy wall AMM: a market opens](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/47): the program from the template, the fixed-size market state and its byte offsets, creation, the mint rules and the seed.
2. [Buy wall AMM: plain trading through the router](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/48): curve pricing both ways, the fee and its split, the ledgers and counters, and `pipeline-check` clean.
3. [Buy wall AMM: the inventory cap](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/49): the ratchet, the decay credit and the trim.
4. [Buy wall AMM: the buy wall](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/50): two-step pricing, the guard and `place_wall`.
5. [Buy wall AMM: payouts and recipient handovers](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/51): `settle`, `pay_rewards`, `sweep_fees` and both handovers.
6. [Buy wall AMM: seeding by another program](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/53): `pipeline_seed_liquidity` with a stand-in launchpad; it can run beside tickets 3 to 5.
7. [Buy wall AMM: the release gate and layout fixtures](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/54): the gate, the fixtures and their CI job, and tests that show it refusing a build that would strand a market.
8. [Buy wall AMM: hardening](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/55): the hardening ticket, before the first deploy, so the registered bytes are hardened and the layout freezes once.
9. [Buy wall AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/56): the end of the program's chain, with the whole lifecycle on devnet and one upgrade through the release gate on a live market.
10. [Buy wall AMM: Aviary panel and forms](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/57): after the deploy and Aviary's own build tickets.

The first waits for the tax AMM's first build ticket, which sets up the on-chain workspace, CI, the router fixture and the review skills.
Tickets 1 to 8 are verified end to end through the real router copied from devnet, in LiteSVM; ticket 9 runs every check in "Done means" on devnet itself.

### Done means

- LiteSVM tests through the real router cover:
  - pricing both ways above, across and inside the wall, and quotes matching swaps in each;
  - the fee and its split at the lowest, a typical and the highest rate, with every wall split from none to all;
  - the trim leaving the price unchanged, and `MIN_LIQUIDITY` stopping one;
  - the ratchet with its decay credit, its one-day limit and the cap floor, and the ratchet switched off;
  - the wall's reference ignoring trades in the same slot, and its floor's crawl;
  - pumping the price, placing the wall and dumping never profiting;
  - each keeper job, its refusals and its rounding, with a frozen or missing recipient account never blocking trading or the other payouts;
  - both recipient handovers and every refusal by anyone else;
  - refusal of exact-out, of bypass, of every refused mint extension and of live mint or freeze authorities;
  - a token with a live transfer hook (Pipeline's `test-hook`, its program or its authority still set) refused at the seed by both seeding paths, and one whose hook was cleared through the seed, swaps and `pay_rewards`;
  - donations never credited, and the counters;
  - seeding by another program at the seeder-scoped address.
- The worked example's numbers are reproduced exactly.
- `pipeline-check` passes every check on a seeded market with no warning (with `exact_out_refund` skipped), both in the tests and against devnet.
- The release gate script exists, runs in CI against the fixtures, and has passed against devnet before every upgrade there.
- On devnet:
  - the program deployed and registered with the router's `register_strategy`, with its metadata and conformance report published;
  - one market created with a fresh test token, seeded, and traded both ways through the router;
  - a sell that trims, the wall placed and then sold into, a settle that burns, rewards paid and fees swept, with slot 1 refused while `DESIGNER_RECIPIENT` is unset.
- Its Aviary panel and forms, as `README.md` asks of every product.
- Whatever else `README.md` requires of our on-chain programs.

documents.title: Tax AMM
documents.body:
## What it is

- A Pipeline strategy whose markets always take their tax in one chosen mint, the tax side, whichever way a trade goes.
- Pricing is constant product, and the tax is taken outside the curve, so a trader pays the tax while trading at the curve's price, and the curve's price stays the market's fair price.
- Liquidity is seeded once and locked for good: no LP shares, no adding or removing, no LP fee.
- Tax builds up in the market's own vault and anyone can pay it out to the market's tax recipients, the burn and the suite share.
- It is built to pair with the containment hook (its market state counts the volume and tax the unlock may need), but works for any two mints that pass its mint rules.

## Not in v1

- Exact-out swaps.
- LP shares, adding liquidity after the seed, or withdrawing liquidity.
- Automatic taxes that move with volatility or volume; rates change only when the tax authority changes them.
- Moving the tax authority to another address; it can only renounce.
- Markets with more than two mints.
- Quote mints with extensions outside the allowlist below, such as PYUSD (permanent delegate, transfer fee configuration, confidential transfers).
- Mainnet: nothing deploys there before Pipeline's router does, and the program is frozen first (see "Upgrades and freezing").

## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_TAX_BPS` | 1000 (10%) | The highest buy or sell tax any tax market may ever charge, so no tax market can be a honeypot through its tax |
| `SUITE_SHARE_BPS` | 1000 (10% of the tax) | The suite share, taken from every tax before the creator's split |
| `SUITE_TREASURY` | set at build time | The wallet the suite share is paid to; on devnet a wallet whose key is in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/` |
| `MAX_RECIPIENTS` | 4 | Tax recipients per market |

The constants are compiled into the program; changing one is a program upgrade, which ends when the program is frozen.

## Markets

### Shape

- Exactly two mints, in the order the creator gives them (index 0 and 1), which is the order `pipeline_market_info` reports.
- The mints must differ, and each must be owned by SPL Token or Token-2022 and pass the mint rules below.
- The tax side is one of the two indexes, chosen by the creator and fixed for the market's life.
- Aviary's launch form defaults the tax side to the quote mint (SOL or USDC), so recipients are paid in SOL or USDC rather than in the token they would sell.

### Addresses

- The market state is a fresh keypair the creator generates and signs with (metadata `init.market_state` is `new_keypair`).
  Pipeline's template keys a pool by its parameters instead, but a tax market's parameters (rates, bounds, authority, seeder, four recipients and their shares, the burn share, the virtual reserve) are far more than the 15 seeds a metadata `pda:` source allows, and a key derived from only some of them could be taken first by a market with the same seeds and bad parameters.
  A fresh keypair can't be taken by anyone else; if someone pre-funds it, the creation fails and the creator retries with another keypair, as Pipeline's guide describes.
  Checked against devnet's router in LiteSVM on 2026-11-12 (`programs/tax-amm/tests/hostile.rs`): once the address holds lamports the router passes it on unsigned, the program's account creation fails with a signer privilege escalation, and the whole `create_market` fails, leaving only the lamports; the same creation with a fresh keypair succeeds.
- The vault authority is the PDA `["authority", market_state]` of the tax AMM program; it signs every transfer and burn out of the vaults.
  So `pipeline_resolve_accounts` lists it, read-only, after the output vault: a swap's transfer out of the vault needs it among the swap's accounts ([Tax AMM: seed a market and trade it](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/60), 2026-11-12).
- Each vault is a token account at the PDA `["vault", market_state, mint]`, owned by the vault authority.
  `pipeline_init_market` creates both itself, after every rule below has passed, so a refused mint meets the rule that refuses it rather than a vault creation that can't read it (Anchor's own vault constraints read the mint first and fail on an extension they don't know); each is sized by its mint's token program (`GetAccountDataSize`), which leaves room for a hooked mint's account extension.
  Lamports someone sent to a vault's address beforehand stay in it without blocking the creation; on a native SOL vault the token program turns them into wrapped SOL, a donation the market never counts (see "Locked for good").
  Metadata describes both as `pda:` sources keyed by `market_state` and `input:mint_0` or `input:mint_1`, which the SDK resolves before the market exists.
- So the vaults and the router's market and fee accounts can all be computed from the keypair's address before `create_market` is sent, which the containment hook needs to bind a home market before its first deposit.
- Markets created through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` instead live at the PDA `["seeded", seeder, mint_0, mint_1]`, as Pipeline's guide asks, with vaults and authority derived from that address in the same way.

### Creation parameters

`init_data` is the Borsh encoding of these fields, in this order (metadata `init.args` lists them the same way, because metadata arguments have no arrays or options):

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tax_side` | u8 | 0 or 1 |
| `buy_tax_bps` | u16 | Within its range |
| `sell_tax_bps` | u16 | Within its range |
| `buy_tax_min_bps`, `buy_tax_max_bps` | u16 | min ≤ max ≤ `MAX_TAX_BPS` |
| `sell_tax_min_bps`, `sell_tax_max_bps` | u16 | min ≤ max ≤ `MAX_TAX_BPS` |
| `tax_authority` | pubkey | The default (all-zero) key means none, so the market's taxes and recipients never change |
| `seeder` | pubkey | The only signer the seed action accepts; must not be the default key |
| `recipient_0` to `recipient_3` | pubkey | Owner wallets; used slots first, unused slots the default key |
| `share_0` to `share_3` | u16 | Each used slot's share in basis points of the creator's part, above 0; unused slots 0 |
| `burn_share_bps` | u16 | The burn's share of the creator's part; 0 if the tax side is either native SOL mint (SPL Token's or Token-2022's), since SOL can't be burned |
| `virtual_side` | u8 | 0 or 1 |
| `virtual_reserve` | u64 | 0 for none |

- There is at least one recipient, and the used shares plus `burn_share_bps` sum to exactly 10,000.
- Each rule refuses with an error of its own (`programs/tax-amm/src/errors.rs`), so Aviary's launch form can say which rule a market breaks; a mint refused for an extension is also logged with Token-2022's number for that extension.
- `pipeline_init_market` refuses anything that breaks a rule, checks that the market signer is the router's PDA `["market", program, market_state]` and stores it, creates the vaults, and records the creation slot and Unix time.
- `pipeline_seed_liquidity` takes the same fields in `SeedRequest.data`, with `seeder` ignored because the calling program's PDA is the seeder.

### Mint rules

- A Token-2022 mint may carry only these mint extensions: transfer hook (any hook program), metadata pointer, token metadata, group pointer, group member pointer, token group and token group member.
- Every other mint extension is refused at creation, including transfer fee, permanent delegate (it could take tokens out of the vaults), confidential transfers, pausable, default account state, non-transferable, mint close authority, interest-bearing, scaled UI amount and permissioned burn, as well as any extension the program doesn't recognise.
- Mint and freeze authorities are allowed, since USDC has both; Aviary shows them.
- In Pipeline's trust flags this means a tax market's mints can only ever show `token-2022`, `mint-authority`, `freeze-authority`, `transfer-hook` and `transfer-hook-authority`; a contained token shows the last two until its unlock clears both.
- The trust flags describe strategy programs and mints, not markets, so no flag ever says a market is taxed: the strategy metadata declares it (category `amm`, tag `tax`) and Aviary reads each market's rates, bounds, authority and recipients from its market state.

### Creating a market

One transaction, as Pipeline's guide recommends:

1. The router's `create_market` with the creation parameters, signed by the creator and the market state keypair.
2. The router's `init_fee_account` for each of the two mints.
3. The tax AMM's `seed` action, signed by the seeder.

A launchpad graduating a token instead calls `pipeline_seed_liquidity`, then the router's `register_existing_market` and `init_fee_account` for each mint, in one transaction.

How big that transaction is, against a transaction's 1,232 bytes without an address lookup table, with the creator as the seeder, measured on 2026-11-12 by [Tax AMM: seed a market and trade it](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/60) (`programs/tax-amm/tests/seed.rs`, as a legacy transaction):

- 1,210 bytes for two SPL Token mints or two Token-2022 mints; the demo script's version 0 transaction is 2 bytes longer, 1,212.
- 1,242 bytes for one of each, and 1,308 with a hooked mint (Pipeline's `test-hook`, which adds the fewest accounts a hook can); a seeder other than the creator adds 96 bytes.
- So a market pairing a Token-2022 token with SOL or USDC, and every contained token's home market, needs an address lookup table for its creation transaction, or sends the seed as a second transaction (the market refuses every swap until then); that choice belongs to [Tax AMM in Aviary: the launch form and the tax panel](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/75).

A launchpad's graduation transaction is about as big, measured on 2026-11-12 by [Tax AMM: seeding from another program](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/63) with the stand-in launchpad, paid for by the creator (`programs/tax-amm/tests/seed_liquidity.rs`, as a legacy transaction): 1,212 bytes for two SPL Token mints or two Token-2022 mints, 1,244 for one of each and 1,310 with a hooked mint.
A real launchpad's own accounts change these numbers, and a pair across token programs or with a hook needs an address lookup table there too.

## Liquidity

### The seed

- `seed { amount_0: u64, amount_1: u64 }` is a custom action signed by the market's `seeder`, from token accounts the seeder owns, allowed once and only before any swap.
- Each side's real amount must be above 0, except the virtual side when `virtual_reserve` is above 0, where it may be 0; that is how a token launches single-sided, with only the token deposited.
- The market records each side's real reserve from what actually arrived in its vault, and opens for swaps.
- Until the seed, quotes and swaps are refused (`pipeline-check` reports this as a warning, as it does for any market not yet open).
- `pipeline_seed_liquidity` seeds and opens the market in the same call, taking at most `amounts[i]` from each escrow, and returns `SeedResult { taken, lp_amount: 0 }`.
  - It creates the market with the same code as `pipeline_init_market`, under every creation rule and mint rule, and takes the seed as the `seed` action does, from escrows the seeder owns, with the same rule for a side left empty.
  - `amounts` holds exactly one amount per mint, and `data` exactly the creation parameters; anything else is refused, the first with an error of its own.
  - `taken` is what the program measured leaving each escrow, which a caller can check against its own measurement.
  - A seeder seeds a pair of mints, in that order, once: its market state's address exists afterwards. The `seed` action on a seeded market is refused, even signed by the launchpad's seeder.

### Locked for good

- There is no instruction that takes liquidity out of a market, and no LP shares, so nobody, the creator and us included, can pull liquidity.
- Tokens sent to a vault outside a swap or the seed are donations: they are never credited as input, never paid out, and stay in the vault.

### Virtual reserve

- Pricing treats the virtual side as holding its real reserve plus `virtual_reserve`.
- A swap can never pay out more of a side than its real reserve; a quote or swap that would is refused.
- The virtual reserve is never paid out and never changes.
- `pipeline-check` sizes its trades from vault balances, so checks on a market with a virtual reserve pass explicit `--amounts`.

## Pricing and the tax

Exact-in only: `pipeline_market_info` reports `supports_exact_out = false` (the template's `SUPPORTS_EXACT_OUT` set to `false`), and an exact-out quote or swap is refused.

For a trade from side `i` to side `o`, with real reserves `R_i`, `R_o`, effective reserves `E` (the real reserve plus `virtual_reserve` on the virtual side) and credited input `a`:

- **Buy tax** (the tax side is `i`): `tax = ceil(a × buy_tax_bps / 10,000)`, `c = a - tax`, `out = floor(E_o × c / (E_i + c))`.
  The trader receives `out`; afterwards `R_i += c` and `R_o -= out`.
- **Sell tax** (the tax side is `o`): `g = floor(E_o × a / (E_i + a))`, `tax = ceil(g × sell_tax_bps / 10,000)`, `out = g - tax`.
  The trader receives `out`; afterwards `R_i += a` and `R_o -= g`, and the tax stays in the tax-side vault.
- Intermediate maths is in u128; the tax rounds up and curve output rounds down, so the product of the effective reserves never falls.
- A quote or swap is refused when `out` is 0, or when the curve would pay out more of `o` than `R_o`.
- The pricing refuses a rate above `MAX_TAX_BPS` for every trade, before anything is priced, although creation and the tax authority's changes already keep such a rate out of every market state, so no pricing path can apply one.
- `pipeline_quote` and `pipeline_swap` call the same pricing function, so quotes include the tax and match swaps exactly, which `pipeline-check`'s `quote_matches_swap` verifies.
- Rates are read at the time of the swap: a rate change applies from the next swap, and a trader's minimum output protects against a change between quote and swap.

### Credited input

- Input is credited with Pipeline's `credited_input`: what the input vault holds beyond what the market has recorded there, capped at what the router sent.
- What the market has recorded in a vault is its real reserve, plus all tax owed if it is the tax-side vault.
- The input stays in the input vault for the whole swap, as Pipeline's guide asks; tax taken from input is only booked as owed.

### Bypass

- Refused: `pipeline_swap` accepts only the router's market signer stored at creation (the template's default).
- So every trade pays Pipeline's fee, emits a swap event and counts in the market's counters.
- No custom action moves the price.

## Taxes

### Rates

- A buy tax and a sell tax, each in basis points, each between 0 and `MAX_TAX_BPS`.
- Each side also has a range, `[min, max]`, fixed at creation inside `[0, MAX_TAX_BPS]`; the rate can only ever move inside it.

### Tax authority

- The tax authority, if the market has one, may sign:
  - `set_taxes { buy_tax_bps, sell_tax_bps }`, each inside its fixed range;
  - `set_recipients { recipient_0..3, share_0..3, burn_share_bps }`, under the same rules as at creation;
  - `renounce_tax_authority`, after which the market's taxes and recipients never change again.
- Changes take effect immediately.
- Nobody else can change anything about a market, us included; the program has no admin.
- Built by [Tax AMM: the tax authority](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/62) on 2026-11-12, with these rules besides:
  - `set_taxes` and creation share one rate rule, and `set_recipients` and creation share one split rule (`programs/tax-amm/src/params.rs`), so a change can never pass a rule creation would refuse.
  - Renouncing turns the market state's tax authority into the default key, as on a market created without one, and sets the renounced flag, so Aviary can tell the two apart and both refuse every action for good.
  - A refused action says why: `AlreadyRenounced` on a market whose authority renounced, `NoTaxAuthority` on one created without an authority, and `NotTaxAuthority` for any other signer, checked in that order.
  - `set_recipients` refuses to empty a recipient slot that is still owed tax (`OwedSlotLeftEmpty`), since nobody could then be paid what the slot holds; the slot can be handed to another wallet instead, or paid out first with `distribute`, in the same transaction if need be.
    The burn slot needs no wallet, so the burn share may drop to 0 whatever the burn is owed.
  - `set_recipients` takes the recipients and the shares as arrays of `MAX_RECIPIENTS`, which encode exactly as the metadata's flattened `recipient_0` to `recipient_3` and `share_0` to `share_3`, as the creation parameters do.
  - Each action writes only the market state: no reserve, owed amount, counter, vault balance or value fixed at creation changes (`programs/tax-amm/tests/tax_authority.rs`).

### Where the tax goes

- From every tax, the suite share comes first: `floor(tax × SUITE_SHARE_BPS / 10,000)`, owed to `SUITE_TREASURY`.
- The rest is the creator's part, split by the market's shares: each recipient `floor(rest × share / 10,000)`, the burn `floor(rest × burn_share_bps / 10,000)`, and any rounding remainder to the first recipient.
- The split refuses shares that do not sum to 10,000 with the burn share, for every tax, although creation and `set_recipients` already refuse them, so the parts always add up to the tax.
- Aviary's launch form shows creators the whole split, the suite share included.

### Payout

- Tax is never paid out during a swap: it is booked as owed per slot (recipients 0 to 3, the burn, the suite share) and stays in the tax-side vault.
  - A recipient account that was closed or frozen would otherwise make every swap fail, turning the market into a honeypot.
  - Swaps then need no recipient accounts.
  - Under the containment hook the home market's vault is the only account allowed to pay out a contained token, so tax held anywhere else would be stuck.
- `distribute { slot }` is permissionless: anyone may call it, at any time, for one slot.
  - The slots are numbered as the market state books them: 0 to 3 the tax recipients, 4 the burn and 5 the suite share.
    A slot number above 5 is refused (`NoSuchSlot`), and so is a recipient slot the market does not use, which has no wallet to pay (`UnusedSlot`).
  - A recipient or the suite share is paid its whole owed amount to the associated token account of its wallet for the tax-side mint, which the instruction creates if missing, at the caller's expense.
    For native SOL that account holds wrapped SOL, which the recipient unwraps by closing it (Aviary offers this).
  - The burn slot burns its owed amount from the vault.
  - A slot owed nothing moves nothing, creates no account and emits no event; any other payout emits a distributed event with the slot, its wallet and the amount.
  - Each slot is paid separately, so one broken recipient account never holds up the others: a frozen recipient account fails only its own slot's `distribute`, swaps go on booking tax to the slot, and it pays out once the account is thawed ([Tax AMM: pay the tax out with distribute](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/61), 2026-11-12).
- Its accounts are the caller, who signs and pays for a missing token account, the market state, the vault authority, the tax-side vault and mint, the slot's wallet, that wallet's associated token account for the tax-side mint, the tax-side token program, the associated token program and the system program, then the tax-side mint's transfer-hook accounts.
  - The slot's wallet is its tax recipient, `SUITE_TREASURY` for the suite share, and the default key for the burn, which pays no wallet.
  - Refused: any other wallet (`NotSlotWallet`); any token account but that wallet's associated token account, including one of the other mint (`NotSlotTokenAccount`); the other vault, another vault authority and the other mint passed as the tax-side mint (`WrongAccount`).
  - An SPL Token account at that address whose owner has handed it to another wallet, which SPL Token allows and Token-2022's associated token accounts do not, is paid all the same, as its owner chose: refusing it would strand the slot's tax, for good once the tax authority has renounced.
  - The tax-side mint is read-only for a payout, so payouts never write-lock it (for wrapped SOL that is the native mint every SOL transfer reads), and writable only for the burn, which lowers its supply; a burn with the mint read-only is refused (`BurnNeedsWritableMint`).
    So the metadata describes the instruction as two actions: `distribute` for the tax recipients and the suite share, with the mint read-only, and `burn` for the burn slot, the same instruction (its discriminator named), with the mint writable.
  - Metadata sources can't name a mint by the market's tax side or a wallet held in the market state, so both actions take them as inputs, `tax_mint` and `recipient`, from which they derive the vault and the token account; Aviary's tax panel, the keeper runner and the demo script read them from the market state, and the program refuses any that are not the slot's.
  - `SUITE_TREASURY`, `BURN_SLOT` and `SUITE_SLOT` are published in the IDL beside `MAX_TAX_BPS` and `SUITE_SHARE_BPS`, so the generated client carries the suite share's wallet and the slot numbers, which follow from `MAX_RECIPIENTS`.
- Owed amounts belong to slots: if the tax authority changes a slot's recipient, what the slot is owed goes to the new recipient, so a recipient leaving should be paid out first (anyone can call `distribute`).
  So until a slot is paid out, the tax authority decides which wallet receives what it is owed, its own included; a recipient protects what it is owed by calling `distribute`, and Aviary's tax panel shows each slot's owed amount beside its wallet.
  A recipient slot still owed tax can't be emptied, so every owed amount always has a wallet or the burn to go to (see "Tax authority"); `distribute` therefore pays a recipient slot whatever its share, and burns the burn slot's owed amount whatever the burn share.
- Owed amounts fit in u64, because together with the real reserve they never exceed the vault's balance.
- Pipeline's API reports raw vault balances, so tax not yet paid out shows there as liquidity; Aviary reads the real reserves from the market state instead.

## Counters for the containment hook

The market state keeps these totals, changed only by `pipeline_swap` calls signed by the market signer, never by custom actions:

| Field | Type | Adds, per swap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `volume[0]`, `volume[1]` | u128 | For the input mint, the credited input (what arrived in the vault, the swap event's `net_sent`); for the output mint, what the trader was paid (the swap event's `received`) |
| `tax_collected` | u128 | The swap's tax, in the tax-side mint |
| `swap_count` | u64 | 1 |

With the creation slot and time, the fixed tax ranges and the tax side, that is everything [Containment hook policy](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/18) might measure an unlock goal by (volume, tax paid, age, or a minimum tax), so the hook can choose without changing the tax AMM.
The market state starts with an 8-byte account discriminator and a version byte, and these fields sit at fixed offsets that later versions never move, because the hook reads them directly.
The build fixes the offsets in the ticket that creates markets, publishes them as constants in the tax AMM's crate and pins them with a test, so the two programs cannot drift apart unnoticed.
[Tax AMM: create a tax market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/59) fixed them on 2026-11-12: the market state is 596 bytes, the tax side is the byte at offset 10 and `tax_collected` the little-endian u128 at offset 460, published as `state::layout::TAX_SIDE`, `TAX_COLLECTED` and `LEN` and pinned with every other field's offset by `programs/tax-amm/tests/layout.rs`.
Besides the fields this file names, the market state holds its status (created; the seed adds open), the vault authority's bump, a flag set when the tax authority renounces, so Aviary can tell a renounced market from one created without an authority, and 64 zero bytes at the end, so a later version can add a field without moving any or reallocating existing markets.
Containment hook policy chose `tax_collected`: the unlock reads it, a home market's tax side must be the quote mint, and no minimum tax is needed, because the goal counts tax and not volume (`docs/spec/containment-hook.md`, "Unlock goal").

## Custom actions and metadata

| Action | Metadata `kind` | Signer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | `add_liquidity` | The seeder |
| `distribute` | `claim` | Anyone (payer for a missing token account) |
| `burn` (`distribute` for the burn slot) | `claim` | Anyone |
| `set_taxes` | `other` | The tax authority |
| `set_recipients` | `other` | The tax authority |
| `renounce_tax_authority` | `other` | The tax authority |

- Every action that moves tokens forwards transfer-hook accounts after its own, as the template's swap does.
- Each instruction emits an event (market created, seeded, taxes changed, recipients changed, authority renounced, distributed) so Aviary's indexer can show a market's history; Aviary reads current values from the market state, not from events.
- The metadata follows `pipeline-strategy-metadata/1` as Pipeline 0.2 reads it: name, description, category `amm`, tags including `tax`, links including `source` and the IDL, `init` as above with `market_state: new_keypair`, every action above under `aviary_actions` (`docs/spec/README.md`, "Metadata, IDL and conformance report"), `security.contact`, and `conformance` pointing at a published `pipeline-check` report and its SHA-256.
- `security.contact`, and the contact in the program's `security.txt`, is this repo's private vulnerability reporting page on GitHub, never a personal address.
- Pipeline's metadata standard has no field for `pipeline_seed_liquidity`, so the metadata describes it in a top-level `seed_liquidity` form shaped as `init` is, which the standard's validator allows as an unknown key and the SDK's `resolveInit` resolves: the market state `pda:strategy:str:seeded,key:input:seeder,key:input:mint_0,key:input:mint_1`, `data` as `init`'s arguments under the same `idl_type` with the seeder marked ignored, and the authority and vaults after Pipeline's fixed seed accounts and the three per mint.
  Tests fail when the form disagrees with the program or with `init`.
- The Anchor IDL is committed at `programs/tax-amm/idl/tax_amm.json`, which `links.idl` names, and the TypeScript client in `programs/tax-amm/scripts/client/` is generated from it with Codama; tests fail when the IDL disagrees with the program or the metadata, and `pnpm typecheck` fails when the client disagrees with the IDL.
  Pipeline's interface crate types don't derive Anchor's traits, which the IDL needs, so the program declares the same Borsh types for its instruction arguments (`interface.rs`), tested to encode exactly as Pipeline's.

## In Aviary

`docs/spec/README.md` has each product add its own panel and forms to Aviary; these are the tax AMM's, built with its build tickets once Aviary's own pages exist.
Everything here is read from the market state and the strategy metadata, and nothing gives a tax market a badge or a better place in the feed.

- **Actions from metadata**: `seed`, `distribute`, `set_taxes`, `set_recipients` and `renounce_tax_authority` are rendered by Aviary's generic custom-action forms from the strategy metadata, like any strategy's.
- **Launch form**, the tax AMM's own form on the create-market page:
  - the tax side defaults to the quote mint (SOL or USDC);
  - it shows the whole split before signing: the suite share first, then each tax recipient and the burn;
  - it builds the creation transaction of "Creating a market" (`create_market`, `init_fee_account` for each mint, then `seed`), simulated before the wallet signs like every transaction Aviary builds;
  - it refuses, with the reason, a mint the mint rules would refuse and a mint whose transfer hook is the containment hook (`docs/spec/containment-hook.md`, "Launch in v1").
- **Tax panel**, on a tax market's page:
  - the tax side, the buy tax and the sell tax, each with its fixed range;
  - the tax authority, or that the market has none or that it renounced, in which case the rates and the tax recipients can never change;
  - the tax recipients with their shares, the burn share and the suite share;
  - the tax collected so far, and what each slot is owed and not yet paid out, with a button per slot that sends `distribute`;
  - the real reserves and the virtual reserve from the market state, since raw vault balances include tax not yet paid out.
- The trade box needs nothing of its own: the tax is inside the quote, as `docs/spec/pipescope.md` says of every strategy's own fees, and the panel shows the rates beside it.
- The wallet page's offer to unwrap wrapped SOL covers tax recipients paid in SOL.

## Upgrades and freezing

- On devnet the program stays upgradeable, with its upgrade authority in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`.
- It is frozen (upgrade authority removed) before any mainnet deployment, because the containment hook's unlock will trust its counters and the vaults hold locked liquidity.
- The general upgrade policy is in `docs/spec/README.md`.

## Building it

- Generate the program from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template with `scripts/new-strategy.sh`, from a scratchpad clone at `5ad130d`, and pin the Pipeline crates to `rev = "5ad130d"` in `Cargo.toml`; the template is code Pipeline means builders to copy, unlike the router (owner, 2026-11-10).
- Keep the program keypair the template creates in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`, not `~/.config/pipeline/keys/`, and never in the repo.
- Build and test with the toolchain in `docs/toolchain.md` (`source scripts/toolchain-env.sh`).

### Order of the build

Decided with the owner on 2026-11-10 in [Cut the containment hook and tax AMM build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/23).

- **Local first, devnet last.**
  Until its last feature ticket, the tax AMM is verified by the LiteSVM tests through devnet's real router bytes and by the demo script run against a local validator that runs devnet's router.
  Only the devnet ticket deploys and registers it, so a half-built strategy never appears in Pipeline's registry and no demo market is stranded by a change to the market state.
- **Deploy, then harden.**
  The hardening ticket comes after the devnet ticket, as the bar's last ticket for the program.
  If it changes the program, it redeploys from a verified build, repeats the devnet demo and republishes the metadata and the conformance report.
- **The name.**
  The strategy registers as Aviary Tax AMM (`docs/spec/README.md`, "Names").
  A later change of name is one `update_metadata` call and a rebuild for the `security.txt`; the crate, the program id and the markets keep theirs.
- The demo script grows with each ticket and builds every market creation and custom action from the strategy metadata with the SDK's generic builders, as Aviary will, so the metadata is tested from the first ticket on.

### Where its policy values live

The owner's standing rule of 2026-11-10 keeps every decision cheap to change, since each is a default MetalLegBob may change.

- The four values of "Constants" are build-time constants in one config module of the program, and no other file repeats them.
  `MAX_TAX_BPS`, `SUITE_SHARE_BPS` and `SUITE_TREASURY` are also published in the program's IDL (Anchor's `#[constant]`), so the TypeScript client generated from it carries them for Aviary's launch form and tax panel and the demo script, rather than any of them restating one.
- The mint extension allowlist of "Mint rules", and the check that applies it, live in one small library crate of the on-chain workspace.
  The tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM all depend on that crate, so there is one list and never a second copy; a product with a stricter rule adds it on top.
  The crate is `programs/mint-rules`; it depends on nothing and reads a mint's extension entries itself, the way Token-2022 lays them out, so an extension Token-2022 adds after the crate was written is refused by its number rather than misread.
- Both are fixed on-chain because traders rely on them, so they can change until a program is frozen and not after.
- Every other policy value is a creation parameter, chosen per market and held in its market state: the rates, their ranges, the tax authority, the tax recipients and their shares, the burn share and the virtual reserve.
- The public name, Aviary Tax AMM, lives only in the strategy metadata's `name` and in the `name` of the embedded `security.txt` (`docs/spec/README.md`, "Names").
- The compute ceilings live in the table below and in one test module that mirrors it.
- The demo markets' parameters live in one named block of the demo script.

### Compute ceilings

Tests assert the measured cost of each instruction with headroom, never above these ceilings.
A cost is what the tax AMM's own invocation consumes, its token program calls included, measured on mints without a transfer hook; a hook's cost is the hook's own to bound.
A cost also leaves out what a bump search spends beyond an address's first bump, which depends on the address and not on the program: 1,500 units for each further bump tried.
That matters for `distribute`, which derives the slot wallet's associated token account for the tax-side mint, and when it creates that account the associated token program derives it twice more, so each bump the wallet's address needs after the first adds 4,500 units to a payout that creates the account and 1,500 to one that does not (measured by [Tax AMM: invariant fuzzing across every instruction](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/65), 2026-11-12).
Half of all wallets need a second bump and one in 128 needs eight, which adds 31,500 units to such a payout, so a caller sizing a payout's compute limit, as the keeper runner does, adds 4,500 units for each bump after the first that the wallet's address needs.
The other instructions' bump searches (the vaults, the vault authority and a seeded market's state) sit far enough under their ceilings that no address realistically reaches them, so the tests leave those in.

| Instruction | Ceiling (CU) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pipeline_quote` | 25,000 | Integrators and Canary quote constantly, and the quoter's own cap is 200,000 |
| `pipeline_swap` | 60,000 | With the router's share and a hooked mint's transfers on top, a swap must stay well under the 200,000 at which `pipeline-check`'s `compute` check warns |
| `pipeline_market_info`, `pipeline_resolve_accounts` | 15,000 each | Read-only, and called for every account resolution |
| `pipeline_init_market` | 120,000 | Creates two vaults and reads both mints' extensions |
| `pipeline_seed_liquidity` | 150,000 | Creates the market state and two vaults and takes from two escrows, inside a launchpad's own instruction, which needs compute too |
| `seed` | 80,000 | Two transfers in |
| `distribute` | 90,000 | One transfer or burn, and creating the recipient's token account when it is missing |
| `set_taxes`, `set_recipients`, `renounce_tax_authority` | 20,000 each | They only write the market state |

### Invariants

For the bar's stateful fuzzing layer, beyond its shared three:

1. Each vault holds at least the market's real reserve of its mint, plus everything owed when it is the tax-side vault; donations only ever add to the surplus.
2. A swap never lowers the product of the effective reserves, never pays out more of a side than its real reserve, and never changes the virtual reserve.
3. Every tax is split exactly: the suite share, the tax recipients' parts and the burn add up to the tax, and `tax_collected` always equals what has been paid out or burned plus what is still owed.
4. No rate ever leaves its range or passes `MAX_TAX_BPS`, and nothing fixed at creation ever changes: the mints, the tax side, the ranges, the seeder and the virtual reserve.
5. After the seed, only router swaps change the real reserves, and only router swaps ever change the counters; `distribute` moves at most what its slot is owed.
6. The counters never fall.
7. Once the tax authority has renounced, or on a market created without one, the rates and the tax recipients never change.

How the fuzzer checks them, built by [Tax AMM: invariant fuzzing across every instruction](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/65) on 2026-11-12 (`programs/tax-amm/tests/fuzz.rs`, the harness in `programs/tax-amm/tests/common/fuzz/`):

- Value is conserved: every token the test wrote into accounts is still held by a known account (the wallets, the vaults, Pipeline's fee accounts and a launchpad's escrows), but for what the burn slot was owed each time it was burned, and each mint's supply fell by exactly those burns.
- Every holder can exit: every wallet's whole holding of either mint, Pipeline's fee on top, quotes, or is refused for a reason this file gives, as dust (`ZeroOutput`) or because the curve would pay out more than the output side's real reserve (`InsufficientLiquidity`); the second happens only on a market with a virtual reserve, whose virtual side is priced but never paid out, and then the largest sale the real reserve covers must quote.
  Every sequence ends with every wallet the test holds the keys of selling all it holds, one after another, and each such sale settles unless this file refuses it.
- Invariant 1 is checked exactly: each vault holds its real reserve, everything owed if it is the tax-side vault, and every donation to it, no more and no less.
- Besides the ten, every step must do exactly what this file says: pass or fail with the error it names, and a swap must quote this file's price and leave the market state exactly as its formulas do (`programs/tax-amm/tests/common/model.rs`); and every instruction a step runs must stay under its compute ceiling.

### Maths proofs

The properties the pricing, tax and split maths satisfy for every input, and the tool that establishes each, are listed in [`docs/security/tax-amm/maths-properties.md`](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/blob/main/docs/security/tax-amm/maths-properties.md), chosen with Book of Knowledge as the bar's "Test layers" 2 asks.
Kani proves what it can in `src/pricing.rs`, `src/split.rs` and `src/params.rs`, Z3 proves the division and rounding claims for every input in `proofs/pricing_z3.py`, and Proptest checks every property on at least 10,000 cases in `tests/maths.rs`.

### `pipeline-check` warns

- None is accepted on a seeded market: the tests and the devnet demo require zero Fail and zero Warn, with `exact_out_refund` skipped because exact-out is refused by design.
- A market that is created but not yet seeded refuses every quote, which `pipeline-check` reports as a `quotes` warn; that is the state between two instructions of one creation transaction, never a demo market's.
- A market with a virtual reserve is checked with explicit amounts, as "Virtual reserve" says.

### Canary checks

The bar asks our strategies to pass Canary checks on devnet: no fail on any market, with every warn named here (`docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md`, "Outcomes").

- `cost`, and `exit_queue`, which shares its bands: a warn whenever the buy tax, the sell tax and the Pipeline fee on both legs take the ordinary trade's round-trip return under 95%, which is whenever the two taxes together pass about 4.5%.
  That is the market's stated tax, shown in its panel, and not a hidden cost.
  The tax alone can never make it a fail: with both taxes at `MAX_TAX_BPS` the round trip still returns about 80%.
- `token_authorities`: a warn while a mint of the market keeps an authority that could act on holders, such as a launcher's mint authority or USDC's freeze authority; that is a fact about the mint, which the tax AMM allows and Aviary shows.
- `custom_instructions` notes `seed`, `distribute`, `set_taxes`, `set_recipients` and `renounce_tax_authority`; Canary lists them and does not call them, so a tax authority changing rates inside its range is not exercised.
- On the home market of a contained token, the containment hook's own warns apply as well (`docs/spec/containment-hook.md`, "Canary checks").
- No other check may warn or fail on a tax market we create.

### Build tickets

Cut by [Cut the containment hook and tax AMM build tickets](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/23) on 2026-11-10, labelled `build`, one session each, in run order:

1. [Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/58): the on-chain workspace, the pins, the fixtures, CI, the review skills and the demo script, with the template's own pricing.
2. [Tax AMM: create a tax market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/59): the market state and its pinned offsets, the creation parameters and their rules, the mint rules and the metadata's `init`.
3. [Tax AMM: seed a market and trade it with buy and sell tax](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/60): `seed`, the pricing with both taxes, the virtual reserve, credited input, the tax booked per slot, and the counters.
4. [Tax AMM: pay the tax out with distribute](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/61): `distribute` for tax recipients, the suite share and the burn.
5. [Tax AMM: the tax authority](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/62): `set_taxes`, `set_recipients` and `renounce_tax_authority`.
6. [Tax AMM: seeding from another program](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/63): `pipeline_seed_liquidity`, with a stand-in launchpad.
7. [Tax AMM: proofs of the pricing, tax and split maths](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/64): the property list chosen with Book of Knowledge, proven with Kani, Z3 and Proptest.
8. [Tax AMM: invariant fuzzing across every instruction](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/65): the stateful fuzzer and its ten invariants, and every compute ceiling asserted.
9. [Tax AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and create a demo market](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/66): the first devnet deploy, with everything in "Done means" shown on devnet.
10. [Tax AMM: hardening ticket](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/67): the hardening ticket, after the deploy.
11. [Tax AMM in Aviary: the launch form and the tax panel](https://github.com/imDev2023/testing-pipeline/issues/75): after the deploy and Aviary's own build tickets.

Tickets 4 to 7 can run side by side once ticket 3 has merged.
Tickets 1 to 8 are verified by LiteSVM tests through the real router copied from devnet and by the demo script on a local validator; ticket 9 is the first to touch devnet.
The buy wall AMM and the containment hook start from what ticket 1 sets up.

### Done means

- LiteSVM tests through the real router cover: the tax maths both ways at 0, typical and maximum rates; the cap and the ranges; the tax authority's three actions and every refusal by anyone else; renounced markets; the split and its rounding; `distribute` for each slot, including a frozen recipient account not blocking others and burning; the virtual reserve and its real-reserve limit; refusal of exact-out, of bypass and of every refused mint extension; donations not credited; and the counters.
- `pipeline-check` passes every check on a seeded market (with `exact_out_refund` skipped), both in the tests and against devnet.
- The invariants above under the bar's fuzzing layer, the compute ceilings under its limits layer, and proofs of the pricing, tax and split maths under its maths layer.
- On devnet: the program deployed and registered with the router's `register_strategy`, its metadata and conformance report published, and one market created, seeded, traded both ways through the router, and paid out with `distribute`.
- Whatever else `docs/spec/README.md` requires of our on-chain programs.

## Not measured yet

- The compute cost of each instruction not built yet.
